A novel perioperative pathway for hip fractures in the older adult: a pre-post quality improvement study using statistical process control
items.abstract: Despite advances in medical care, the incidence of medical complications, especially delirium, remains high in patients with hip fracture. Although individual components of hip fracture pathways have been studied, the components together have not. At a tertiary academic medical center, an internal review identified a high rate of unnecessary preoperative cardiac testing and postoperative delirium among patients with hip fracture admitted to the hospital medicine service. We designed a multidisciplinary perioperative pathway aimed at reducing delirium, time to surgery, and length of stay by addressing common medical conditions in older adult patients with hip fractures. A novel pathway incorporating regional anesthesia, multimodal analgesia, preoperative anemia correction, and guideline-based cardiac evaluation was implemented at a tertiary care academic center. Led by hospitalists, this pathway was introduced in two sequential phases: Period 1 – educational initiative on evidence-based cardiac testing, regional anesthesia, and opioid-sparing analgesia, beginning July 1, 2018; Period 2 – expanded interventions targeting blood utilization, nerve blocks, carbohydrate loading, and physical therapy staffing, beginning July 1, 2023. Cardiology co-management guidelines aligned with American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association (ACC/AHA) recommendations; an order set for multimodal, opioid-sparing analgesia including a femoral nerve block within 2 h of admission; clear carbohydrate drinks; expedited operative repair targets; and preoperative anemia management with intravenous iron and epoetin alfa. Outcomes for patients admitted July 2021–December 2022 (Period 1, n = 183) were compared with those admitted January 2023–July 2024 (Period 2, n = 189). Statistical process control (SPC) charts were used to assess special-cause variation in nerve block use, carbohydrate drink consumption, delirium, and acute kidney injury (AKI). Implementation led to significant reductions in cardiology consultation time, length of stay, intra- and postoperative blood transfusions, and time to surgery. There was increased use of nerve blocks and preoperative carbohydrate drinks, with no change in delirium rates or 30-day readmissions. Statistical process control methods were used to detect special cause variation after implementation of selected interventions. Mortality remained low at 0.5%. Hospitalist-led multidisciplinary care pathways can reduce hospital stay, expedite perioperative care, and improve implementation of evidence-based practices in geriatric hip fracture management. 12/2021 (Control ##21E.1180).

items.title: Early implementation of exercise to facilitate recovery after elective colorectal surgery—a randomized clinical pilot trial
items.abstract: Background Early mobilization is a key component of enhanced recovery after elective colorectal surgery. This pilot trial evaluated the safety and feasibility of an early supervised postoperative exercise intervention in addition to standard care. Methods In this single-center randomized controlled pilot trial, 31 patients undergoing elective colorectal surgery were randomized to an intervention group ( n = 16) or control group ( n = 15). One patient withdrew after randomization, leaving 30 patients for modified intention-to-treat analysis. The intervention consisted of individualized, physiotherapist-supervised exercise sessions on postoperative days 1, 3, and 5. The control group received standard postoperative care according to the institutional ERAS protocol. The originally registered primary endpoint was time to first bowel movement; prior to final analysis, safety and feasibility were designated as the primary outcomes in accordance with the pilot nature of the study. The change was documented transparently. Secondary outcomes included physical performance (Short Physical Performance Battery [SPPB], handgrip strength), time to first bowel movement, patient-reported outcomes, and postoperative complications. Results Thirty patients completed the study (retention 96.8%). Adherence to the intervention was 100%, and no intervention-related adverse events occurred. The intervention group showed significantly better preservation of physical performance, reflected by a more favorable change in SPPB score from baseline to postoperative assessment. No significant between-group differences were observed for time to first bowel movement, handgrip strength, postoperative complications, or other secondary outcomes. Conclusions Early supervised postoperative exercise after elective colorectal surgery was safe and feasible. Although no differences were found for most secondary outcomes, the intervention improved postoperative physical performance. These exploratory findings warrant confirmation in adequately powered randomized trials. Trial registration German Clinical Trials Register, DRKS00036327 (retrospectively registered, 22.04.2025).

items.title: Perioperative complications at scale: a multi-center analysis of 1.2 million surgical inpatients and the ethical imperative for risk transparency
items.abstract: Abstract Background Major inpatient surgery is associated with significant postoperative morbidity, yet large-scale contemporary data characterizing complication patterns remain limited. Understanding complication epidemiology is essential for individualized risk assessment and shared decision-making. This study aimed to validate prior findings of perioperative complication rates and characterize complication patterns by type, timing, surgical service, patient demographics, and the COVID-19 pandemic period. Methods We developed a tool in early 2019 to prospectively collect perioperative outcomes for patients undergoing major inpatient surgery across 35 different medical centers. We analyzed data from 1,214,539 surgical inpatients receiving care between October 2017 and December 2023. Complications were time stamped and identified using ICD-10 codes, and categorized as pulmonary, cardiac, renal, neurologic, hemorrhagic, or septic. Complication proportions were stratified by surgical service line, postoperative day, age, sex, and American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status. Results The overall complication rate was 7.6% (range 0.52%-23.72% by service line). Cardiac surgery (23.72%), ECMO (20.31%), and neurosurgery (19.89%) had the highest complication rates. The most frequent complications within 7 days per 1000 patients were: postoperative pulmonary complications (6.41), acute kidney injury (5.36), postsurgical sepsis (4.64), acute coronary syndrome (1.00), stroke (0.69), and cardiac arrest (0.63). Complications increased with age (0.67% ages 0–10 years to 15.65% ages 91–100) and were higher in males (9.20%) than females (6.46%). Post-pandemic complication rates (7.68%) declined below pre-pandemic levels (8.32%) and were highest during the emergency surgery only phase of the pandemic (10.53%). Complication rates ranged from a facility-level low of 0.96% to a high of 15.98%, while at the procedure level (CPT codes), certain low-volume interventions had 100% complication rates. Conclusions Complications following major inpatient surgery occur in up to 1 in 4 patients in high-risk surgical populations, and vary significantly by institution and procedure. Surgical facilities should utilize similar methodologies to define their own outcomes to drive perioperative quality improvement. Furthermore, patients have a fundamental right to know these data before consenting to surgery. Institutional complication rates should be made publicly available to facilitate shared decision-making and informed consent.

items.title: Sex differences in perioperative heart rate variability and recovery in gastric cancer patients undergoing robot-assisted gastrectomy: a retrospective cohort study using wearable monitoring
items.abstract: Purpose This study aims to analyze sex differences in perioperative autonomic dysfunction in gastric cancer (GC) patients using a wearable HRV monitoring device. Additionally, we explore the relationship between HRV, sex, and postoperative recovery. Methods A total of 160 GC patients were enrolled and divided into two sex-based groups, with 80 patients in each group. Perioperative HRV, inflammatory markers, and nutritional indices were monitored. Time to first flatus, postoperative length of stay (PLOS), and complications were compared between groups. Furthermore, the correlation between HRV indices and PLOS was analyzed. Results Perioperative HRV trajectories differed significantly between sexes (all sex × time interactions P < 0.001), with variable magnitude, direction and timing of across‑index sex‑related differences. Overall, females showed smaller postoperative declines and faster restoration toward preoperative HRV values. Female patients also showed lower postoperative inflammatory markers, higher cortisol (Cor) levels, shorter first flatus time. Both POD1 pNN50 and POD1 rMSSD were identified as independent predictors of prolonged PLOS. The Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve analysis revealed an apparent AUC of 0.864, and after bootstrap internal validation, the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.822, indicating good discriminative performance with expected shrinkage upon validation. Conclusion Female sex was associated with more favorable autonomic recovery (as reflected by faster HRV restoration) and lower postoperative systemic inflammatory markers, although postoperative cortisol levels were higher in females. These patterns may contribute to faster gastrointestinal recovery. POD1 pNN50 and POD1 rMSSD were identified as independent predictors of prolonged PLOS. HRV indices show promise as non-invasive biomarkers for monitoring perioperative recovery, though these exploratory findings require rigorous external validation in larger, multicenter prospective studies before any clinical application can be considered.

items.title: The impact of long-term aspirin use on patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty
items.abstract: Due to the aging population and the high incidence of osteoarticular diseases, the demand for the future development of total hip arthroplasty (THA). Aspirin use has increased substantially owing to its multiple benefits. The aim of our study was to explore the influence of Long-Aspirin Use (L-AU) on perioperative complications in patients undergoing THA. By querying the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) database, the data of patients undergoing THA from 2019 to 2022 were acquired after removing irrelevant data. Propensity score matching (PSM) was designed to reduce the impact of demographic and comorbidity characteristics on perioperative complications. T Test , Chi-Square Test, Rank Sum Test, as well as logistic regression analysis, were used for perioperative complications risk analysis and resource consumption analysis. The proportion of ICD-coded long-term aspirin use (L-AU) among patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty in the unweighted NIS analytic sample increased from 12.13% to 18.21% between 2019 and 2022. After multivariable adjustment, L‑AU was significantly associated with elevated risks of any complication, acute myocardial infarction, and acute cerebrovascular disease. Meanwhile, L‑AU was significantly associated with reduced odds of septicemia and respiratory failure, as well as lower odds of prolonged length of stay and lower total hospital costs. No statistically significant associations were observed between L‑AU and most other perioperative complications. In this retrospective analysis, long-term aspirin use was associated with selected in-hospital outcomes among patients undergoing THA, including lower odds of septicemia and respiratory failure and higher odds of acute myocardial infarction and acute cerebrovascular disease. These associations do not establish causality, and the effects of perioperative aspirin continuation, discontinuation, or resumption could not be assessed. Prospective studies with detailed medication and clinical data are needed to clarify the perioperative risks and benefits of aspirin management in this population. This shows that a total of 369,846 patients undergoing primary THA between 2019 and 2022, through exclusion of inappropriate samples among them, obtained the remaining 310,925 patients who were classified into the long-term aspirin use (L-AU) cohort (n=49,613) and matched non-L-AU cohort (n=49,613) after propensity score matching analysis.

items.title: Risky lifestyle factors among patients scheduled for ventral hernia repair: a cross-sectional study of smoking, nutrition, alcohol, and physical inactivity (SNAP)
items.abstract: Background Risky lifestyle factors, including Smoking, Nutrition (malnutrition and obesity), risky Alcohol intake, and Physical inactivity (SNAP factors), are well-established predictors of postoperative complications. While advances such as Enhanced Recovery After Surgery have improved perioperative care, evidence on preoperative risk factor optimisation remains limited, particularly in hernia surgery. The aim was to map the prevalence of SNAP factors in patients undergoing ventral hernia repair and to estimate the potential impact of targeted preoperative intervention. Methods This cross-sectional study included patients aged ≥ 18 years scheduled for primary or incisional ventral hernia repair at two Danish university hospitals (March 2024–May 2025). Data on SNAP factors were obtained through structured interviews (by telephone or at the outpatient clinic) and review of health records. The prevalence of risky lifestyle factors was analysed with 95% confidence intervals, and hypothetical scenarios were modelled to estimate the potential impact of targeted prehabilitation. Results A total of 304 participants were included. Overall, 50% [95% CI 44–56%] had at least one SNAP factor with obesity (32% [27–37%]), smoking (14% [11–19%]), and risky alcohol intake (9% [6–13%]) being the most common. A subset of patients (12% [9–16%]) exhibited two or more coexisting SNAP factors. Age ≥ 65 years was associated with a significantly higher prevalence of SNAP factors in univariate (OR 1.66 [1.02–2.73]) and multivariable (OR 1.65 [1.01–2.72]) analyses. Conclusion Patients scheduled for ventral hernia repair frequently present with risky SNAP factors, particularly obesity and smoking. These findings highlight a major potential for risk factor reduction through targeted, multimodal prehabilitation in this population. Trial registration NCT06611462.

items.title: Anesthetic Management of Glucose-6-Phosphate Dehydrogenase Deficiency in Cardiac Surgery: A Narrative Review
items.containerTitle: Journal of Cardiothoracic and Vascular Anesthesia
items.abstract: Global prevalence of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency approaches 450 million individuals. G6PD deficiency impairs management of oxidative stress and has been associated with premature development of coronary atherosclerosis. Anesthesia, cardiac surgery, and cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) may exacerbate oxidative stress. This review article summarizes literature pertaining to perioperative management of individuals with G6PD deficiency undergoing cardiac surgery. Perioperative care for individuals with G6PD deficiency centers on avoidance of oxidative stress and triggering medications. Although many anesthetic medications have been safely used in G6PD deficient populations, there is emerging evidence that suggests propofol, dexmedetomidine, and remifentanil have pleiomorphic antioxidant properties. Cardiac surgery and CPB potentially instigate erythrocyte trauma and promote oxidative stress. Centrifugal pumps avoid mechanical deformation of red cells and generate a significantly lower inflammatory response than roller pumps. While selection of large vascular cannulae promotes laminar flow and imparts less sheer stress on erythrocytes, minimized CPB circuitry reduces the non-biologic contact interface with erythrocytes and is associated with less inflammation than conventional CPB circuitry. Moreover, maintenance of normothermia during CPB may help prevent hemolysis in individuals with G6PD deficiency by preserving red cell deformity. Importantly, transient acidemia during CPB may potentially trigger hemolysis in G6PD deficient individuals and the balance between perfusion supply and demand warrants consideration. Strategies to mitigate intraoperative hemolysis in G6PD-deficient individuals are needed to support safe perioperative care. Intraoperative care demands vigilance for signs of hemolysis to support prompt diagnosis and management.

items.title: Vasopressors to treat or prevent hypotension during and after major surgery: a scoping review
items.containerTitle: Journal of Cardiothoracic and Vascular Anesthesia
items.abstract: Perioperative hypotension is common and associated with adverse postoperative outcomes. Vasopressors are central to management, yet the optimal agent and their subsequent impacts on end organ outcomes remain unclear. We undertook a scoping review to characterise the current evidence base and address the need for a full systematic review or meta-analysis. A protocol was formulated a priori as per PRISMA-ScR. Subsequently, MEDLINE, Embase and Scopus were searched from 1 January 2000 to 18 July 2025 for studies comparing parenteral vasopressors in adults undergoing major surgery. Randomised control trials and observational studies were included. Data on study design, vasopressor strategies, initiation criteria, and postoperative outcomes were extracted and synthesised descriptively. Sixteen studies (n = 6,927) were included. Most were small, single-centre and observational, predominantly in cardiothoracic surgery. Vasopressor initiation criteria were highly variable with studies divided broadly between hypotension-based triggers and vasoplegic syndrome, the latter inconsistently defined. A variety of vasopressors were evaluated yet no two studies compared identical regimens. Postoperative outcome reporting was heterogenous, and outcome definitions varied and showed minimal alignment with StEP-COMPAC consensus standards. Eight studies reported significant differences in postoperative clinical outcomes between vasopressor strategies; however, effects were inconsistent, and no vasopressor strategy demonstrated a consistent benefit across studies. Overall, the evidence base for vasopressor therapy in perioperative hypotension is fragmented. Variability in initiation criteria, interventions and outcome definitions limits comparability and precludes meaningful synthesis. Standardised definitions and adequately powered multicentre trials are required to determine optimal vasopressor strategies and their effects on postoperative organ dysfunction.

items.title: Use of von Willebrand Factor in VA-ECMO-associated acquired von Willebrand Syndrome: a nationwide retrospective study
items.containerTitle: Journal of Cardiothoracic and Vascular Anesthesia
items.abstract: Objectives VA-ECMO is a life-saving therapy for refractory cardiocirculatory failure but carries a high bleeding risk, partly due to acquired von Willebrand syndrome (aVWS). With limited evidence-based treatments, von Willebrand Factor (VWF) is often used off-label. This study examines nationwide use of VWF in VA-ECMO patients with aVWS in Germany and compares bleeding, thromboembolic events, and survival between treated and untreated patients. Design Retrospective cohort study based on reimbursement data (2019–2023). Setting Multi-institutional analysis of adult VA-ECMO cases treated in German hospitals. Participants 530 adult patients supported with VA-ECMO and diagnosed with aVWS. Interventions Administration of any dose of VWF during VA-ECMO support versus no VWF treatment. Measurements and Main Results Of 530 patients, 389 (73%) received VWF across 35 of 71 centres contributing patients. Intracranial haemorrhage (ICH) occurred less frequently in the VWF group (8% vs 15%, p=0.0238). However, haemothorax (37% vs 20%, p=0.0028) was more common with VWF. Thromboembolic events did not differ between groups. ICU LOS was shorter in VWF-treated patients (14 vs 18 days, p=0.0168). 90-day survival was numerically higher in the VWF group but did not reach statistical significance (p=0.188). Conclusions In this cohort of VA-ECMO patients with aVWS, VWF was frequently used and associated with lower ICH rates and shorter ICU LOS, there was no evidence of increased thromboembolic events, but higher rates of other bleeding complications. Prospective randomized trials are warranted to clarify the impact of VWF on clinical outcomes.

items.title: Effects of the sodium glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitor empagliflozin on perioperative endothelial function in patients undergoing cardiac surgery: an exploratory analysis of MERCURI-1
items.containerTitle: Journal of Cardiothoracic and Vascular Anesthesia
items.abstract: Objective To investigate whether short-term treatment with Empagliflozin (EMPA) is associated with attenuation of endothelial dysfunction and cardiac injury in patients undergoing cardiac surgery. Design An exploratory study using samples from the open-label randomized MERCURI-1 study. Setting Academic university hospital. Participants Adult patients undergoing cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass. Interventions Patients received 10 mg/day EMPA starting three days before surgery and continuing until two days postoperatively or received standard perioperative care. Measurements and Main Results Blood samples were collected at baseline (prior to EMPA therapy), on the day of surgery (before the first incision), and one day after surgery (Post-D1). Plasma biomarkers for endothelial activation (endothelin-1), vascular leakage (angiopoietin-2), glycocalyx degradation (syndecan-1), cardiac injury (Troponin I and NT-proBNP), and systemic inflammation (IL-6, IL-8 and CRP) were measured. In vitro , human cardiac microvascular endothelial cells were exposed to patient plasma, and endothelial permeability was assessed. Surgery-induced changes in biomarkers of endothelial activation and vascular leakage did not differ significantly between the EMPA and control groups. The adjusted between-group differences were 0.097 pg/mL for endothelin-1 (95% CI -0.478 to 0.672, p = 0.735), -465 pg/ml for angiopoietin-2 (95% CI -2355 to 1426, p = 0.623), and 19540 pg/ml for syndecan-1 (95% CI -10016 to 49095, p = 0.19). No significant differences were found for cardiac injury and inflammatory biomarkers. In vitro , no difference in endothelial resistance was found between the EMPA and control groups. Conclusions In this exploratory sub-study, we found no significant differences in endothelial activation, vascular leakage, cardiac injury or inflammation between the EMPA and control groups. Given the limited sample size, smaller treatment effects cannot be excluded.

items.title: Outflow Graft Kinking as a Precipitant of Right-Sided HeartMate 3 Thrombosis and Pulmonary Embolization in Biventricular Support
items.containerTitle: Journal of Cardiothoracic and Vascular Anesthesia
items.abstract: We previously reported the case of a young woman with lymphocytic myocarditis and end-stage biventricular heart failure who received biventricular HeartMate 3 (HM3) assist devices (Abbott Laboratories, Abbott Park, IL) as destination therapy.1. items.title: Interventions during cardiopulmonary bypass to increase tissue oxygenation as measured by mitochondrial oxygen tension
items.containerTitle: Journal of Cardiothoracic and Vascular Anesthesia
items.abstract: Objectives A low cutaneous mitochondrial oxygen tension (mitoPO 2 ) during cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) is an early indicator of insufficient tissue oxygen delivery and predicts cardiac surgery associated kidney injury (CSA-AKI). MitoPO 2 monitoring may therefore be an early trigger to improve tissue oxygenation during CPB and potentially prevent related complications such as CSA-AKI. However, currently it is unknown how mitoPO 2 can be improved during CPB. The objective of this study was to evaluate whether a range of interventions could increase low mitoPO 2 during CPB. Design An interventional before-after pilot study Setting Operating room of a tertiary academic university hospital Participants 9 adult patients undergoing elective cardiac surgery on cardiopulmonary bypass were included. Interventions The following interventions were applied during CPB, in a fixed order, each followed by a 10 min equilibrium period: increase in CPB pump flow, suppletion of albumin, a mean arterial and pressure (MAP) of 80mmHg. A linear mixed model was performed to correct for pre-intervention trends and slopes. Measurements and Main Results In this pilot study, oxygen delivery variables and mitoPO 2 were continuously recorded during CPB at 30 seconds intervals. At baseline while on CPB, conventional markers of tissue perfusion and oxygen delivery were within normal range. Increasing CPB pump flow index to achieve a flow index to 3L/min/m 2 resulted in an increased mitoPO 2 from 31 (20 – 35) mmHg to 40 (25 - 44) mmHg (p=0.016). Venous oxygen saturation concurrently increased from 77 (76 – 78)% to 81(79 – 83)% (p=0.016), indicating supraphysiological blood flow. Increasing MAP and administration of albumin did not result in a significant change in mitoPO₂. Conclusions Augmenting the CPB pump flow index significantly increased mitoPO₂. This shows that mitoPO₂ responds to changes in perfusion, supporting its potential as a physiological target to guide perfusion during cardiopulmonary bypass.

items.title: Four-Factor Prothrombin Complex Concentrate Dosing for Perioperative Bleeding in Cardiac Surgery Utilizing Cardiopulmonary Bypass
items.containerTitle: Journal of Cardiothoracic and Vascular Anesthesia
items.abstract: Objective To compare the efficacy and cost of 1000 IU versus 1500 IU four-factor prothrombin complex concentrate (4F-PCC) in adults undergoing cardiac surgery requiring cardiopulmonary bypass. Design Single-center, retrospective pre-post study. Participants Adult patients who received intraoperative 4F-PCC during cardiac surgery requiring cardiopulmonary bypass between April 2024 and October 2025. Patients receiving 4F-PCC for heart transplantation, durable ventricular assist device procedures, noncardiac surgery, or anticoagulation reversal were excluded. Interventions Patients were grouped by initial dose: 1500 IU or 1000 IU. The primary outcome was successful hemostatic response, defined as no chest re-exploration, repeat 4F-PCC, or non-red blood cell allogeneic transfusion 1 to 24 hours after 4F-PCC. Noninferiority was assessed using an adjusted absolute risk difference with a prespecified 10% margin. Secondary outcomes included total hemostatic therapy cost and chest tube output. Measurements and Main Results Of 936 screened patients, 341 met criteria: 154 in the 1000 IU group and 187 in the 1500 IU group. Successful hemostatic response occurred in 74.68% and 74.87%, respectively (P=0.97). The adjusted absolute risk difference was -0.24% (95% CI, -8.98% to 8.49%), consistent with noninferiority. The adjusted mean difference in total hemostatic therapy cost was -$885 per patient (95% CI, -$1262 to -$509), favoring 1000 IU. Chest tube output did not differ at 6 hours (343.49 vs 362.97 mL, P=0.87) or 24 hours (784.99 vs 814.62 mL, P=0.60). Conclusions In this real-world cohort of patients undergoing CPB, a reduced fixed dose of 1000 IU 4F-PCC resulted in similar hemostatic outcomes to the standard 1500 IU dose, with reductions in hemostatic agent cost. These findings support further randomized studies evaluating 4F-PCC dosing.

items.containerTitle: Journal of Cardiothoracic and Vascular Anesthesia
items.abstract: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy (TTC) is a reversible, stress-induced cardiomyopathy characterized by transient left ventricular systolic dysfunction, most commonly presenting with apical ballooning in the absence of obstructive coronary artery disease.1 Dynamic left ventricular outflow tract obstruction (LVOTO) complicates up to 20-25% of cases and is associated with increased morbidity and mortality. Older age, septal bulging, mitral regurgitation, and hemodynamic instability are risk factors for LVOTO.

items.title: Real-time hemodynamic profiling during mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair using pulse contour analysis
items.containerTitle: Journal of Cardiothoracic and Vascular Anesthesia
items.abstract: Objectives To characterize perioperative hemodynamic response patterns during transcatheter edge-to-edge mitral valve repair (M-TEER) using pulse contour analysis (PCA), and to identify determinants of heterogeneous cardiac output responses following mitral regurgitation (MR) reduction. Design Prospective, single-center observational study. Setting Single tertiary academic medical center. Participants Sixteen consecutive patients undergoing M-TEER with the PASCAL Ace system (Edwards Lifesciences). Interventions Continuous PCA monitoring was performed from baseline until 4 h postprocedural alongside periprocedural echocardiography. The primary endpoint was the change in PCA-derived cardiac output (PCA-CO). Secondary endpoints assessed associations between hemodynamic response, procedural success, and ventricular function. Measurements and Main Results Hemodynamic responses varied according to MR reduction and ventricular function. Sustained PCA-CO improvement occurred only with successful MR reduction (≤2+; 24% ± 11%; p = 0.049). Patients with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction showed an early, transient increase in PCA-CO, reaching 108% of baseline (IQR, 86–136%) after first-device implantation (Dunn-adjusted p = 0.035), which was no longer evident at 4 h (p = 0.80). In contrast, patients with preserved ejection fraction showed a delayed, sustained increase at 4 h (14% ± 13%; p = 0.035). Patients with a left ventricular end-diastolic diameter <60 mm also showed increased PCA-CO at 4 h (12% ± 18%; p = 0.049). Changes in PCA-CO correlated inversely with systolic pulmonary artery pressure (ρ = −0.60; p = 0.026), while left atrial v-wave amplitude decreased significantly (p < 0.001). Conclusions Early hemodynamic changes after M-TEER is not universal but depends on effective MR reduction and ventricular functional reserve. Continuous PCA identified distinct response patterns despite technically successful valve repair.

items.title: Beating Heart Transplantation May Facilitate Liberal Use of Extended Criteria Donors
items.containerTitle: The Journal of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery
items.abstract: Objective Extended criteria donor (ECD) hearts are particularly vulnerable to ischemia-reperfusion injury and thus more prone to primary graft dysfunction. We test the hypothesis that by minimizing ischemia-reperfusion and cooling-rewarming injury, ex-vivo machine perfusion and beating heart transplant (BHT) can allow liberal and safer use of ECD hearts. Methods Between 2023 and 2025, 130 BHTs (109, isolated, 21 combined with kidney and/or liver) were performed in our center. These were retrospectively compared to 138 historical and concurrent transplants performed using controlled cold storage (CCS) between 2020 and 2025. ECD was defined based on the EXPAND trial criteria. Results Among the BHT group, 64% (83/130) utilized ECD hearts, compared to 37% (51/138) in the CCS group (P Conclusion Beating heart implantation using continuous normothermic perfusion may allow expanded use of ECD hearts, including from older and distant donors, without compromising early outcomes.

items.title: Superior Prognosis of Neoadjuvant Immunochemotherapy over Neoadjuvant Chemoradiotherapy in Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma Patients with pCR
items.containerTitle: The Journal of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery
items.abstract: Background Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (NCRT) is the standard regimen for locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), while neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy (NICT) has emerged as a promising alternative. Achieving pathological complete response (pCR) after neoadjuvant therapy is associated with favorable prognosis, yet whether the modality used to achieve pCR influences long-term outcomes remains unclear. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 332 ESCC patients who attained pCR following neoadjuvant therapy (220 in the NCRT group and 112 in the NICT group). Prognostic outcomes, including short-term clinical outcomes, long-term survival, and recurrence patterns, were compared between the two groups. Results Among all pCR patients, the NCRT group exhibited a significantly higher incidence of postoperative pneumonia compared with the NICT group (28.6% vs. 14.3%, P = 0.004). Regarding recurrence patterns, the NCRT group showed higher rates of both local and distant recurrence. After multivariable adjustment, NICT conferred superior overall survival (OS) (HR = 0.248, 95% CI: 0.076-0.809, P = 0.021) and disease-free survival (DFS) (HR = 0.215, 95% CI: 0.077-0.599, P = 0.003) relative to NCRT. Conclusions Among ESCC patients achieving pCR after neoadjuvant therapy, NICT was associated with significantly better OS and DFS, as well as a lower incidence of postoperative pneumonia, compared with NCRT. Given its survival benefit and favorable safety profile, NICT may be a preferred neoadjuvant strategy for selected patients, pending prospective corroboration.

items.title: Long-Term Outcomes After Heart-Lung Transplantation: A Contemporary 20-Year Single-Center Experience
items.containerTitle: The Journal of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery
items.abstract: Objective (s): We aimed to evaluate long-term outcomes after heart-lung transplantation (HLTx) including comparisons between adult congenital (CHD) and non-congenital (non-CHD) recipients and outcomes before and after implementation of the 2018 United Network for Organ Sharing heart allocation system change. Methods Consecutive patients undergoing HLTx between February 2006 and February 2026 were retrospectively reviewed. The primary endpoint was overall survival. Secondary endpoints included chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD)-free survival and perioperative outcomes. Kaplan-Meier analysis was used for time-to-event outcomes. Results Sixty-two patients underwent HLTx, including 20 (32.3%) with CHD and 42 (67.7%) with non-CHD etiologies. Despite greater operative complexity, perioperative outcomes were comparable between groups, with an overall 30-day mortality of 11.3%. Median overall survival was 7.8 years with estimated 1-, 5-, and 10-year survival of 80.1%, 58.8%, and 37.9%, respectively. Median CLAD-free survival was 5.9 years with estimated 1-, 5-, and 10-year rates of 76.6%, 53.5%, and 24.0%, respectively. Overall and CLAD-free survival were similar between CHD and non-CHD recipients (p=0.151 and p=0.354, respectively). Most late deaths were lung-related (20/27, 74%), whereas cardiac causes were uncommon (1/27, 3.7%), and CAV developed in two patients (3.2%). Recipients transplanted after the allocation change demonstrated improved survival (p=0.022), mainly due to a decline in perioperative mortality from 17.5% to 0% (p=0.044). Conclusions Long-term outcomes after HLTx remain primarily limited by CLAD and lung-related complications. Adults with CHD achieved survival comparable to non-CHD recipients. Improved contemporary outcomes appear to be driven predominantly by reduced perioperative mortality.

items.title: Functional outcome after recurrent laryngeal nerve injury following thoracic aortic surgery
items.containerTitle: The Journal of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery
items.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Recurrent laryngeal nerve injury is a recognized complication of aortic surgery, yet data on long-term functional outcomes remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate the incidence of recurrent laryngeal nerve injury and to assess voice recovery after thoracic aortic surgery. METHODS: Single-centre retrospective analysis included adult patients undergoing aortic arch or thoracoabdominal aortic surgery between 2001 and 2024. Recurrent laryngeal nerve injury was diagnosed by postoperative vocal cord paralysis. Aortic arch surgery included partial and total arch replacement, while thoracoabdominal surgery involved the proximal descending aorta. The primary endpoint was full voice recovery. Secondary endpoints included recovery of normal vocal cord mobility, residual dysphonia, the need for voice therapy, and vocal cord interventions. RESULTS: Among 2,983 patients undergoing aortic surgery, 70 (2.3%) were diagnosed with postoperative recurrent laryngeal nerve injury. Median follow-up was 17 [IQR: 7-25] months. The incidence of recurrent laryngeal nerve injury was 1.7% after arch surgery and 5.3% after thoracoabdominal procedures. At final follow-up, 34 patients (50%) achieved full voice recovery, while 20 (30%) had mild dysphonia, 9 (13%) moderate dysphonia, and 5 (7%) severe dysphonia. Voice therapy was performed in 49 (70%) patients, and 10 (14%) required additional vocal cord interventions. CONCLUSIONS: In this large cohort, the incidence of recurrent laryngeal nerve injury after aortic surgery was lower than previously reported. Functional outcomes were favourable, with most patients achieving full or near-complete voice recovery through conservative or interventional management. Structured follow-up and multidisciplinary care remain essential to optimize outcomes after recurrent laryngeal nerve injury.

items.title: Mid-Term Outcomes for Lung Transplantation in for COVID-19 Respiratory Failure: An Analysis of the United Network for Organ Sharing Database
items.containerTitle: The Journal of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery
items.abstract: Background Lung transplantation is a feasible therapeutic option for irreversible lung injury caused by COVID-19, but comprehensive mid-term outcome data remain limited. This study evaluated outcomes after lung transplantation for COVID-19 acute respiratory distress syndrome (CARDS) and post-COVID pulmonary fibrosis (CPF) using a national registry. Methods We performed a retrospective analysis of the United Network for Organ Sharing database from 2020 through 2024. Recipient characteristics, perioperative complications, and graft failure-free survival were analyzed in adult lung transplant recipients with a primary diagnosis of CARDS, CPF, or non-COVID restrictive lung disease (NCRLD). Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and multivariate logistic regression were performed to adjust for potential confounders. Results During the study period, 256 transplants were performed for CARDS, 338 for CPF, and 8071 for NCRLD. Post-COVID-19 recipients were younger (54 vs. 64 years, p 48 hours (67.5% vs. 43.3%, p Conclusions Lung transplantation for post-COVID-19 lung damage yields comparable short-term and mid-term survival outcomes despite higher perioperative morbidity and resource utilization. Long-term studies are needed to assess chronic lung allograft dysfunction in this population.

items.title: Prognostic Stratification of Adjuvant Immunotherapy After Neoadjuvant Chemoimmunotherapy and Quality Surgery in LA-ESCC
items.containerTitle: The Journal of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: In locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (LA-ESCC), neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy (NCIT) plus high-quality surgery (R0 resection with systematic lymphadenectomy >19 nodes) is a promising strategy. However, the value of adjuvant immunotherapy remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the association between postoperative adjuvant immunotherapy and survival outcomes in a multicenter cohort. METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study enrolled LA-ESCC patients receiving NCIT from eight high-volume Chinese centers between 2019 and 2023. After screening for high-quality surgery, propensity score matching (PSM) balanced characteristics between the two groups: NCIT plus surgery (NCIT+S) and NCIT plus surgery followed by adjuvant immunotherapy (NCIT+S+ICI). The primary endpoints were overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS). A prognostic framework based on major pathological response (MPR) and postoperative pathological N stage (ypN) was constructed to refine patient selection. RESULTS: Among 724 patients with a median follow-up of 40.3 months, 3-year OS and DFS rates were 73.0% and 67.7%, respectively. After PSM, adjuvant immunotherapy significantly improved DFS (77.1% vs 65.8%, log-rank P=0.037), but not OS (83.4% vs 69.4%, log-rank P=0.058). Multivariate analysis identified ypN, MPR, and postoperative adjuvant immunotherapy as independent prognostic factors for DFS. Stratification by MPR and ypN status showed that DFS benefit from adjuvant immunotherapy was restricted to the non-MPR/ypN+ subgroup (HR=0.339; 95% CI: 0.173-0.662; log-rank P<0.001), with a significant treatment-by-subgroup interaction (P for interaction=0.025). CONCLUSIONS: Among LA-ESCC patients receiving NCIT and high-quality surgery, adjuvant immunotherapy significantly improves 3-year DFS in the non-MPR/ypN+ subgroup, with no significant benefit in other subgroups.

items.title: American Association for Thoracic Surgery Quality Gateway Procedural Outcomes Models for General Thoracic Surgery Quality Assurance
items.containerTitle: The Journal of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery
items.abstract: Objective To develop quality assurance models for adverse procedural events after lung resection and esophagectomy for cancer. Methods Using procedural outcomes after 16,430 lung resections and 3,068 esophagectomies for cancer at 9 hospitals in 7 hospital systems, we developed 5 individual and 2 composite outcome models from preoperative information. Random forest quantile classification for imbalanced data with model-free variable priority screening identified predictors. Out-of-bag prediction provided regularized estimates and internal validation. Hospital-holdout analysis assessed institutional benchmark stability. Results Of 71 lung resection and 63 esophagectomy preoperative variables, 35 and 29, respectively, were identified as important predictors across the 7 outcome models. These included demographics, advanced cancer, organ dysfunction, higher acuity, and planned surgical approach and resection extent. Out-of-bag calibration covered a modest range of probabilities. Out-of-bag geometric mean ranged from 0.588 to 0.713 for lung resection and 0.517 to 0.649 for esophagectomy. Continuous risk factors, particularly pulmonary function, provided high-importance information content, with complex dependency and interaction structure among predictors. Risk-factor magnitude differed among hospitals, as did their risk-adjusted outcomes according to patient risk as determined by counterfactual inference within a framework of virtual twins. For lung resection operative mortality, hospital-specific contrasts were stable when each focal hospital was excluded from the aggregate benchmark. Conclusions Using contemporary machine learning, initial models for adverse procedural events after lung resection and esophagectomy for cancer have been developed. They provide surgeons, their patients, and hospital and hospital systems tools for patient risk assessment and for informing quality improvement initiatives in general thoracic surgery.

items.title: Contemporary Results of Operations for Mitral Regurgitation Caused by Posterior Mitral Valve Prolapse: The AATS Adult Quality Gateway
items.containerTitle: The Journal of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE: In patients undergoing surgical repair of posterior mitral valve prolapse, we compared outcomes in high- and low-volume mitral surgery hospitals to those predicted by the AATS Adult Quality Gateway (AQG) and the Society of Thoracic Surgeons Adult Cardiac Surgery Database (STS-ACSD). METHODS: Five hospitals performed 1,517 mitral valve operations, 1,471 repairs (97%) and 46 replacements (3.0%), in the AQG training set of 55,246 adult patients. Mitral repair techniques included leaflet resection (80%), creating artificial chordae (20%), and anuloplasty (99%); surgical approach was sternotomy or partial sternotomy in 945 (64%) and anterior thoracotomy or robotic in 525 (36%). The remaining 14 hospitals performed 159 mitral valve operations, 145 repairs (91%) and 14 (8.8%) replacements. RESULTS: In high-volume hospitals, predicted mortality by AQG was 0.87% and by STS-ACSD 0.77%; however, observed mortality was 1 patient (0.070%). For major morbidity and mortality, AQG predicted 8.1% and STS-ACSD 6.5%, but observed was 4.0%. Patients undergoing valve replacement were more likely to be older and more symptomatic and had more tricuspid regurgitation and mitral anular calcification. All repair outcomes were worse (e.g., operative mortality was 3/145 [2.1%]) in low-volume hospitals. CONCLUSIONS: Requiring limited data entry and employing novel statistical methodology (e.g. virtual twins), AQG provided predictions similar to those of STS-ACSD, both confirming and augmenting understanding of the volume-outcome relationship in surgical management of posterior mitral valve prolapse.

items.title: Right Heart Failure Pheno-Endotype Drives Prognosis after Tricuspid Valve Surgery
items.containerTitle: The Journal of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Tricuspid valve surgery is neither complex nor time-consuming yet is associated with high surgical mortality. Our goal was to characterize heterogeneity of right heart variables and manifestations of right heart failure in patients with severe tricuspid regurgitation and evaluate survival after tricuspid valve surgery. METHODS: From 1/2007 to 1/2014, 522 adults with severe tricuspid regurgitation underwent cardiac surgery. Median follow-up was 3.7 years. Right heart morphology and function variables were measured de novo from stored echocardiographic images. To discover possible pheno-endotypes, unsupervised cluster analysis was performed by sidClustering.rfsrc using preoperative clinical, morphologic, ventricular function, and hemodynamic variables. Variable priority classification was used to characterize resulting pheno-endotypes. Post-surgery survival was assessed by cluster. RESULTS: ), 46%; and Cluster 3 (n=224), predominantly patients with worse right ventricular dysfunction (fractional area change 30%±12%), 21% (worst prognosis). Elevated model for end-stage liver disease with sodium was the most important predictor of time-related mortality and separated Clusters 1 and 2 from Cluster 3. CONCLUSIONS: Patients presenting for cardiac surgery with severe tricuspid regurgitation cluster into 3 pheno-endotypes, illustrating clinical presentation and patient heterogeneity and predicting distinctive prognosis. Right heart function and right heart failure severity need to be recognized to guide patient selection and management.

items.title: Distal Reinterventions after Branched Stented Anastomosis Frozen Elephant Trunk Repair (B-SAFER): A Report from a Prospective Trial.
items.containerTitle: The Journal of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery
items.abstract: Objective Optimal timing for distal reintervention after frozen elephant trunk repair remains debated. We evaluated patient characteristics, clinical outcomes, and predictors of distal aortic reintervention following Branched Stented Anastomosis Frozen Elephant Trunk Repair (B-SAFER). Methods From May 2021 to January 2025, 405 patients underwent B-SAFER in a prospective, single-arm, nonrandomized PS-IDE cohort. Among them, 117 patients required 148 distal reinterventions. Indications for initial repair were acute type A dissection (36/189, 31%), chronic dissection (62/138, 53%), and degenerative aneurysm (19/78, 16%). Most reinterventions (n=132, 92%) were planned. Primary endpoints were operative mortality, stroke, and paralysis. Kaplan-Meier analysis assessed survival and freedom from reintervention. Median follow-up was 1.3 years, and median time to reintervention was 8.7 months. Results Mortality after first reintervention was 6.5% (n=8). Permanent stroke occurred in one patient (0.8%), with no cases of paralysis. Causes of death included sepsis (n=4), hemorrhagic shock (n=2), pulmonary embolism (n=1), and intracranial hemorrhage (n=1). Freedom from reintervention at 2 years was 64%, lowest in chronic dissections (48%), intermediate in degenerative aneurysms (71%), and highest in acute dissections (74%). Larger descending and abdominal aortic diameters were the strongest predictors of reintervention. Survival at 2.5 years was similar across groups (81% acute, 81% chronic, 77% degenerative). Conclusions Distal reinterventions after B-SAFER are common, safe, and are associated with acceptable early outcomes. Disease chronicity and aortic diameter predict reintervention risk. Frozen elephant trunk is an effective platform for staged aortic repair, and earlier reintervention in high-risk patients warrants further study. (245).

items.title: Analyzing the Economic and Logistical Impact of Lung Procurement on Transplant Centers in the Era of Continuous Distribution
items.containerTitle: The Journal of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery
items.abstract: Objective The recent transition to the Composite Allocation Score (CAS) has increased travel distances for lung transplants, but an associated cost analysis has not been performed. We assessed travel costs and short-term outcomes of lung transplantation before and after transitioning to CAS. Methods The United Network for Organ Sharing database was queried for all lung transplants from 1/2020 to 12/2024. Redo and pediatric lung and multiorgan transplants were excluded. Patients were stratified between pre- and post-CAS, which began on 3/9/2023. Outcomes were distance of donor-to-recipient in nautical miles (nm), inflation-adjusted travel costs, and perioperative outcomes. Results A total of 7,835 (58.6%) pre-CAS and 5,538 (41.4%) post-CAS patients were included. Post-CAS patients were more likely female (41.7% vs. 38.5%, p 1000 nm) increased (10.7% vs. 2.0%, p Conclusions CAS has reduced waitlist duration with preserved one-year survival for lung transplant patients, but introduces greater logistical complexity and cost, which requires continued reevaluation to ensure economic viability and long-term sustainability of transplant programs.

items.title: Evolving Trends in Tracheobronchoplasty: Longitudinal Outcomes of Open and Robotic Approaches
items.containerTitle: The Journal of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery
items.abstract: Objective Tracheobronchoplasty (TBP) is an operation to treat excessive central airway collapse by stabilizing the posterior membranous wall of the central airways. We compare postoperative complications and longitudinal outcomes between the open and robotic TBP, with attention to evolving outcomes in robotic TBP. Methods We conducted a retrospective review of all open TBP (2018-2020) and robotic-assisted TBP (2020-2025) at a high-volume center. The primary outcomes were major complications, classified by Clavien-Dindo grade ≥3a. Secondary outcomes included quality-of-life metrics and 6-minute walk test (6MWT) at 3 and 12 months post-operatively. A subgroup analysis compared early (2020-2023) versus recent (2024-2025) robotic-assisted TBP cases. Results 132 patients were included: 69 open and 63 robotic TBP. There were no significant differences in the major complication rates on univariate or adjusted multivariable analysis (adjusted OR 0.70, p=0.47). Both groups demonstrated improvement in quality-of-life scores and 6MWT at 3 and 12 months post-operatively. Robotic TBP had longer operative times (475 vs. 397 minutes; p Conclusions Robotic TBP is safe and effective when compared to the open approach in selected patients, demonstrating comparable complication rates and durable improvements in quality-of-life measures. With shorter ICU stays and decreasing operative times, ongoing experience with robotic TBP continues to yield improvements in efficiency and postoperative recovery.

items.title: Preoperative Predictors of Outcome for Adults Undergoing Congenital Cardiac Surgery: Multicenter Model Validation
items.containerTitle: The Journal of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery
items.abstract: Objective Adults with congenital heart disease (ACHD) undergoing cardiac surgery represent a growing population in whom conventional surgical risk models perform suboptimally. We externally validated a previously described ACHD-specific preoperative risk model and evaluated whether performance could be improved through recalibration/model updating. Methods We conducted a prospective, multicenter observational study of patients ≥16 years undergoing congenital cardiac surgery at four centers (March 2020-April 2023). The primary composite adverse outcome (CAO) comprised in-hospital death, prolonged ventilation >7 days, or new-onset dialysis. We evaluated discrimination and calibration of the original preoperative model (including MELD-XI, cognitive impairment, body-mass index [BMI], prior chest wall incisions, and complex anatomy) and then performed bootstrap-based model updating (200 resamples) to derive refined models with and without the Adult Congenital Heart Surgery (ACHS) procedural mortality score. Results Among 538 patients, CAO occurred in 4.3% (n=23). In external validation (n=383 complete cases), the original model preserved discrimination (AUC=0.729, 95% confidence interval: 0.602-0.855) but systematically overestimated risk, indicating need for recalibration. The refined model retained BMI, prior chest incisions, cognitive impairment, age, serum albumin level, and ventricular systolic dysfunction. Discrimination was good without procedural complexity (AUC=0.799; 0.697-0.900) and improved with inclusion of the ACHS score (AUC=0.857; 0.779-0.935). Conclusions In this prospective multicenter external validation, an ACHD-specific preoperative risk model maintained discrimination but required recalibration. Incorporating procedural complexity enhanced discrimination, supporting a hybrid patient- and procedure-based approach to guide perioperative planning.

items.title: Interstage Reinterventions in Hybrid Stage I Palliation - Impact on Survival to Comprehensive Stage II Operation
items.containerTitle: The Journal of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE: The need for interstage reinterventions is one of the perceived limitations of Hybrid Stage 1 Palliation (HS1P). We aim to evaluate the impact of unplanned interstage reinterventions on survival to comprehensive stage II (CS2) and characterize their frequency, type, and timing. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 199 infants who underwent HS1P at a single institution from 2009 to 2025, tracking all reinterventions between HS1P and CS2. We assessed the likelihood of reaching CS2 using a series of Fine-Gray models at distinct landmarks to assess competing risks, comparing reintervention and non-reintervention groups. RESULTS: The reintervention rate in our study was 43%, with 132 unique reinterventions received in 86 patients. In the reintervention group, progression to CS2 was 78%, with 4.7% of patients dying after HS1P. Among the 33 patients (17%) who died after HS1P, 88% did not receive reinterventions and 76% died prior to HS1P discharge. Reinterventions before 90 days post-HS1P were associated with no difference in progression to CS2 (sHR 1.20, CI 0.83-1.74), but reinterventions before 150 days post-HS1P were associated with a decreased likelihood of reaching CS2 (sHR 0.61, CI 0.41-0.93). The most common reintervention target was the retrograde aortic arch (45%), with aortic atresia in 72% of these patients. CONCLUSIONS: Interstage reinterventions after HS1P are common, but, if done early, do not appear to worsen survival to comprehensive stage II. Reinterventions play an integral part of HS1P care rather than a marker of failure, especially when performed early.

items.title: Outcomes After Curative-intent Resection of Synchronous Primary Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC): Two is Worse than One
items.containerTitle: The Journal of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery
items.abstract: Objective Outcomes following curative-intent resection of synchronous primary lung cancer (SPLC) remain incompletely defined. We compared recurrence and survival in SPLC versus solitary primary tumors among patients with clinical stage I non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Methods Retrospective cohort study of Veterans undergoing curative-intent resection for clinical stage I NSCLC in the Veterans Health Administration (2006-2020). SPLC was defined as two distinct clinical stage I NSCLC tumors diagnosed within six weeks, with curative-intent treatment of both tumors within one year. Propensity score matching (PSM) (1:1) was used to compare patients with SPLC to those with solitary tumors. The primary outcome was cumulative incidence of recurrence (CIR); secondary outcomes were overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS). Additional analyses examined the role of adjuvant treatment and drivers of recurrence in SPLC patients. Results Of 12,606 Veterans with resected clinical stage I NSCLC, 337 (2.7%) had SPLC. SPLC presented with larger tumors and more advanced pathologic stage. Histology was discordant between the two tumors in 44.2% of SPLC cases. In the propensity-matched cohort (281 pairs), SPLC was associated with higher CIR (HR 1.51, 95% CI 1.10-2.07), worse DFS (HR 1.24, 95% CI 1.03-1.50), and worse OS (HR 1.21, 95% CI 1.01-1.45). Within SPLC, wedge resection of both tumors was independently associated with recurrence. Conclusions After adjustment, SPLC was associated with higher recurrence and worse survival than solitary tumors, supporting recognition of SPLC as a higher-risk phenotype within clinical stage I NSCLC.

items.title: Cardiothoracic Surgery Training Attrition (2014–2023): Predictors, Trends, and Delay-Adjusted Rates Across Traditional and Integrated Pathways.
items.containerTitle: The Journal of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery
items.abstract: Objectives Resident attrition disrupts training pipelines and threatens cardiothoracic (CT) surgical workforce sustainability. This study quantifies national attrition rates and identifies predictors using trainee data from the Association of American Medical Colleges (AAMC), while accounting for reporting delays. Methods We analyzed de-identified records of 1,476 CT surgery residents entering ACGME-accredited programs from 2014 to 2023. Attrition was defined as departure before expected completion. Rates were stratified by year, gender, citizenship, and training pathway: integrated (TS-I) versus traditional (TS). Multivariable logistic regression, LASSO, Random Forest, and XGBoost with nested cross-validation were used to identify predictors. A parametric nowcasting model corrected for administrative reporting lag. Results The overall attrition rate was 3.9% (57/1,476), significantly higher in the TS-I than the TS pathway (7.0% vs. 2.6%, p 36 group (aOR 6.05, 95% CI 1.87-19.62) compared with those ≤30 years. Gender and citizenship were not significant after adjustment. Model performance was consistent across methods (AUC 0.67-0.72). Delay-adjusted analyses corrected an apparent decline in recent cohorts, revealing a stable underlying rate with a 3-4-year reporting lag. Conclusions Training pathways are the strongest predictor of CT resident attrition, with TS-I trainees at markedly higher risk. Correcting reporting delays is critical for accurate workforce planning. These findings support targeted retention interventions for at-risk trainees.

Contemporary Trends in Approval for Donation After Circulatory Death Heart Transplantation in the United States
items.abstract: Objective To characterize contemporary U.S. patterns of donation after circulatory death (DCD) candidate approval and center adoption, and to quantify the association between DCD approval and waitlist outcomes. Methods From the UNOS registry, 20,613 adult candidates listed for isolated heart transplantation in 2019-2024 were identified; 2023-2024 was defined as the contemporary era. Listing centers with ≥20 candidates in 2023-2024 (n=103) were classified as high (≥75%) or low (<25%) DCD approval. One-year cumulative incidence of transplantation and waitlist death or delisting was modeled by Fine-Gray sub distribution hazards regression. Results DCD approval at listing is associated with higher 1-year transplantation [adjusted sHR 1.29, 95% CI 1.13-1.47] and lower waitlist death/delisting [sHR 0.56, 0.42-0.76] at the candidate level. Contemporary center-level DCD approval (60.4% overall) is sharply bimodal: 21 centers (20%) approved none and 9 (9%) approved all. Center adoption gradually expanded: by 2024, mean center-level approval reached 79% among early adopters (first DCD approval 2019-2020, n=49), 60% among intermediate adopters (2021-2022, n=24), and 50% among late adopters (2023-2024, n=19). High-approval centers have higher 1-year transplantation [89% vs. 81%, adjusted sHR 1.43, 95% CI 1.17-1.74] and lower death/delisting [3% vs. 7%, sHR 0.54, 0.37-0.78] compared to low-approval centers; the gap persisted after accounting for pre-DCD-era program quality. Conclusions DCD approval was associated with improved contemporary era waitlist outcomes at both the candidate- and center-levels. Expanding access depends on program adoption more than candidate selection and translates into benefit that warrants institutional investment.

items.title: Predicting Successful Biventricular Conversion in Patients with Palliated Hypoplastic Left Ventricles
items.abstract: Objectives For patients with palliated hypoplastic left ventricles (HLV), the decision for biventricular (BiV) conversion can be challenging. We sought to identify preoperative characteristics that predict successful BiV repair. Methods Retrospective study from 2005-2025 of patients with palliated HLV who underwent BiV conversion. All had preoperative cardiac magnetic resonance imaging or computed tomography, and catheterization data. The primary composite outcome included death, transplant, or BiV repair takedown. The secondary composite outcome included unexpected re-intervention related to LV dysfunction or LV failure. Results Of 175 patients, 51% had prior LV recruitment, 42% had abnormal segmental anatomy, 51% had right dominant atrioventricular canal defect, 44% had abnormal conotruncal anatomy, and 13% had endocardial fibroelastosis (EFE). 17% met the primary outcome and 42% met the secondary outcome. For 119 (68%) with at least 3 years of follow-up, CART analysis identified risk factors of EFE, left ventricular end-diastolic pressure (LVEDP), mitral valve orifice area index, right ventricular mass index, and heart rate, with an area under the curve of 0.75 (95% CI 0.62-0.87) on out-of-sample cross-validation. By multivariate logistic regression, EFE (OR 5.85, p=0.01), LVEDp (OR 1.27, p=0.03) and right ventricular mass index (OR 1.07, p <0.01) were associated with the primary outcome at 3 years. Conclusions We present a CART-derived risk stratification model that identifies combinations of preoperative factors associated with LV adequacy following biventricular repair. Although the model requires external validation, it provides empirically derived thresholds that may complement clinical assessment.

items.title: Prolonged air leak after segmentectomy: anatomical risk factors and comparison with lobectomy
items.abstract: Objectives To identify anatomical risk factors for prolonged air leak (PAL) after segmentectomy and compare the risk of PAL between segmentectomy with these factors and lobectomy. Methods This two-institution retrospective study included 914 of 1,102 consecutive patients who underwent segmentectomy (n=314) or lobectomy (n=600) between 2020 and 2025. Multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify anatomical risk factors for PAL after segmentectomy and to compare the risk of PAL between segmentectomy with these factors and lobectomy. The anatomical factors evaluated were the number of resected segments, location of resected segments (upper vs lower lobe), and segmentectomy type (simple vs complex segmentectomy). Results Resection of ≥3 segments (odds ratio, 4.33; 95% confidence interval, 1.17–16.1; p=0.028) and upper-lobe location (odds ratio, 3.31; 95% confidence interval, 1.20–9.13; p=0.021) were independently associated with PAL after segmentectomy, with a high PAL incidence observed after left upper division segmentectomy. PAL occurred in 19.7% of segmentectomies with both anatomical factors, compared with 1.7% of those without either factor (p<0.001). Segmentectomy with both anatomical factors was associated with a significantly higher risk of PAL compared with lobectomy (odds ratio, 2.43; 95% confidence interval, 1.22–4.84; p=0.011). Conclusions Resection of ≥3 segments and upper-lobe location were associated with an increased risk of PAL after segmentectomy, and procedures involving both factors, such as left upper division segmentectomy, showed a higher risk of PAL than lobectomy.

items.title: Hemodynamic Phenotype and Early Outcomes of Aortopulmonary Collaterals in Neonates With d-Transposition Undergoing Arterial Switch Operation
items.abstract: Objective Aortopulmonary collateral vessels (APCs) are increasingly recognised in neonates with d-transposition of the great arteries (d-TGA), yet it remains unclear whether treated (haemodynamically significant) APCs represent a distinct haemodynamic phenotype associated with early postoperative vulnerability after arterial switch operation (ASO). We evaluated the prevalence, phenotype, and early outcomes of APCs in a contemporary Australian ASO programme. Methods We performed a retrospective review of neonates undergoing ASO at The Children's Hospital at Westmead (Sydney Children's Hospitals Network) between January 2014 and September 2024. APCs were identified by echocardiography, catheterisation, or operative findings, following a clinically triggered stepwise diagnostic algorithm. APCs were classified as significant if they were judged haemodynamically important and required coil occlusion and/or surgical ligation. Baseline characteristics and early postoperative outcomes were compared between significant and non-significant APC groups. Exploratory analyses assessed potential predictors of significant APCs. Results Among 239 ASO patients, 17 (7.1%) had APCs identified; 8/17 (47%) required intervention (significant) and 9/17 (53%) were non-significant. Patients with significant APCs were smaller at surgery (median 3.05 kg vs 3.70 kg) and more frequently had an echocardiographically confirmed patent ductus arteriosus at preoperative assessment (100% vs 33.3%). Significant APCs were observed in patients with substantially longer postoperative support requirements, including mechanical ventilation, ICU length of stay, and hospital length of stay. All deaths, reoperations, and recatheterisations occurred in the significant-APC group. Conclusions APCs identified in neonates undergoing arterial switch operation appear to cluster within a recognisable clinical phenotype characterised by persistent ductal patency and a more complex postoperative recovery. Although the clinically triggered diagnostic pathway precludes causal inference and likely underestimates the true prevalence of APCs, these findings support heightened awareness of collateral vessels in patients with an atypical postoperative course and provide a foundation for future prospective investigation.

items.title: Estimated Costs and Cost-Effectiveness of Pediatric Cardiac Surgery: A World Atlas
items.abstract: Objectives Public health stakeholders in Low-and Middle-Income Countries (LMIC) assume pediatric cardiac surgery (PCS) to be a very costly enterprise, prioritizing other investments in public health. As advocates for global availability of PCS, we need tools to demonstrate the Cost-Effectiveness (CE) of the health interventions we recommend, providing guidance to the decision makers. We estimated the costs and CE of PCS in every country (currently available or not). Methods We designed and made publicly available 2 calculators based on 2022 demographic data and 2023 prices: A Congenital Heart Disease (CHD) incidence and a PCS Costs and CE calculators. Cost-effectiveness was calculated at 39.9 Disability Adjusted Life Years (DALY) averted per surgical survivor as previously published. We used Gross National Income per capita (GNI p/c) at purchasing power parity for CE calculations. Results The median estimated cost of PCS per patient, across all countries and territories included (n=215), was $6 963 (IQR $5617). Calculated Median CE among countries included (n=163) was $173 (IQR $133) per DALY averted. With a cost-effectiveness lower than the annual GNI p/c in every single country studied, funding of PCS would be a highly cost-effective health intervention. Conclusions While final prices for PCS may be out of the reach for most families, our estimated costs would seem to be within range of other publications and highly cost-effective in every country studied. It is up to each society's willingness to pay to decide the future of their children born with CHD.

1-Year Outcomes of Endovascular Repair of Zone 0/1 Aortic Arch Lesions with a Thoracic Branched Endoprosthesis
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: The GORE® TAG® Thoracic Branch Endoprosthesis (TBE) pivotal non-randomized, multicenter, prospective trial evaluated 1-year outcomes in patients at high risk for open surgical repair undergoing aortic arch and descending thoracic aorta endovascular repair (Zone 0/1). METHODS: Endpoints evaluated from endovascular procedure through 12 months included aortic-related death, disabling stroke, permanent paraplegia or paraparesis, new onset renal failure, and unanticipated reintervention. Core-lab identified endpoints included aortic rupture or enlargement (≥5 mm), Type I/III endoleak, device integrity, device migration, fistula, patency, and new dissection. RESULTS: The 77 enrolled patients had aneurysm (n=50), dissection (n=24), or other isolated lesion types (n=3); 90.9% had a Zone 0 proximal stent landing zone. Patients were a mean age of 70.8±10.8 years, 66.2% male, and 57.1% white and all had the aortic and side branch component implanted. Technical success was 94.8%. Early outcomes to 12 months included 8 (10.4%) aortic-related deaths, 6 (7.8%) disabling strokes (all aneurysm cohort), 4 (5.2%) unanticipated reintervention, 2 (2.6%) aortic ruptures, and 1 (1.3%) renal failure. Type IA/IB or Type III endoleaks occurred in 6 (7.8%) patients. Loss of side branch patency occurred in 1 (1.3%) patient. There was no permanent paraplegia or paraparesis or loss of device integrity or migration. A total of five patients had aortic enlargement; none required reintervention. CONCLUSIONS: Early data from this prospective investigation of the TBE device in Zone 0/1 applications signals that the device is a reasonable therapeutic alternative in patients with appropriate anatomy deemed high risk for open arch surgery.

items.title: Characterizing One-Year Mortality in Early Survivors of Open Thoracoabdominal Aortic Repair
items.abstract: Background Although operative mortality after open thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm (TAAA) repair is well characterized, only limited data describe 1-year survival among patients who survive the index hospitalization. This study sought to further characterize 1-year mortality among operative survivors of open TAAA repair. Methods From January 1986 through July 2025, 3838 open TAAA repairs were performed within our single practice. After operative deaths and patients lacking 1-year follow-up were excluded, 3378 early survivors comprised the study cohort. Demographic, operative, and postoperative data were compared between patients who survived ≥1 year after repair and those who did not. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of 1-year mortality. Results Among early survivors, 328 (9.7%) died within 1 year. One-year mortality was associated with older age, prior percutaneous coronary intervention, prior stroke, and chronic kidney disease. Postoperative complications-namely paraplegia (odds ratio [OR] 1.96, P=.03), dialysis dependence (OR 2.00, P=.001), arrhythmia (OR 1.48, P=.01), tracheostomy (OR 2.17, P Conclusions Among operative survivors of open TAAA repair, 1-year mortality remains considerable and is primarily determined by persistent postoperative complications and repair durability rather than intraoperative variables. Vigilant surveillance, structured rehabilitation, and multidisciplinary follow-up may be needed to ensure success beyond the perioperative period.
