Current Generation Self-Expanding and Balloon-Expandable Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Retrospective Multicenter Analysis
items.abstract: Background Evolving transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) technology warrants updated comparisons of the most commonly used current generation self-expanding (SE) versus balloon-expandable (BE) transcatheter heart valves (THV). Methods This 9-center retrospective analysis stratified patients undergoing TAVR from 2021-2024 into SE-THV and BE-THV cohorts balanced via propensity score matching. Primary outcomes were all-cause and cardiovascular mortality, stroke, and permanent pacemaker (PPM) need. Secondary outcomes were paravalvular leak (PVL) and acute kidney injury. All outcomes were assessed perioperatively and at 30 and 400 days. Analyses were repeated within LVEF , aortic valve area, and center-level strata. Results The total cohort included 2,594 BE-THV and 1,058 SE-THV patients. Matching yielded 680 patients per cohort. After matching , SE-THV patients had higher risk for ischemic stroke (p Conclusions In this cohort, SE-THV correlated with higher rates of ischemic stroke, PPM need, and PVL during index hospitalization and increased mild and moderate PVL upon follow-up. Mortality did not differ during index hospitalization or at follow-up. The normal LVEF SE-THV cohort was associated with higher stroke risk compared to all other groups.

items.title: Topical Vancomycin for Prevention of Grade 2 or Higher Sternal Wound Infection After Cardiac Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Trial
items.abstract: Background To evaluate the efficacy and safety of topical vancomycin paste over the sternal edges in preventing sternal wound infection (SWI). Methods This single-center, prospective, single-blind controlled trial 1:1 randomized 360 adult patients undergoing elective full sternotomy cardiac surgery to receive either vancomycin paste or normal saline (NCT04500275). The primary endpoint was SWI within 90 postoperative days. The secondary endpoints included postoperative acute kidney injury, emergence of resistant pathogens and systemic vancomycin exposure. Results The incidence of grade 2 or higher SWI within 90 days was significantly lower in the vancomycin group than in the placebo group (1 of 180, 0.6% vs. 7 of 180, 3.9%, p = .031). The subdistribution hazard ratio was 0.14 (p = .065). Deep SWI rate was 0.6% vs. 2.8% (p = .099). The incidence of acute kidney injury was comparable between the groups (31.7% vs. 28.9%, p = .251), even in patients with CKD stages ≥ 3. Systemic vancomycin concentrations were negligible and declined over time in non-dialysis patients. Levels above 10-20 mg/L persisted in some patients undergoing hemodialysis. Three cases of vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus from various sources were observed in the vancomycin group of patients with CKD stage ≥ 3 or undergoing hemodialysis. Conclusions Topical vancomycin reduced grade 2 or higher SWI without increasing the risk of acute kidney injury. Systemic exposure was negligible, except in patients undergoing hemodialysis. While the emergence of VRE cannot be excluded, its incidence was negligible and does not outweigh the benefits of SWI reduction when using topical vancomycin.

items.title: Body Height and Stentgraft Diameter Drive Thrombus Formation After Frozen Elephant Trunk Repair: A Risk-Focused Analysis
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Intraluminal thrombus formation is an increasingly recognized complication after frozen elephant trunk (FET) repair. This study aims to identify the key factors driving thrombus risk, and to characterize the prognostic impact of thrombus on long-term survival. METHODS: Retrospective single-center analysis of 458 patients undergoing FET repair between 2013 and 2024. Parameters were evaluated for association with new intraluminal thrombus formation using Fine-Gray competing risk regression. Thrombus risk was visualized using a height-stentgraft diameter risk heatmap. Estimated intraprosthetic blood velocity was analyzed by receiver-operating-characteristic analysis and restricted cubic splines. RESULTS: Sixty patients (13.1%) developed new intraluminal thrombus during a median follow-up of 3.2 years (IQR 1.1-5.5). In multivariable analysis, the standardized stentgraft-to-patient-height-ratio was independently associated with new thrombus formation (HR 1.55 [95% confidence interval 1.11-2.16]; p=0.009), alongside fresh frozen plasma transfusion (HR 1.46 [95% CI 1.00-2.13]; p=0.049). The risk-heatmap demonstrated highest adjusted thrombus risk in short-statured patients receiving large-diameter stentgrafts. Estimated intraprosthetic blood velocity was significantly lower in patients who developed thrombus; an optimal velocity threshold of 14.4 cm/s (area under the curve 0.644; sensitivity 82.8%, specificity 43.2%) was associated with a 3-fold higher thrombus rate below vs. above this threshold (16.1% vs. 5.0%). Maximum thrombus diameter was an independent predictor of death within the thrombus subgroup (HR 1.130 [1.041-1.227] per mm; p=0.004). CONCLUSIONS: Post-FET thrombus risk is highest when a disproportionately large stentgraft is implanted in a short-statured patient; reduced intraprosthetic blood velocity may represent a contributing hemodynamic mechanism, a hypothesis-generating finding that requires prospective validation.

items.title: Transcarotid Access for Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement With the Evolut Self-Expanding Valve: Outcomes from a Real-World Registry
items.abstract: Background Transcarotid access for transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is the most commonly used alternate access in the United States. Real-world evidence on transcarotid access using the Evolut self-expanding valve based on larger numbers of patients may help inform treatment optimization towards better outcomes. Methods The Society of Thoracic Surgeons/American College of Cardiology Transcatheter Valve Therapies Registry™ was queried for patients undergoing native TAVR using transcarotid access with an Evolut (January 2015-December 2024). In-hospital, 30-day, and 1-year outcomes are reported. Results We identified 2,105 patients (mean age 78.3±7.9 years) with mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons predicted risk of mortality 6.4±5.3. Most were high/extreme surgical risk (60.0%) with New York Heart Association class III/IV heart failure symptoms (66.8%) and mean baseline Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ) Score 45.3±25.4. Implant success was 99.6% primarily using general anesthesia (95.8%) with median procedure time of 88.0 (Q1=68.0, Q3=115.0) minutes. Median length of stay was 2.0 (Q1=1.0, Q3=3.0) days; 89.0% were discharged to home. In-hospital, 30-day and 1-year all-cause mortality was 2.1%, 3.8% and 16.5%; stroke occurred in 3.1%, 3.8% and 5.1% of patients, respectively. At 30 days, major vascular complications (1.9%), valve related (0.4%) and non-valve related (10.9%) readmissions were low. The mean change in KCCQ score from baseline to 1-year was +30.5±27.1 points. Conclusions Transcarotid TAVR with the Evolut TAV is an effective, safe approach for patients with unfavorable iliofemoral anatomy. Heart teams should become facile with this technique to provide optimal care across the anatomy spectrum.

items.title: The Society of Thoracic Surgeons (2026) Expert Consensus Document on Management of Borderline Left Heart Excluding Unbalanced Atrioventricular Septal Defect and Strategies for Biventricular Conversion
items.abstract: Background Strategies to recruit the left ventricle in borderline left heart (BLH), whether utilizing primary or staged recruitment strategy, are challenged by lack of consensus regarding optimal substrate, timing, and technique. Methods A panel of experienced congenital cardiac surgeons, cardiologists and imaging experts were convened to develop key questions related to BLH management, excluding unbalanced atrioventricular septal defect, from neonatal period through 1 year, using the PICO (Patients/Population, Intervention, Comparison/Control, Outcome) framework. Literature searches were performed for each question. Using a modified Delphi method, consensus statements were developed. Results For neonates with BLH, primary biventricular repair should be adopted cautiously, and only with favorable anatomic and physiologic criteria determined by echocardiography and/or magnetic resonance imaging. Neonates in the 'grey-zone', with smaller mitral and aortic valve sizes, endocardial fibroelastosis, indexed left ventricular diastolic volume 2 and ascending aortic flow 2 , should undergo staged recruitment to potentially facilitate growth of left-sided structures and more durable surgical rehabilitation of left ventricular inflow and outflow. Timing and type of subsequent procedures should be guided by interval cardiac catheterization and magnetic resonance imaging data. Initial palliation of grey-zone neonates can be accomplished with either surgical Norwood or hybrid stage 1 with possible atrial level restriction, and subsequent endocardial fibroelastosis resection along with aortic and mitral valve repair as components of successful complete biventricular conversion. Conclusions Biventricular approaches in BLH should be guided by integration of anatomic and physiologic criteria, with most neonates recommended for staged recruitment rather than primary repair.

items.title: Mitral Annular Calcification: Operative Decision Making and Technical Considerations
items.abstract: Background Mitral annular calcification (MAC) presents a formidable challenge in mitral valve surgery owing to risks of atrioventricular groove disruption, circumflex artery injury, and paravalvular leaks. The optimal operative strategy varies according to the severity of annular calcification, extent of ventricular extension, and the patient-specific risk profile. Methods A narrative expert review was performed synthesizing contemporary surgical series, imaging-guided approaches, and transcatheter strategies for mitral valve intervention in the setting of MAC. Technical considerations, complication avoidance strategies, and decision-making frameworks were integrated into a new severity-based operative algorithm. Results We developed a decision matrix to stratify patients into four categories to guide preoperative planning and operative decisions. MAC management lies on a spectrum between working around the MAC with no resection ("respect" the MAC) to complete MAC resection with atrioventricular groove reconstruction ("resect" the MAC). Severe or circumferential MAC demands tailored strategies, including transcatheter or hybrid approaches. In patients with mild MAC, mitral valve repair remains feasible and preferred. Moderate MAC requires individualized decision-making; repair is achievable when leaflet mobility is preserved, and decalcification permits secure annuloplasty. Replacement is favored when leaflet restriction or annular rigidity precludes durable reconstruction. The extent of decalcification should be tailored to the patient's risk profile and surgical expertise to ensure durable results. Conclusions Mitral valve intervention in the setting of MAC requires an individualized approach. We propose a practical management algorithm, stratified by patient risk and anatomic feasibility.

items.title: Regionalization and Joint Reporting: A Counterpoint Perspective
One Year Survival of High-Risk Patients Undergoing Coronary Revascularization
items.abstract: Background In high-risk patients requiring coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) we sought to evaluate the differential impact of comorbid and cardiovascular risk factors on perioperative versus one year survival with the hypothesis that different phenotypes of perioperative risk may portend different longitudinal outcomes and that not all high-risk features are equivalent. Methods The Society Thoracic Surgeons (STS) Adult Cardiac Surgery Database (ACSD) was used to assess all patients (n=75,385) ≥65 years of age undergoing isolated CABG with a predicted risk of mortality (PROM) greater than 4% (2012-2022). The database was linked with Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) claims data to evaluate one-year mortality. Change in risk-adjusted odds ratios for 30-day and 1-year mortality were assessed using landmark analysis to identify variables associated with early versus late mortality. Results A total of 67,376 (89.4%) patients survived 30-days of those 8,998 (13.4%) died between 30 days and one year. Liver disease and home oxygen were associated with increased mortality at both 30 days and 1 year. However, unresponsive state, prior CABG, percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) within 6 hours, cardiogenic shock, and temporary mechanical support were associated with early mortality but exhibited no significant effects at 1 year. Finally, cancer, Medicaid coverage, and dialysis were initially neutral for 30-day mortality but emerged as independent risk factors for 1-year mortality. Conclusions In high-risk CABG, prognostic determinants evolve over time. These findings underscore the importance of incorporating temporal risk dynamics into clinical decisions.

items.title: We Love Aortic Surgery, But It’s the Genes that Hold the Key to Thoracic Aortic Aneurysm Disease
Open TAR: Still the Benchmark
Lifetime Management of Aortic Stenosis: Expert Review of Evidence and Consensus Guidelines
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: The 2025 European Society of Cardiology/European Association for Cardio-Thoracic Surgery Guidelines introduced a Class I recommendation for transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) in selected patients aged 70 years or older with tricuspid aortic stenosis and suitable anatomy, while surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) remains recommended in younger low-risk patients. In patients with long expected survival, this framework requires careful consideration of valve durability, future reintervention, and patient preferences. This expert review, developed by the Italian Cardiac Surgery Working Group, examines contemporary evidence and consensus recommendations from a lifetime-management perspective. METHODS: We performed a narrative, evidence-based synthesis of randomized trials, trial-based meta-analyses, and propensity-matched real-world registries comparing transfemoral TAVI and SAVR, with primary emphasis on low-risk patients. Lower-intermediate-risk evidence was included only when directly relevant to lifetime management, durability, or reintervention. RESULTS: Evidence suggests that treatment effects are time-dependent: early non-inferiority of TAVI may attenuate with longer follow-up, particularly in patients with substantial life expectancy. Randomized durability data remain limited, whereas propensity-matched real-world registries have suggested possible higher late mortality after TAVI in younger, lower-risk populations. Reintervention after a transcatheter-first strategy may be associated with increasing technical complexity and procedural risk over time. CONCLUSIONS: This review supports appropriate application of current guidelines through a pragmatic framework for individualized, Heart Team-based decision-making. Transfemoral TAVI is often appropriate in patients with limited life expectancy or recognized high surgical risk when anatomically feasible. In patients with long expected survival, SAVR should retain a central role as an important reference strategy.

items.title: Electrosurgical septotomy across the full spectrum of aortic dissection
items.abstract: Objectives Transcatheter electrosurgical septotomy divides the dissection membrane to reconstitute a single aortic lumen. Reported experience is largely confined to chronic post-dissection aneurysms. We assessed the technique across the full spectrum of descending aortic dissection, including stand-alone treatment of malperfusion. Methods Retrospective intention-to-treat analysis of 21 consecutive patients scheduled for septotomy between June 2022 and May 2026. The membrane was crossed by needle re-entry and divided with an electrified through-and-through guidewire at 40–60 W under fluoroscopy, without routine intravascular ultrasound or image fusion. A perfused-lumen index (perfused lumen divided by total aortic diameter) was measured before and after the procedure. Results Septotomy was performed in 20 of 21 patients (technical success 95% on an intention-to-treat basis). Indications were landing-zone preparation (57%), malperfusion (33%), preparation for open repair and true-lumen collapse. Malperfusion resolved in all 7 patients treated for that indication, and the perfused-lumen index rose from a median of 0.16 to 0.98 (18 patients, P < 0.001). There was no stroke, spinal cord ischaemia or retrograde type A dissection. Thirty-day, in-hospital and overall mortality were 10%, 14% and 19%, with one fatal delayed aortic rupture and no intraprocedural death. Three unplanned reinterventions occurred; median follow-up was 5.1 months. Conclusions Electrosurgical septotomy was feasible across the full spectrum of aortic dissection and, in selected patients, as stand-alone treatment for malperfusion, using standard electrosurgical equipment. Given the small heterogeneous cohort and short follow-up, these findings demonstrate feasibility rather than durability.

items.title: Reinventing coronary bypass surgery: A journey
Corrigendum to: Building the Future: A Proposed Framework for Training Residents in Minimally Invasive Cardiac Surgery
Development of the ECMO nursing self-efficacy Perception scale: A validity and reliability study
items.abstract: Caring for patients receiving ECMO in the ICU is a complex process that requires advanced knowledge, technical skills, and confident clinical decision-making from nurses. Despite the increasing use of ECMO in Türkiye, no comprehensive, validated tool exists to measure ICU nurses’ self-efficacy in ECMO care. This methodological study aimed to develop the ECMO Nursing Self-Efficacy Perception Scale (ECMO-SEPS) and evaluate its psychometric properties. The scale was developed in two stages. In the first stage, an item pool was generated through an extensive literature review and qualitative interviews with seven ICU nurses experienced in ECMO care. In the second stage, the scale’s content and construct validity were assessed using confirmatory factor analysis, including convergent and discriminant validity evaluations. Reliability analyses included internal consistency, evaluated by Cronbach’s alpha coefficients, and test–retest reliability, assessed with intraclass correlation coefficients. The final scale consists of 37 items across three subscales: cognitive, affective, and psychomotor, collectively explaining 70.5% of the total variance. Confirmatory factor analysis supported the three-factor structure with acceptable to good model fit indices. The overall Cronbach’s alpha was 0.97, with 0.97, 0.81, and 0.96 for the cognitive, affective, and psychomotor subscales, respectively, indicating high internal consistency. Test–retest results demonstrated excellent stability over time. In conclusion, the ECMO-SEPS is a valid and reliable instrument for objectively assessing ICU nurses’ self-efficacy in ECMO care. Its use may facilitate standardized evaluations and inform evidence-based education, workforce planning, and clinical practice in ECMO programs.

items.title: Anticoagulation after transcatheter and surgical bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement: A narrative review
items.abstract: Background Bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement, specifically surgical (SAVR) and transcatheter (TAVR), is among the most frequently performed cardiac interventions globally, yet anticoagulation strategies after implantation remain incompletely defined. Atrial fibrillation, notably prevalent pre- and post-operatively in these patients, substantially amplifies thromboembolic risk and complicates decision-making in an already elderly, frail, and comorbid population. Objectives To critically evaluate current anticoagulation strategies after bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement across sinus rhythm and atrial fibrillation in both SAVR and TAVR, and to identify evidence gaps and guideline inconsistencies. Methods We conducted a narrative review of major international guidelines (ESC/EACTS 2025, ACC/AHA 2020, and NICE 2021) and key clinical trials on antithrombotic therapy in valve replacement populations. Focus was placed on bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement, with mechanical and non-aortic valves excluded. Results Aspirin monotherapy is the most consistently supported strategy after bioprosthetic TAVR in sinus rhythm, though guidelines diverge on duration and recommendation strength. In atrial fibrillation, all three guidelines apply uniform CHA 2 DS 2 -VASc-based frameworks irrespective of AF phenotype, procedural context, or detection modality, reflecting lacking evidence rather than deliberate clinical judgement. No trial has enrolled patients specifically with new-onset post-procedural AF or stratified by AF subtype, and subclinical AF after bioprosthetic AVR remains entirely uncharacterised. Conclusions Guideline divergence reflects a structurally inadequate evidence base rather than genuine clinical equipoise. Individualised decisions informed by procedure type, AF phenotype, frailty, and bleeding risk are required to guide clinical practice, alongside an adequately powered stratified randomised trial incorporating mandatory continuous rhythm monitoring.

items.title: Di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) exposure during cardiopulmonary bypass: A narrative review of human clinical evidence and future directions
items.abstract: Background Di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) is widely used as a plasticizer in polyvinyl chloride medical devices employed during cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB). Although migration from these devices and blood-storage systems has long been recognized, the human clinical evidence remains limited and methodologically heterogeneous. Methods This narrative review used a structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Google Scholar from database inception through 23 August 2026. Original peer-reviewed human clinical studies measuring parent DEHP or its metabolites in blood, plasma, or urine among patients undergoing CPB were eligible for the primary synthesis. Relevant mechanistic, biomaterial, transfusion-medicine, guideline, and regulatory sources were used for context. Results The searches identified 237 database records; 33 duplicates were removed, and 204 unique records were screened. Thirteen full-text reports were assessed, and seven human clinical studies published between 1983 and 2025 were included. Across adult and pediatric settings, perioperative increases in parent DEHP and/or urinary or circulating metabolites were documented. The studies implicated multiple sources, including CPB components, blood-storage systems, and ancillary blood-contacting devices, but none provided complete patient-level source apportionment. DEHP-free tubing reduced, but did not eliminate, exposure. RBC washing reduced DEHP and MEHP in vitro, but a reduction in patient-level internal exposure has not been established. Conclusion Human clinical evidence consistently demonstrates internal exposure to DEHP or its metabolites during cardiac surgery involving CPB. However, small heterogeneous cohorts, variable analytes and sampling schedules, and limited outcome follow-up preclude causal inference regarding clinical harm. Prospective multicenter studies using standardized biomonitoring and source-apportionment methods are required.

items.title: Weight-stratified analysis of the heterogeneous effects of miniaturized cardiopulmonary bypass on perioperative outcomes in children with congenital heart disease: A retrospective cohort study
items.abstract: Introduction Miniaturized cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) circuits may reduce intraoperative transfusion in pediatric cardiac surgery, but their effects across body weight categories remain unclear. This study compared transfusion and outcomes between conventional and miniaturized CPB circuits, emphasizing weight-stratified analyses. Methods This retrospective study included 3,196 pediatric cardiac surgery patients (2015–2024) receiving conventional ( n = 548) or miniaturized ( n = 2,648) circuits. Primary outcomes were transfusion avoidance during CPB, in the ICU, and combined. Secondary outcomes included ICU length of stay, mechanical ventilation, ultrafast-track extubation, 24-h chest tube drainage (normalized to mL/kg), and hematocrit dynamics. Multivariable logistic regression and subgroup analyses were performed. Results Miniaturized circuits improved CPB transfusion avoidance overall (47.9% vs. 29.0%; P < 0.001), especially in children weighing 3–9 kg (all P < 0.01). ICU transfusion avoidance was lower with miniaturized circuits overall (82.1% vs. 94.5%; P < 0.001), except in the 1–2 kg subgroup. Combined avoidance was higher with miniaturized circuits across 3–9 and 12–13 kg (all P < 0.05). ICU length of stay was shorter with miniaturized circuits in most weight subgroups, whereas it was prolonged in the 2–3 kg subgroup (150 vs. 75 h; P < 0.001). Overall mean 24-h chest tube drainage was significantly lower in the miniaturized group (9.05 ± 9.10 vs. 10.82 ± 7.76 mL/kg; P < 0.001); however, stratified analysis showed a significant increase only in the 4–5 kg subgroup (14.52 ± 7.88 vs. 11.96 ± 6.69 mL/kg; P = 0.046), with no differences in other weight strata. Multivariable analysis indicated that miniaturized circuits were an independent predictor of increased ICU transfusion risk (OR 2.59; P < 0.001), whereas higher body weight was associated with reduced risk (OR 0.76 per kg; P < 0.001). Conclusions Miniaturized CPB circuits reduce intraoperative transfusion, particularly in children weighing 3–9 kg, but are associated with higher postoperative ICU transfusion and variable effects on chest tube drainage that are weight-dependent. The net benefit appears weight-dependent. These findings underscore the need for weight-stratified circuit selection, although further prospective studies are warranted.

items.title: Outcomes of preoperative intra-aortic balloon pump insertion in high-risk coronary artery bypass grafting: A decade of single-centre experience
items.abstract: Background The role of prophylactic preoperative intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) in patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) remains uncertain. This study aims to evaluate the safety and outcomes of preoperative IABP insertion in high-risk CABG patients. Methods A retrospective review of outcomes of patients who had preoperative IABP insertion undergoing isolated CABG at a single United Kingdom quaternary centre was conducted between January 2015 and June 2025. Indications for IABP insertion were divided into prophylactic (critical coronary anatomy) and non-prophylactic insertion (haemodynamic instability and persistent angina). Primary outcome was 30-day mortality, and secondary outcomes included 90-day mortality, incidence of postoperative complications, specific complications related to IABP insertion and postoperative length of stay. Comparative analysis was performed between the two groups. Kaplan-Meier survival analyses were performed. Results 610 patients underwent isolated CABG with preoperative IABP; 302 (49.5%) received prophylactic IABP and 308 (50.5%) had non-prophylactic insertion. There were 14 (2.3%) 30-day mortality and 20 (3.3%) 90-day mortality, with no significant difference in mortality between the two groups. Mean postoperative length of hospital stay was 11 ± 7 days; this was significantly longer in the non-prophylactic group (12 ± 8 vs 10 ± 7 days, p < 0.01). Postoperative neurological dysfunction occurred in 42 patients (6.9%) and dialysis in 5 (0.8%), with no differences between the two groups. There were 25 (4.1%) IABP-related complications; 8 localised haematoma managed conservatively, 4 wound infections treated with intravenous antibiotics, 5 lower limb ischaemia (3 required surgical re-vascularisation), 2 fatal bowel ischaemia, 2 renal and splenic malperfusion, 2 localised femoral artery dissection and 2 retroperitoneal haematoma (1 required emergency laparotomy). Conclusion This study supports the selective use of prophylactic IABP in patients undergoing high-risk CABG. In this selected cohort, preoperative IABP use was associated with low early mortality, favourable long-term survival and an acceptable complication profile.

items.title: Antithrombin III use in pediatric and neonatal ECMO: A systematic review and meta-analysis
items.abstract: Background Antithrombin (AT) supplementation has been increasingly incorporated into pediatric extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) anticoagulation protocols to address heparin resistance and optimize anticoagulation. However, considerable variability exists in monitoring practices, replacement strategies, and reported clinical outcomes. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate contemporary evidence regarding AT supplementation in pediatric ECMO. Methods A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science identified studies evaluating AT monitoring or supplementation during neonatal or pediatric ECMO through September 2025. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data on monitoring strategies, replacement protocols, anticoagulation parameters, thrombosis, bleeding, and mortality. Comparative studies reporting extractable dichotomous outcomes were included in random-effects meta-analyses. Results Twenty-five studies met inclusion criteria, consisting predominantly of retrospective single-center cohorts. Marked heterogeneity was observed in indications for supplementation, replacement thresholds (50-100%), therapeutic targets (60-120%), formulations, dosing strategies, and anticoagulation monitoring. AT supplementation consistently increased AT activity, improved anti-factor Xa measurements, and in several studies, reduced unfractionated heparin requirement. However, higher anti-Xa levels and increased AT activity did not consistently translate into improved clinical outcomes. Meta-analysis demonstrated no significant association between AT supplementation and thrombosis (OR 1.10, 95% 0.54-2.24), bleeding (OR 1.15, 95% CI 0.85-1.54), or mortality (OR 1.24, 95% CI 0.63-2.43). Pharmacokinetic investigations suggested standard dosing frequently underestimates replacement requirements in pediatric ECMO. Conclusion Current evidence supports the role of AT supplementation in improving laboratory markers of anticoagulation, but does not demonstrate consistent reductions in bleeding, thrombosis, or mortality. Wide variation in monitoring, dosing, and outcome definitions limits comparisons across studies. Future multicenter investigations should prioritize standardized definitions, age-specific therapeutic targets, and prospective evaluation of replacement strategies to better define the role of AT supplementation in pediatric ECMO.

items.title: Optimal timing of surgical intervention for post-myocardial infarction ventricular septal rupture: A comprehensive evidence review
items.abstract: Background Ventricular septal rupture (VSR) is a rare but devastating complication of acute myocardial infarction, historically associated with extremely high mortality rates. The optimal timing of surgical repair-balancing the risks of operating on friable, acute necrosis against the dangers of progressive cardiogenic shock during a waiting period-remains a central clinical dilemma. Methods A systematic narrative review was conducted following PRISMA guidelines. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane Library databases were searched from 2000 to 2024 for studies comparing early (≤7 days) versus delayed (>7 days) surgical repair of post-MI VSR. Data were extracted on patient characteristics, mechanical circulatory support (MCS) use, surgical techniques, and clinical outcomes, including operative mortality, reoperation rates, and long-term survival. Results Evidence from contemporary observational studies confirms that delayed surgical repair is associated with significantly lower operative mortality compared to early repair, primarily due to superior tissue integrity and lower rates of residual shunt. However, this mortality gap has substantially narrowed in the contemporary era with routine use of advanced MCS, particularly veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) and Impella devices. These technologies enable hemodynamic stabilization, transforming early repair from a salvage procedure to a more controlled intervention. Modern management has evolved from a rigid temporal dichotomy to a patient-tailored strategy emphasizing immediate stabilization, risk stratification, and selective MCS bridging to the optimal surgical window. Conclusion While delayed repair remains preferred for hemodynamically stable patients, early repair supported by advanced MCS represents a viable and often necessary strategy for patients with refractory shock. The decision paradigm has shifted toward “stabilize, support, then repair,” requiring multidisciplinary heart team collaboration. Future directions include standardized MCS protocols, validated risk scores, and exploration of hybrid percutaneous-surgical approaches to further improve outcomes for this high-risk population.

items.title: Effects of patient demographic and clinical data on the assessment of cerebral oxygen monitoring values during coronary artery bypass grafting
items.abstract: Objectives To determine the effects of patient demographic and clinical data on regional cerebral oxygen saturation (rSO2) values. Design Prospective observational study. Setting Training and research hospital. Participants Eighty patients who were scheduled for elective on-pump coronary artery bypass grafting. Interventions Near-infrared spectroscopy was used to monitor bilateral brain oxygen saturation at twelve time points (T1–T12). Measurements and main results The right and left rSO2 values showed a ≥20% decrease pattern from T3 to T12. Patients with a ≥20% decline in the right rSO2 were older and had a higher baseline mean arterial pressure (MAP) and longer cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) times. Patients with a ≥20% decline in the left rSO2 had a higher baseline MAP. Age, baseline MAP, female sex and CPB time for the right rSO2 and baseline MAP values and female sex for the left rSO2 values were positively associated with a ≥20% decline in univariate logistic regression analyses. Baseline MAP and CPB time for the right rSO2 values and baseline MAP for the left rSO2 values retained their statistical significance in multivariate logistic regression analyses. Activated clotting time (ACT) showed a statistically significant and inverse relationship with the left rSO2 values. Conclusions Higher baseline MAP values for right and left rSO2 values and longer CPB times for right rSO2 values were independently associated with a ≥20% decline. ACT was inversely associated with a ≥20% decline in the left rSO2 values. Univariate analysis revealed that older age and female sex were associated with a ≥20% decline in rSO2values. Clinical trial number The study was registered at Clinicaltrials.gov (NCT07228546).

items.title: Standardizing cardiopulmonary bypass management for left ventricular assist device implantation: A clinical framework and checklist
items.abstract: Background Patients undergoing left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation often present with end-stage heart failure, severe pulmonary hypertension, and systemic inflammation. During this procedure, cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) acts as a double-edged sword: it provides essential life support but can exacerbate right ventricular (RV) dysfunction and trigger severe vasoplegia. Despite the critical nature of the transition from CPB to mechanical support, there is a lack of standardized, phase-specific CPB management protocols. Methods Based on current guidelines, frontline perfusion experience, and an interdisciplinary approach integrating mechanical engineering principles with surgical practice, a comprehensive clinical framework for CPB management was developed. The protocol deconstructs the procedure into four distinct phases: pre-bypass assessment, on-bypass management, weaning, and post-bypass care. Results A four-stage standardized checklist and an intraoperative emergency quick reference card were created to facilitate clinical translation. Key interventions include identifying anatomical “minefields,” maintaining a golden balance of hemodilution, executing a dynamic flow-speed handover to prevent suction events, and managing hemodynamics cautiously during protamine administration to mitigate RV dysfunction. Conclusions Standardizing CPB management during LVAD implantation provides a practical tool to optimize hemodynamic stability and improve perioperative safety.

items.title: Lunar phases, meteorological conditions, astrological signs, and postoperative outcomes of acute type A aortic dissection: Results of a retrospective cohort study
items.abstract: Background Acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) is a surgical emergency associated with high mortality. While patient-related risk factors are well-established, beliefs persist regarding the influence of lunar phases, meteorological conditions, and astrological signs on disease occurrence and outcomes. Methods We retrospectively analysed all patients who underwent emergency surgery for ATAAD at Bordeaux University Hospital between 1996 and 2020. The primary objective was to assess the association between environmental factors (lunar phases, atmospheric pressure, temperature, and astrological signs) and ATAAD incidence. Secondary objectives included assessing their association with 30-day mortality and postoperative morbidity (intensive care unit length of stay, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation use, and mesenteric infarction). Meteorological data were available for 603 patients from 2010 onward. Results Among 920 patients (70% male; mean age 63 ± 13 years), the 30-day mortality rate was 9.7%. Lunar phases were not associated with ATAAD incidence (first quarter 26%, last quarter 25%, new moon 25%, full moon 24%; p = 0.91), mortality, or complications. Atmospheric pressure showed no association with ATAAD occurrence or outcomes. Temperature showed a weak correlation with ATAAD incidence (r = 0.11, p = 0.01), but not with mortality. Astrological signs were not associated with ATAAD incidence, mortality, or morbidity. Longer cardiopulmonary bypass duration (odds ratio [OR] = 0.994 per minute; p = 0.01) and diabetes (OR = 4.63; p = 0.01) were associated with 30-day mortality. Conclusions Environmental factors were not associated with ATAAD incidence or outcomes. Established clinical factors remain the primary determinants of mortality.

items.title: Impact of hypothermia level on neurological and renal outcomes in emergency aortic surgery: a single-centre experience
items.abstract: Background Temperature management during emergency surgery for acute aortic syndrome is critical for neurological, renal, and systemic protection. Recent European Association for Cardio-Thoracic Surgery (EACTS) guidelines recommend moderate hypothermia with antegrade cerebral perfusion for hemiarch procedures. Nevertheless, deep hypothermic circulatory arrest (DHCA) remains common. This study evaluates neurological and other postoperative outcomes across different intraoperative temperature ranges. Methods A single-centre retrospective study of consecutive patients undergoing surgery for acute aortic syndrome between 2018–2023. Demographic, intraoperative, and postoperative data on mortality, hospitalization, neurological, renal outcomes, and blood product usage were collected. Patients were stratified by intraoperative temperature: deep (≤20°C), low-moderate (20.1–24°C), high-moderate (24.1–28°C), and mild (>28°C) hypothermia. Logistic regression identified predictors of binary adverse outcomes. A sensitivity analysis was conducted using 24.0°C as the threshold in hemiarch surgery patients. Results A total of 175 patients (median age 64 years; 37% female) were included; of whom 89% underwent hemiarch replacement. Cardiopulmonary bypass duration decreased progressively with warmer intraoperative temperatures, ranging from 270.5 minutes in deep hypothermia to 164 minutes in mild hypothermia. The 30-day mortality was 18.9% ( n = 33/175), and the overall stroke rate was 19.4% ( n = 34/175). Among patients undergoing hemiarch repair, warmer temperatures were associated with lower stroke incidence (mild hypothermia 11%) compared with high-moderate (8.8%), low-moderate (26%), and deep hypothermia (27%) ( p = 0.049), and with shorter intensive care admission ( p = 0.036). However, multivariate regression showed that the four-category comparison did not reach significance for the assessed outcomes once adjusted for confounding variables. A sensitivity analysis at 24.0°C showed an independent association with reduced stroke risk (OR 0.23, 95% CI 0.08-0.64, p = 0.005). Discussion Our findings support current EACTS recommendations favouring moderate-to-mild hypothermia for hemiarch replacement, with potential protective effects. Further studies should determine the optimal temperature strategy for patients undergoing total arch replacement.

items.title: Interpreting persistent vasopressor dependence during VA ECMO weaning
Comparing hemolysis among extracorporeal pumps: A large-scale retrospective study
items.abstract: Background Hemolysis is a frequent and clinically relevant complication during extracorporeal life support (ECLS, or ECMO), associated with acute kidney injury, systemic inflammation, and increased mortality. Direct comparisons between pumps regarding hemolysis are limited. This study evaluated and compared hemolysis profiles among several devices in clinical practice. Methods We conducted a retrospective, single-center cohort study adult patients who received veno-arterial (V-A) or veno-venous (V-V) ECMO between January 2020 and December 2023 ( N = 230). Patients were categorized by one of four ECMO pump types, and hemolysis was assessed using lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) and plasma-free hemoglobin (pfHb) as primary markers. Multivariable linear mixed-effects models were used to analyze associations between pump type and hemolysis, adjusting for several covariates including revolutions per minute (RPM), hematologic indices, ECMO mode, and severity scores. Results Partial thromboplastin time ( p < 0.005), hemoglobin ( p < 0.001), and use of continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT, p < 0.001) were positively correlated with both LDH and pfHb concentrations and hemolysis, while fibrinogen ( p < 0.03) was inversely correlated. Without RPM adjustment, NovaLung exhibited the highest LDH (680.3 U/L) and pfHb (29.4 mg/dL), followed by the Cardiohelp, Rotaflow, and CentriMag. In the RPM-adjusted analysis, LDH was highest in Cardiohelp (737.4 U/L), followed by the Rotaflow, CentriMag, and NovaLung; whereas pfHb was highest in Cardiohelp (25.8 mg/dL), followed by the Rotaflow, NovaLung, and CentriMag. Conclusions This study provides a clinical associations of the safety and performance of four centrifugal pumps in real-world ECMO practice in adults. We demonstrate that pump-specific RPM may be potentially correlated with hemolysis during ECMO in clinical practice, illustrating that the diagonal pump, which operated at the highest RPMs, was associated with the highest hemolysis in models without the RPM adjustment. Future studies are warranted to further clarify the impact of hemolysis on outcomes.

items.title: Prominent V Waves Augment Right Ventricular Afterload Independent of the Lung Vessels in Heart Failure: Implications for Clinical Assessment of Pulmonary Vascular Disease
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Left atrial (LA) stiffening augments the LA V wave, pressurizing the pulmonary artery (PA) out of proportion to left ventricular end-diastolic pressure. We characterized the pathophysiologic, diagnostic, and clinical implications of LA stiffening, as defined by prominent V waves, in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and less than moderate mitral regurgitation at rest underwent invasive hemodynamic exercise testing. Patients with heightened operant LA stiffening were defined by the PA wedge pressure (PAWP) V wave exceeding mean PAWP by ≥10 mm Hg. A previously used formula for V wave–corrected PAWP was validated against the PAWP waveform pressure-time-area to explore impact of the V wave on transpulmonary pressure gradients. Clinical, echocardiographic, hemodynamic, and outcome data were compared for patients with and without prominent V waves. RESULTS: Compared with patients without prominent V waves (n=844, 79%), those with prominent V waves (n=225, 21%) were older and more likely to be women, with more severe LA myopathy, evidenced by greater LA volume index (42.2±15.0 versus 32.5±13.0 mL/m 2 , P <0.001), lower LA reservoir strain (16.4±7.5% versus 23.2±8.3%, P <0.001), more atrial fibrillation (61.3% versus 22.9%, P <0.001), and increased operant LA reservoir stiffness (0.59±0.25 versus 0.23±0.24 mm Hg/mL, P <0.001). Patients with prominent V waves had markedly higher PA systolic pressure than those without (54±16 versus 38±12 mm Hg, P <0.001) despite no difference in end-diastolic PAWP-PA pressure gradient (3±5 versus 3±4 mm Hg, P =0.950). Incorporating the V wave into PAWP improved correlation between directly measured PAWP pressure-time integral compared with mid–A wave PAWP (R 2 =0.96 versus R 2 =0.86, P <0.001 for comparison). In patients with prominent V waves, the prevalence of combined pre- and postcapillary pulmonary hypertension decreased from 60.2% to 29.3% after V wave correction for the transpulmonary pressure gradients. Despite similar corrected pulmonary vascular resistances in patients with and without prominent V waves, apparent PA compliance was much lower in patients with prominent V waves (3.03±1.56 versus 4.90±2.27 mL/mm Hg, P <0.001), augmenting right ventricular afterload, and these changes were coupled with more severe right ventricular dysfunction, tricuspid regurgitation, blunted cardiopulmonary exercise reserve, and increased risk of hospitalization for heart failure or death in patients with versus without prominent V waves (adjusted hazard ratio, 2.09 [95% CI, 1.53–2.86]; P <0.001). CONCLUSIONS: More than 1 in 5 patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction display prominent V waves in excess of end-diastolic PAWP. This augments right ventricular afterload due to backward transmission of the V wave, contributing to right heart failure that is independent of the pulmonary vasculature. Failure to account for the V wave during hemodynamic assessment overestimates the severity of pulmonary vascular disease present.

items.title: Clarifying the Clinical Relevance of V Waves
Correction to: Infective Endocarditis: Diagnosis, Antibiotic Therapy, and Management: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association
Cardiovascular Complications of Chronic Liver Disease
items.abstract: Chronic liver disease is an increasingly prevalent and heterogeneous syndrome with important consequences for cardiovascular function. As the global burdens of chronic liver disease and cirrhosis continue to rise, cardiovascular disease has emerged as a major driver of overall morbidity and mortality in affected patients. Despite the growing recognition of the intersectionality between hepatology and cardiology care clinically, cardiovascular disease risk among patients with liver disease is underrecognized. This state-of-the-art review summarizes the current understanding of the bidirectional interactions between the liver and the cardiovascular system. Shared mechanisms—including inflammation, endothelial injury, and neurohormonal overactivation—that contribute to the development of adverse myocardial remodeling, atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, heart failure, arrhythmias, pulmonary vascular syndromes, and cirrhosis-associated cardiovascular syndromes are reviewed. A specific focus is placed on metabolic dysfunction–associated steatotic liver disease, the most common form of chronic liver disease, while highlighting the distinct cardiovascular manifestations associated with other types of chronic liver disease. These include alcohol-associated liver disease and infiltrative diseases that affect the liver and heart with cardiovascular implications across the spectrum from early stages of liver disease through cirrhosis. We discuss practical approaches to detecting liver disease, including the assessment of liver fibrosis noninvasively in individuals at risk. We discuss the approach to assessing cardiovascular risk through cardiac imaging, biomarkers, and cardiac functional testing once chronic liver disease is detected. Management considerations for commonly encountered cardiovascular conditions and a critical appraisal of the evolving evidence supporting cardiometabolic therapies in patients with chronic liver disease are discussed to underscore potential cardiovascular and liver benefits. Critical evidence gaps and future research priorities are identified, including the development and evaluation of liver-informed cardiovascular risk models, incorporation of cardiovascular end points into liver disease trials, and implementation of integrated cardiohepatometabolic care pathways. Improved recognition of chronic liver disease and related cardiovascular disease risk represents a major opportunity to facilitate earlier disease detection, enhance risk stratification, and improve outcomes across the spectrum of chronic liver disease.

items.title: Letter by Khouri et al Regarding Article, “CXCR6+ T Cells Drive Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Myocarditis”
The Amyloid Atrium: A Distinct Phenotype Demanding a Distinct Paradigm
Approach to Heart Failure With Mildly Reduced Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction
Trends and Distribution of Low-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol Levels Among US Adults and Adolescents Without Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease, 1999 to 2023
Prevalence, Predictors, and Clinical Implications of Residual Shunt After Patent Foramen Ovale Percutaneous Closure
Response by Munir et al to Letter Regarding Article, “CXCR6 + T Cells Drive Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Myocarditis”
Under Pressure: Right Ventricular Obstruction by Pericardial Cyst
Molecular Imaging of Thrombotic Sources of Ischemic Stroke
Dual Control of Low-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol Levels by ANGPTL3 and ANGPTL8
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Inactivation of ANGPTL3 (angiopoietin-like protein 3; A3) is a proven therapeutic strategy for lowering plasma lipid levels independently of the low-density lipoprotein receptor, yet the optimal approach to inactivate A3 remains unclear. A3 is proteolytically cleaved and circulates as full-length, N-terminal, and C-terminal fragments. The specific contribution of each form of A3, and of its paralog, ANGPTL8 (angiopoietin-like protein 8; A8), in modulating circulating levels of ApoB (apolipoprotein B)–containing lipoproteins remain poorly defined. Clarifying these relationships will inform next-generation A3-directed therapies. METHODS: We performed liver perfusion studies to directly compare the number and composition of very-low-density lipoprotein particles secreted from mice with and without A3. To amplify effects on cholesterol metabolism, we generated Ldlr −/− mice expressing wild-type A3, full-length A3, or N-terminal A3 fragments, with or without coexpression of A8, and analyzed plasma lipids, circulating A3 and A8 complexes, and intravascular lipase activities. Complementary in vitro assays and structural modeling were used to assess relative endothelial lipase inhibition by A3 alone or in complex with A8. RESULTS: Liver perfusion studies revealed that A3 inactivation does not alter the rates of hepatic secretion of very-low-density lipoprotein in wild-type or Ldlr −/− mice. Inactivation of A8 alone lowered plasma low-density lipoprotein cholesterol levels by ≈20%, an effect dependent upon the expression of both endothelial lipase and A3. Maximal inhibition of lipoprotein lipase required coexpression of A8 plus both full-length A3 and N-terminal A3 fragments, indicating that A3 cleavage, in addition to A8 expression, is essential for maximal lipoprotein lipase inhibition. In contrast, A8 expression, but not A3 cleavage, was required for optimal endothelial lipase inhibition. CONCLUSIONS: A8 acts in concert with A3 to differentially modulate lipoprotein lipase– and endothelial lipase–mediated lipolysis, which antagonizes hepatic clearance of newly secreted atherogenic ApoB–containing lipoproteins. This mechanistic framework refines our understanding of A3-targeted lipid lowering and highlights the therapeutic potential of dual A3- plus A8-directed strategies to treat dyslipidemia and prevent atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.

items.title: Bleeding With Asundexian Versus Placebo in Patients With Noncardioembolic Ischemic Stroke or High-Risk TIA: OCEANIC-STROKE Randomized Trial
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: OCEANIC-STROKE (XXX) showed that asundexian added to antiplatelet therapy reduced ischemic stroke without significantly increasing bleeding in patients with noncardioembolic ischemic stroke or high-risk transient ischemic attack. We characterized bleeding categories, sites, and key subgroups. METHODS: In the safety population, 12 254 participants received at least 1 dose of asundexian (n=6124) or placebo (n=6130). Bleeding was categorized by International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis criteria as major, clinically relevant nonmajor (CRNM), or minor. While-on-treatment analyses included events through 2 days after the last dose, with death and permanent discontinuation as competing risks. RESULTS: Major bleeding occurred in 117 (1.9%) participants with asundexian and 107 (1.7%) with placebo (cause-specific hazard ratio [csHR], 1.10 [95% CI, 0.85–1.44]; P =0.46). Major or CRNM bleeding occurred in 339 (5.5%) and 307 (5.0%), respectively (csHR, 1.12 [95% CI, 0.96–1.30]; P =0.16), and any bleeding in 763 (12.5%) and 752 (12.3%) (csHR, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.93–1.13]; P =0.65). Treatment effects for major and major or CRNM bleeding were consistent across prespecified subgroups, including planned dual antiplatelet therapy. Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 41 (0.7%) and 36 (0.6%) participants. Any gastrointestinal bleeding occurred in 186 (3.0%) and 147 (2.4%) (csHR, 1.28 [95% CI, 1.03–1.59]), and lower gastrointestinal bleeding in 102 (1.7%) and 59 (1.0%) (csHR, 1.75 [95% CI, 1.27–2.41]), primarily rectal bleeding. Any procedure-related bleeding and any mucosal bleeding did not differ significantly. CONCLUSIONS: Asundexian added to antiplatelet therapy reduced ischemic stroke without significantly increasing major, major or CRNM, or any bleeding. Lower gastrointestinal bleeding was more frequent with asundexian, whereas treatment effects on major and major or CRNM bleeding were consistent across prespecified subgroups. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov ; Unique Identifier: NCT05686070.

items.title: Multidisciplinary Approach to Antiplatelet Management in Coronary Syndromes: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association
items.abstract: Antiplatelet therapy is a cornerstone of care for patients with acute coronary syndrome and chronic coronary disease, yet its optimal use requires careful balancing of thrombotic risk reduction with bleeding complications. Since the mid-2000s, advances in stent technology, antiplatelet pharmacotherapy, procedural technique, and risk stratification tools have led to increasingly individualized approaches to antiplatelet management. Current guidelines and evidence emphasize tailoring agent selection, intensity, and duration of therapy according to patient-, procedure-, and disease-specific factors rather than a uniform strategy. However, the growing complexity of evidence, frequent care transitions, social determinants of health, and variability in patient characteristics have increased the risk of inappropriate prescribing, nonadherence, and adverse outcomes. This scientific statement reviews contemporary evidence informing antiplatelet strategies and highlights the critical role of the multidisciplinary cardiovascular team (interventional cardiology, general cardiology, pharmacists, advanced practice nurses) and the importance of their collective expertise in ensuring antithrombotic stewardship in patients with acute coronary syndrome and chronic coronary disease.

items.title: Definition and Prognosis of Mitral Regurgitation in Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy: A Multicenter International Cohort Study
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: In transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy, mitral regurgitation (MR) severity may be underestimated by conventional (semi-)quantitative echocardiographic criteria due to restrictive low-flow hemodynamics. We sought to define and validate disease-specific MR risk thresholds and compare their prognostic performance with guideline definitions. METHODS: In a multicenter cohort study (8 centers, 4 countries), 1101 patients with newly diagnosed transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (derivation, n=722; validation, n=379) underwent standardized echocardiography with blinded core laboratory analysis, including MR measures (vena contracta width, effective regurgitant orifice area, regurgitant volume, and regurgitant fraction). All-cause mortality and time to first heart failure hospitalization (HFH) served as end points. Prognostic thresholds were derived from spline analysis, validated externally, and compared with American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology, European Society of Cardiology/European Association for Cardiothoracic Surgery, and American Society of Echocardiography definitions. RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 24.9 months (interquartile range, 12.0–42.0), 314 patients (28.5%) died and 244 (22.2%) experienced HFH. All MR metrics independently predicted mortality and HFH (all P <0.05). Spline-derived thresholds identified intermediate risk at vena contracta width ≥3.0 mm, effective regurgitant orifice area ≥0.10 cm 2 , regurgitant volume ≥15 mL, and regurgitant fraction ≥20% and high risk at effective regurgitant orifice area >0.25 cm 2 , regurgitant volume >38 mL, and regurgitant fraction >35%. Compared with guideline grading (≈12%–13%), the composite MR grading scheme classified a significantly higher proportion (21%) as severe MR and provided superior discrimination for clinical outcomes at 12 and 24 months in both the derivation and validation cohort. After multivariable adjustment, only the composite MR grading scheme remained strongly predictive for both mortality (hazard ratio, 1.20 [1.07–1.36]) and HFH (hazard ratio, 1.21 [1.05–1.38]). CONCLUSIONS: Quantitative MR thresholds in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy are substantially lower than current guideline cutoffs. A validated, risk-based composite MR grading scheme improves prediction of both mortality and HFH, better reflecting the restrictive low-flow pathophysiology of transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy and supporting disease-specific MR grading. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov ; Unique identifier: NCT06836011.

items.title: Correction to: Development and Validation of the American Heart Association’s PREVENT Equations

ICare-FASTER (Improving Care by Faster Risk Stratification Through Use of High-Sensitivity Point-of-Care Troponin in Patients Presenting With Possible Acute Coronary Syndrome in the Emergency Department): A Stepped-Wedge Cluster-Randomized Trial
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Point-of-care high-sensitivity cTn (cardiac troponin; hs-cTn) testing has the potential to expedite decision-making and reduce emergency department (ED) length of stay for patients presenting with possible myocardial infarction by ensuring that results are consistently available when sought by clinicians. We assessed the real-life effectiveness and safety of implementing point-of-care hs-cTn testing in the ED. METHODS: We conducted a pragmatic, stepped-wedge cluster-randomized trial. The control arm was usual care with an accelerated diagnostic pathway using a single-sample rule-out step with a central laboratory hs-cTn assay. The intervention arm used the same pathway with a point-of-care hs-cTnI assay. The primary effectiveness outcome was ED length of stay assessed using a generalized linear mixed model. The safety outcome was myocardial infarction or cardiac death within 30 days. RESULTS: Six sites participated, with 59 980 ED presentations (44 747 individuals; mean 61±19 years of age; 49.5% female) from February 2023 through January 2025; 31 392 presentations were during the intervention arm. After adjustment for covariates associated with length of stay, the intervention reduced length of stay by 13% (95% CI, 9%–16%; P <0.001), corresponding to a reduction of 47 minutes (95% CI, 33–61 minutes) from a mean length of stay in the control arm of 376 minutes. The 30-day myocardial infarction or cardiac death rate was similar in the control and intervention arms (0.39% and 0.39%, respectively; P =0.54). CONCLUSIONS: Implementation of whole-blood hs-cTnI testing at the point of care into an accelerated diagnostic pathway was safe and reduced length of stay in the ED compared with laboratory testing. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.anzctr.org.au ; Unique identifier: ACTRN12619001189112.

items.title: Opportunistic Screening for Chagas Disease Using an Artificial Intelligence–Enabled ECG: Prospective Evaluation of Feasibility and Diagnostic Accuracy
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Chagas disease (ChD), a neglected cardiovascular condition, affects 7.5 to 10.5 million people worldwide. Opportunistic screening during routine electrocardiography may allow earlier detection of unrecognized infections, enabling timely antiparasitic therapy or optimized cardiac care. This study prospectively evaluated the feasibility and diagnostic accuracy of an artificial intelligence (AI)–enabled ECG model enriched with 3 epidemiological questions (AI-ECG-EPI model) as an opportunistic screening for ChD in endemic regions of Brazil. METHODS: We conducted a prospective study embedded in the Telehealth Network of Minas Gerais, Brazil, across 107 municipalities in hyperendemic and endemic regions. From October 2023 to September 2024, adults undergoing routine tele-ECGs were eligible. The primary exposure was the output of the AI-ECG-EPI model: all positive individuals and a 3:1 sample of negative individuals were invited for serology (index test–dependent sampling), the reference standard. Weighted analyses (inverse probability) accounted for this sampling design. Diagnostic metrics included sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, likelihood ratios, area under the receiver operating characteristics curve, and area under the precision recall curve. The AI-ECG-EPI model was compared with both an epidemiological questions model and an AI ECG–only model. RESULTS: Among 75 779 eligible ECGs, the AI-ECG-EPI model was available for 59 154 individuals; 6812 (11.5%) screened positive. A total of 7804 selected were invited for serology, and 3509 completed testing (2517 positive; 992 negative). ChD was confirmed in 36.8% of positive and 9.3% of negative individuals. The weighted prevalence of ChD was 12.2%. Sensitivity was 34.3%, specificity 91.6%, harmonic mean of precision and recall score 0.52, and diagnostic odds ratio 5.69. The AI-ECG-EPI model showed higher discrimination than both the epidemiological questions model and AI ECG–only model (area under the receiver operating characteristics curve, 77.6% versus 70.0% and 64.5%, respectively; P <0.001). Precision recall curves showed higher precision across most recall levels. Exploratory analysis suggested improved risk reclassification (net reclassification improvement, 0.503). Performance was higher in women and in individuals with Chagas cardiomyopathy. CONCLUSIONS: In this community-based study, an AI-ECG-EPI model integrated into a public telecardiology network enabled feasible opportunistic screening for ChD in primary care. It showed acceptable diagnostic accuracy, with higher discrimination than epidemiological questions and AI ECG–only models, and identified many previously undiagnosed patients in endemic regions, supporting its potential role in scalable screening strategies. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov ; Unique identifier: NCT02646943.

items.title: Correction to: Abstract 4365705: Cardiology Medications and Medicare Spending: Opportunities for Savings Using Mark Cuban Cost Plus Drug Company and Costco Member Prescription Program Pricing
Radiation Vasculopathy of the Coronary Arteries: State-of-the Art Review
items.abstract: Radiation-associated coronary artery disease (RACAD) is a distinct form of coronary artery disease with several specific biological and clinical aspects as well as key knowledge gaps. RACAD is prevalent in patients with cardiac exposure to radiotherapy. As radiotherapy is integral to the effective treatment of many thoracic malignancies, improved long-term survivorship is coupled with increased risk for RACAD. Ionizing radiation induces free radical generation and activation of proinflammatory cascades, leading to endothelial dysfunction and accelerated atherosclerosis. Risks for RACAD are determined both by radiotherapy, including the radiation dose and the proximity of coronary arteries to the radiotherapy field, and by patient-specific factors, such as younger age, higher baseline cardiovascular risk, and concurrent cardiotoxic systemic therapies. Importantly, radiotherapy delivery is highly individualized on the basis of tumor location and treatment strategy, resulting in heterogeneous coronary exposure to radiation and patient-to-patient variability. Clinical presentation may occur early, within 1 to 2 years, especially in patients with higher cardiac radiation doses (eg, lung or esophageal cancer), or after a latency period of 5 to 20 years with lower cardiac dose radiation exposure (eg, left-sided breast cancer). Patients generally present with symptoms similar to conventional coronary artery disease. However, RACAD symptoms may be underrecognized in cancer survivors due to overlapping treatment-related fatigue, pulmonary disease, or competing oncologic symptoms. Diagnosis and management generally follow standard coronary artery disease guidelines while incorporating cancer-specific considerations, such as planned oncologic surgeries, bleeding risk, postradiotherapy complications such as atretic internal mammary arteries, and cardiotoxic effects of systemic cancer therapies. Primary prevention of RACAD is critical, emphasizing advances in precision radiotherapy, including delivery techniques with improved coronary dosimetry, and cardiac shielding. Key knowledge gaps include understanding long-term outcomes with contemporary 3-dimensional conformal radiotherapy techniques, validated cancer-specific risk prediction models on the basis of coronary dosimetry, optimal surveillance protocols, targeted molecular pharmacotherapies, and risk analysis of percutaneous versus surgical management of RACAD. Prospective studies are needed to develop cancer- and dosimetry-specific risk calculators, validating cardioprotective interventions, and improving multidisciplinary cardio-oncology collaboration to optimize early detection of RACAD and timely intervention in the growing population of cancer survivors.

items.title: Multimodal KCNQ1 Variant-Effect Maps Define Ion Channel Mechanisms and Disease Risk
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Variants in the ion channel gene KCNQ1 are the leading cause of congenital long QT syndrome (LQTS), a disorder characterized by QT prolongation and risk of fatal arrhythmias. The expanding use of genetic testing has led to the identification of numerous variants of uncertain significance, complicating clinical interpretation and risk stratification. Functional characterization of KCNQ1 variants is essential to define their role in long QT syndrome and advance precision medicine in cardiovascular care. METHODS: We generated a nearly comprehensive variant library of 13 403 protein-coding variants in KCNQ1 . Using 4 pooled assays followed by high-throughput sequencing, we characterized the variants’ effects on cell surface abundance and channel function in both the variant-only and heterozygous states. Case–control analyses and data from large-scale biobanks were used to assess the clinical impact of loss-of-function variants on QT prolongation and long QT syndrome. Heterozygous assay results were used to determine dominant-negative effects, which were also evaluated for association with arrhythmia risk. Protein structural clustering of distinct classes of deleterious variants was analyzed. RESULTS: Across the 4 assays, we generated 49 305 functional measurements of KCNQ1 variants. Of the 13 403 KCNQ1 studied variants, 1757 demonstrated strong pathogenic evidence, and 6660 showed moderate benign evidence. Loss-of-function variants were significantly associated with QT prolongation and long QT syndrome in case–control and biobank analyses. Deleterious variants clustered within distinct structural domains based on their functional classification. A majority of pathogenic variants exhibited dominant-negative effects; these variants were linked to a higher risk of arrhythmia diagnoses than were haploinsufficient variants. CONCLUSIONS: This comprehensive KCNQ1 functional atlas provides novel functional evidence for most KCNQ1 variants of uncertain significance. It also reveals mechanistic principles linking genetic variation to ion channel biology and arrhythmia susceptibility, advancing cardiovascular precision medicine.

items.title: Multidisciplinary Collaboration in the Performance of Aortic Surgery: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association
items.abstract: Intraoperative management of a patient undergoing cardiac surgery requires continuous and independent interventions by multiple healthcare professionals, including surgeons, anesthesiologists, and perfusionists, among others. Although each clinician performs tasks based on their training and accepted techniques, guidelines, and protocols, an action by one member of the team can have immediate consequences for other team members. Aortic surgery adds a level of complexity, with the need for interventions such as single-lung ventilation, systemic cooling (and subsequent rewarming), and myocardial, cerebral, and visceral protection. Much has been made of the utility of the multidisciplinary team. This scientific statement is intended to approach the patient undergoing aortic surgery from 3 different viewpoints: that of the surgeon, the anesthesiologist, and the perfusionist. This scientific statement is not intended to provide an exhaustive summary of approaches to aortic surgery but rather to illustrate the specific concerns that each member of the team may have.

items.title: Mainstreaming Cardiovascular Care for Women: From Special Population to Standard Practice

A Female-Specific Life Course Approach to the Prevention and Management of Cardiovascular Disease: A Presidential Advisory From the American Heart Association, American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine
items.abstract: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in women, contributes markedly to healthcare expenditures, and is projected to increase substantially by 2050 if current trends continue. There is growing recognition of the complex role of sex as a biologic variable and its influence on cardiovascular health and disease. However, cardiovascular risk remains underrecognized and underaddressed in girls and women, particularly as it relates to female-specific exposure to sex hormones (both endogenous and exogenous), which are systemic modulators of cardiovascular biology. Moreover, girls and women uniquely experience fragmented care spanning specialties, including pediatrics, adolescent medicine, primary care, obstetrics and gynecology, maternal-fetal medicine, cardiology, endocrinology, hematology, and neurology. Consequently, there is a need for a unified life course approach that addresses the female-specific interconnectedness of hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health. To address these gaps, the American Heart Association, in collaboration with the American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine, established a Female Life Stage framework to optimize the prevention and management of cardiovascular disease in girls and women. Physiologic changes in sex hormones define clinically distinct life stages (ie, perimenarche, ovarian cycling, perimenopause, postmenopause), which directly inform female-specific considerations for screening, prevention, and management of cardiovascular disease. This presidential advisory details the framework and its scientific rationale, highlights opportunities for implementation across settings, and identifies priorities for research, clinician education, patient advocacy, and policy. This framework offers a transformative opportunity to equitably improve cardiovascular health for all girls and women.

items.title: Consensus Guidance for the Female-Specific Prevention and Management of Cardiovascular Disease: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association, American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine
items.abstract: There is growing recognition that the optimal prevention and management of cardiovascular disease in girls and women requires attention to sex-specific considerations relevant to the interconnected domains of hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health across the life course. Dysregulation in these health domains tends to co-occur and is associated with increased risk of cardiovascular disease. However, healthcare for girls and women is uniquely fragmented across clinical specialties, including pediatrics, adolescent medicine, primary care, obstetrics, maternal-fetal medicine, gynecology, cardiology, endocrinology, hematology, and neurology. Furthermore, inconsistent alignment across society guidelines contributes to missed opportunities to optimize cardiovascular health. Therefore, the American Heart Association, American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine convened a multisociety science advisory group and developed the Female Life Stage construct. This construct defines 4 distinct and clinically meaningful stages—perimenarche (S1), ovarian cycling (S2), perimenopause (S3), and postmenopause (S4)—to enable female-specific screening, prevention, and treatment considerations. In addition, this construct incorporates pregnancy as a unique modifying life event when cardiovascular risk may emerge or be unmasked (eg, adverse pregnancy outcomes). This scientific statement crosswalks major society guidelines, synthesizes the evidence, and provides consensus-based clinical guidance for each Female Life Stage and interconnected health domain (ie, hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health). We conclude with a call to action to improve clinical workflows, enhance clinician education, and address scientific and implementation gaps to improve cardiovascular health in girls and women.

items.title: One Life Course, Many Specialties: Building a System for Cardiovascular Health in Girls and Women
items.abstract: ardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death in women and men, yet women remain underrepresented in clinical trials, remain undertreated, and often experience worse outcomes.Their hormonal, physiological, psychosocial, and therapeutic risks require tailored care.The 3 multispecialty publications in this issue of Circulation describe women's cardiovascular life course, guide prevention and management, and examine women's cardiovascular disease centers.Together, they establish a scientific foundation for reorganizing care around women throughout their lives.

items.title: Women’s Cardiovascular Health: From Recognition to Action
Promises to Keep: Closing the Gaps in Women’s Cardiovascular Health
Women’s Cardiovascular Health Begins in Childhood

Comprehensive Centers of Excellence for Women’s Cardiovascular Care: A Science Advisory From the American Heart Association, American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine
items.abstract: Improving cardiovascular health in women is an urgent public health priority given the persistent and pervasive gaps in awareness, prevention, and management of cardiovascular disease in this population. Advances in scientific understanding have led to increased recognition of female-specific considerations in cardiovascular disease, which informed the development of the Female Life Stage construct by the American Heart Association in collaboration with the American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine. This construct integrates assessment of hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health across life stages. However, gaps remain in operationalizing this construct and optimizing the delivery of patient-centered, interdisciplinary care among women. Over the past several decades, women’s cardiovascular centers have emerged as leaders, expanded rapidly, and elevated the recognition of cardiovascular diseases that exclusively, disproportionately, or differently affect women (eg, myocardial infarction with nonobstructive coronary arteries, spontaneous coronary artery dissection, Takotsubo syndrome). In this science advisory, we describe the current landscape of women’s cardiovascular centers and propose a national infrastructure to support the expansion of dedicated Comprehensive Centers of Excellence for Women’s Cardiovascular Care. These centers are conceptualized as interdisciplinary care models comprising 4 defining pillars: interdisciplinary clinical care, education and training, research, and community engagement. By establishing integrated pathways that span clinical disciplines, these centers can reduce fragmentation, enhance earlier risk identification, and expand opportunities to increase representation of women in clinical research. In doing so, they offer a bold opportunity for a scalable and equitable model to improve cardiovascular health for all women.
