Price Variation in Outpatient Percutaneous Coronary Intervention
items.abstract: ore than 600 000 percutaneous coronary interventions (PCIs) are performed annually in the United States. 1 Increasing procedural safety, same-day discharge pathways, and expansion of Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services reimbursement have accelerated the transition of elective PCI into outpatient settings, including hospital outpatient departments (HOPDs) and ambulatory surgical centers (ASCs).[2][3][4] Although outpatient PCI may reduce resource utilization and overall spending, little is known about how negotiated prices vary across outpatient sites of care. 2 The 2021 Hospital Price Transparency Rule requires hospitals to disclose payer-specific negotiated rates for all services and has enabled national analyses of pricing variation for cardiovascular services.5 Previous work leveraging these data has demonstrated substantial variation in commercial prices for common cardiovascular procedures, but outpatient PCI pricing remains poorly characterized.5 We used national price transparency data to quantify variation in prices for outpatient PCI across HOPDs versus ASCs and to evaluate associations between facility characteristics and negotiated commercial prices.

items.title: Optimizing US Prehospital Care of ST-Segment–Elevation Myocardial Infarction Because Time Is Life, Not Just Muscle
Effect of Activin Type II Receptor Signaling in Patients With HFpEF and Pulmonary Hypertension: A Critical Analysis of Biological Mechanisms and Clinical Trials
items.abstract: The totality of evidence indicates that the mechanisms underlying the increase in pulmonary vascular resistance in patients with combined postcapillary and precapillary pulmonary hypertension (CpcPH) associated with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) differ meaningfully from those responsible for the increase in pulmonary vascular resistance in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension. CpcPH-HFpEF is a complex disorder involving the pulmonary veins, left atrium, and pulmonary arterioles, but recent evidence has highlighted a potentially central role for pulmonary venous and left atrial (LA) dysfunction. Epicardial adipose tissue occupies anatomical proximity to both structures, allowing derivative secretory products to influence their structure and function. The most well-characterized proinflammatory adipokine released from an expanded epicardial fat mass is activin A, which causes fibrosis and cardiomyocyte stiffness and senescence in underlying tissues by signaling through activin type II receptor signal transduction. Such signaling regulates pulmonary venular responses to mechanical stretch, and circulating activin A is elevated in patients with HFpEF who have enlarged LA chambers, pulmonary venous hypertension and increased pulmonary vascular resistance. The adipokine hypothesis of HFpEF identified activin A and activin type II receptor signaling as key adipokine mediators in the pathogenesis of HFpEF. Experimentally, activin A signaling promotes the development of both atrial myopathy and HFpEF, and activin type II receptor ligand traps alleviate HFpEF and ameliorate both the pulmonary vascular and left heart abnormalities in experimental models in which CpcPH-HFpEF is induced by obesity. These collective observations led to the prospective hypothesis that adipokine modulation by sotatercept would mediate benefits on the left heart in patients with CpcPH-HFpEF. These expectations were validated when the CADENCE trial showed that sotatercept decreased both pulmonary artery wedge pressures and left atrial volume index in patients with CpcPH-HFpEF, which are effects that could not explained by a decrease in pulmonary vascular resistance. Activin A released from an expanded epicardial adipose tissue promotes both pulmonary venous and left atrial remodeling and fibrosis in vivo, which (in turn) are effects that can be attenuated by an activin A decoy. The efficacy of sotatercept to slow the progression of CpcPH-HFpEF is now being tested in a phase III outcomes trial.

items.title: Cardiac Allograft Vasculopathy Demonstrated by Coronary Angiography and Histopathological Correlates

ROR2 Drives Right Ventricular Heart Failure Through Disruption of Proteostasis
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: No therapies exist to reverse right ventricular failure (RVF), and the molecular mechanisms that drive RVF remain understudied. We recently reported that the developmentally restricted noncanonical WNT receptor ROR2 (receptor tyrosine kinase-like orphan receptor 2) is upregulated in human RVF in proportion to severity of disease. Here we test the mechanistic role of ROR2 in RVF pathogenesis. METHODS: ROR2 was overexpressed or knocked down in neonatal rat ventricular myocytes and then characterized using confocal microscopy, RNA sequencing, proteomics, proteostatic functional assays, and pacing to assess contractile properties. The impact of cardiac ROR2 expression was evaluated in mice by AAV9-mediated overexpression and by AAV9-mediated delivery of short hairpin RNA to knockdown ROR2 in a pulmonary artery banded pressure overload model of RVF. ROR2 -modified mice were evaluated by echocardiography, histology, and right ventricle protein synthesis and proteasome capacity. RESULTS: In neonatal rat ventricular myocytes, we find that ROR2 profoundly dysregulates the coordination between protein translation and folding. This imbalance leads to excess protein clearance by the ubiquitin proteasome system with dramatic impacts on sarcomere and cytoskeletal structure and function. Inhibiting the ubiquitin proteasome system or restoring chaperone expression is sufficient to partially rescue ROR2-induced structural and contractile deficits in cardiomyocytes. In mice, forced cardiac ROR2 expression is sufficient to disrupt proteostasis and drive RVF, whereas conversely Ror2 knockdown partially rescues proteostasis and right ventricle structure and function in a pressure overload model of RVF. CONCLUSIONS: In sum, ROR2 is a key driver of RVF pathogenesis through proteostatic disruption and thus provides a promising target to treat RVF.

items.title: Outcomes of Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome by Subtype and Presence of Ventriculocoronary Connections: A Fetal Heart Society Multicenter Retrospective Study
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS) is classified by anatomic subtype: mitral atresia and aortic atresia (MA/AA), mitral stenosis and aortic atresia (MS/AA), and mitral stenosis and aortic stenosis (MS/AS). The MS/AA subtype is associated with ventriculocoronary connections (VCCs). We assessed whether specific HLHS subtypes are associated with an increased risk of mortality and whether this risk is stratified by VCCs identified during fetal or postnatal echocardiography. We also assessed whether the type of neonatal intervention performed modified the risk. METHODS: We performed a multicenter retrospective cohort study of fetuses and infants <2 months old with HLHS who were admitted between January 2012 and December 2016 to participating Fetal Heart Society institutions. Clinical and demographic data were collected. Fetal and transthoracic echocardiograms from a subset of patients with MS/AA and those with suspected VCCs were reviewed. Cox proportional hazards analysis was performed, controlling for cardiac center (random effect), birth weight, genetic diagnosis, extracardiac malformation, and restricted/intact atrial septum. RESULTS: Among 16 centers, 591 patients were born alive with intention to treat. MA/AA was the most common subtype (261, 44%), followed by MS/AA (200, 34%) and MS/AS (130, 22%). Of those with MS/AA, 115 (58%) had suspected VCCs. Median follow-up was 9.0 (interquartile range: 7.0, 10.8) years. Overall transplant-free survival (TFS) was 55.6% at 5 years and 49.4% at 10 years. When comparing MA/AA, MS/AS, and MS/AA with and without VCCs (reference group: MS/AA without VCCs), MS/AA with VCCs had the lowest TFS (hazard ratio [HR], 1.69 [1.12, 2.57]; 5-year TFS, 44.7%; 10-year TFS, 40.3%). This was followed by MA/AA (HR, 1.40 [0.95, 2.05]; 5-year TFS, 54.1%; 10-year TFS, 46.6%). Survival of MS/AA without VCCs (5-year TFS, 60.4%; 10-year TFS, 56.9%) was similar to MS/AS (HR, 0.91 [0.59, 1.41]; 5-year TFS, 65.0%; 10-year TFS, 58.3%). Among those with a prenatal diagnosis of HLHS (n=532), patients with MS/AA and VCCs suspected on fetal echocardiogram had a lower TFS compared with those with MS/AA without fetal suspicion for VCCs (HR, 1.79 [1.12, 2.85]). Fetal echocardiography was used to diagnose VCCs in 33 of 103 (32%) cases with MS/AA and VCCs suspected postnatally. Of patients with MS/AA and VCCs, type of stage I palliation was not associated with TFS ( P =0.784). CONCLUSIONS: In a large, multicenter cohort of HLHS patients, the MS/AA subtype with VCCs had the lowest TFS. Prenatal diagnosis of VCCs was associated with a lower TFS. This study underscores the prognostic value of assessing for VCCs in patients with HLHS both before and after birth.

items.title: Early Discharge Strategy Including Subcutaneous Furosemide in Hospitalized Heart Failure
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients hospitalized for heart failure often require prolonged intravenous diuretic therapy, contributing to costs and risks associated with inpatient care. OBJECTIVES: We evaluated whether an early discharge strategy using subcutaneous furosemide delivered via a wearable minipump could increase days alive and out of hospital (DAOH). METHODS: In this multicenter, open-label, randomized, active-controlled trial in the United Kingdom, 172 patients hospitalized for heart failure requiring ongoing parenteral diuretics were randomly assigned to an early discharge strategy or usual care. Patients in the early discharge group received pH-neutral subcutaneous furosemide via a wearable, patient-operated minipump; postdischarge care included a review every 3 days while receiving subcutaneous furosemide. Both groups had a 2-week clinic review. The primary outcome was DAOH at 30 days after randomization. RESULTS: A total of 92 patients were assigned to early discharge and 80 to usual care. The early discharge strategy resulted in 4.0 more DAOH at 30 days (95% CI: 2.1-5.8 days; P < 0.001). Index hospitalization was shorter by a mean of 5.5 days (95% CI: 7.4-3.6 days; P < 0.001). The benefit in DAOH was sustained at 60 days (difference 4.2 days; 95% CI: 0.9-7.6 days), despite more heart failure readmissions in the early discharge group (13 [14%] patients vs 5 [6%] patients; OR: 2.45; 95% CI: 0.81-7.43). Serious adverse events occurred in 25% and 23% of patients, respectively. Device-related problems occurred with 3% of minipump placements, but none were serious. CONCLUSIONS: An early discharge strategy using a subcutaneous furosemide minipump increased DAOH compared with usual care. (Use of a Novel SUBCUTaneous Preparation of Furosemide to Facilitate Early Supported Discharge of Patients With Heart Failure [SUBCUT-HF II]; NCT05419115).

Transseptal Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement for Mitral Annular Calcification
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with symptomatic mitral valve dysfunction (MVD) and mitral annular calcification (MAC) represent one of the most challenging populations in structural heart disease. Advanced age, multiple comorbidities, extensive annular calcification, and unfavorable anatomy often preclude surgical mitral valve replacement or transcatheter repair, leaving many patients with limited treatment options. Whether fully percutaneous transseptal transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) can provide a meaningful treatment pathway for patients with MAC-related MVD remains uncertain. OBJECTIVES: The goal of this study was to evaluate 1-year clinical, echocardiographic, and patient-centered outcomes after transseptal TMVR with the SAPIEN M3 system in patients with symptomatic MAC-related MVD. METHODS: The ENCIRCLE (SAPIEN M3 System Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement Via Transseptal Access) trial MAC Registry is a prospective, multicenter, single-arm study that enrolled symptomatic patients with MAC-related MVD, including ≥ moderate to severe mitral regurgitation (MR), severe mitral stenosis, or combined moderate MR with at least moderate mitral stenosis, who were considered unsuitable for surgery or transcatheter repair. The primary endpoint was a nonhierarchical composite of all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization (HFH) at 1 year. RESULTS: Among 364 screened patients, TVMR was attempted in 100, and the valve was implanted in 93. Mean age was 76.1 ± 9.2 years, 51.0% were male, 73.0% were in NYHA functional class III/IV, and mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality score for mitral valve replacement was 8.4% ± 4.9%. At 1 year, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of all-cause mortality or HFH was 33.6% (95% CI: 25.0%-44.1%), with 21.1% all-cause mortality and 19.4% HFH. Disabling stroke occurred in 5.1%, clinically significant left ventricular outflow tract obstruction in 4.8%, valve thrombosis in 2.3%, hemolysis requiring transfusion or mitral valve reintervention in 9.2%, and mitral valve re-intervention in 11.4%. Among implanted patients, MR ≤1+ was achieved in 98.5% at 1 year. Improvements in NYHA functional class, Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary score, and 6-minute walk distance were sustained through 1 year. CONCLUSIONS: In carefully selected patients with symptomatic MAC-related MVD unsuitable for surgery or transcatheter repair, transseptal TMVR with the SAPIEN M3 system was associated with sustained MR reduction and meaningful improvements in symptoms and quality of life through 1 year. These findings support consideration of transseptal TMVR as a treatment pathway for selected patients with MAC-related MVD.

items.title: Exercise Prescriptions for Cardiovascular Health in Adults: 2026 ACC Scientific Statement
items.abstract: Regular physical activity and structured exercise are foundational for cardiovascular prevention and treatment, yet exercise prescription remains inconsistently integrated into routine cardiovascular care. This American College of Cardiology scientific statement provides contemporary, practical guidance for clinicians on prescribing exercise across the spectrum of cardiovascular health and disease. The statement reviews evidence supporting physical activity, exercise training, and cardiorespiratory fitness as powerful determinants of cardiovascular outcomes, emphasizing that the greatest absolute benefits occur when inactive individuals begin moving and that additional benefits accrue with higher volumes and intensity, within appropriate clinical limits. It summarizes approaches to aerobic, resistance, balance, and flexibility training; highlights the role of cardiac rehabilitation and supervised, home-based, hybrid, and virtual models; and addresses individualized exercise prescription for patients with coronary artery disease, peripheral artery disease, heart failure, cardiomyopathies, hypertension, overweight and obesity, adult congenital heart disease, and older age. The statement also discusses when exercise testing is useful to assess safety, guide intensity, establish baseline fitness, and monitor responses, while recognizing that routine preparticipation testing is not required for most asymptomatic individuals. Wearable devices and digital tools are reviewed as adjuncts to self-monitoring, goal setting, and cardiac rehabilitation extension, with attention to equity, access, and digital literacy. Key implementation priorities include improving clinician training, embedding physical activity counseling into cardiovascular care, tailoring prescriptions to patient goals and functional capacity, and expanding research on long-term adherence, clinical outcomes, diverse populations, and scalable delivery models. Exercise should be prescribed as a core component of cardiovascular prevention and disease management.

items.title: Occupational Disparities in Cardiovascular Risk and Management in Contemporary China
items.abstract: Background Although occupational disparities in cardiovascular health are increasingly recognized, a comprehensive understanding of cardiovascular health across contemporary occupational contexts-particularly in rapidly transitioning economies-remains limited. Objectives This study aimed to characterize geographic and occupational patterns of cardiovascular risk, risk-factor management, and potential prevention opportunities among employed adults in contemporary China. Methods In this nationwide cross-sectional study, we analyzed 1,421,390 employees aged 20 to 65 years who underwent health examinations at 167 centers across 24 provinces in China between 2021 and 2023. Eighteen occupations were defined based on participants' employer registration and industry affiliation, and were classified into primary, secondary, and tertiary sectors, with the tertiary sector further subclassified into modern, public, and life services. Age- and sex-standardized prevalence of coronary heart disease (CHD) and cardiometabolic risk factors was estimated, along with age- and sex-standardized rates of treatment and control for hypertension and diabetes, and treatment for hypercholesterolemia and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) control. Ten-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk was calculated using the Prediction for ASCVD Risk in China model. We then assessed changes in the proportion of individuals classified as having moderate-to-high 10-year ASCVD risk under simulated scenarios that set elevated blood pressure and total cholesterol to target levels and current smoking to noncurrent smoking and compared these reductions across occupations. Results The mean age of participants was 33.8 years, and 53.4% were male. Overall, the age- and sex-standardized prevalence of CHD was 1.33% (95% CI: 1.29%-1.37%) and demonstrated a pronounced north-south gradient (P Conclusions Occupational context may provide a practical framework for identifying patterns of cardiovascular risk, management gaps, and prevention opportunities among China's working population. Despite lower observed disease burden, modern occupational sectors showed suboptimal risk-factor management, whereas simulated ASCVD risk reductions varied across occupations, highlighting distinct prevention needs and opportunities across occupational contexts.

Interpreting High-Sensitivity Cardiac Troponin in Clinical Practice and Emerging Directions
items.abstract: High-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) assays have solved the problem of detecting myocardial injury and, in doing so, created the problem of classifying it. Abnormal troponin concentrations are now known to be common across a wide spectrum of cardiac and systemic disease, and the central challenge of contemporary practice is no longer whether myocardial injury can be detected, but whether it can be correctly classified. Misclassification occurs in both directions and with real consequence: nonischemic myocardial injury is frequently mislabeled as secondary myocardial infarction (MI), contributing to the overdiagnosis of MI, and chronic myocardial injury, which carries a risk of subsequent MI or cardiovascular death approaching that of primary MI, is routinely dismissed once infarction has been excluded. This narrative review argues that accurate classification cannot be delegated to an algorithm and instead requires integrated, context-aware interpretation grounded in 4 domains: 1) the analytical and biological properties of hs-cTnI and hs-cTnT, including assay-specific and sex-specific thresholds, clearance kinetics, and sources of analytical interference and false-positive results; 2) the capabilities and limitations of guideline-endorsed serial testing, including the European Society of Cardiology 0/1h and 0/2h algorithms, point-of-care platforms, and artificial intelligence-based decision support; 3) rigorous application of the Fifth Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction, in particular the distinctions between myocardial injury, necrosis, and infarction, and between diagnosis and risk stratification; and 4) recognition of the non-acute coronary syndrome conditions-chronic kidney disease, heart failure, sepsis, tachyarrhythmias, pulmonary embolism, takotsubo syndrome, and others-in which troponin elevation is expected rather than anomalous. We provide explicit bedside guidance for the situations that clinicians find most difficult, including suspected secondary MI, the observe zone, and troponin elevation without a dynamic pattern. Finally, we review emerging understanding of troponin biology, clearance, proteolysis and fragmentation, macrotroponin, antitroponin autoantibodies, and extracellular vesicle-associated troponin, which may eventually allow the assay itself to carry more of the interpretive burden. Until then, that burden rests with the clinician.

items.title: Beyond HFmrEF
Occlusion-Focused Triage vs Very-High-Risk NSTEMI Criteria
items.abstract: Background The current ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI)/NSTEMI framework may not fully identify patients with ACO who present without diagnostic STE. Although immediate invasive management is recommended for patients with very-high-risk NSTEMI features, these criteria are inconsistently applied in clinical practice. The OMI/NOMI framework has been proposed as an alternative strategy. Objectives This study sought to compare the occlusive and nonocclusive myocardial infarction (OMI/NOMI) classification with guideline-defined very-high-risk non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) criteria for the identification of acute coronary occlusion (ACO) in patients without diagnostic STE. Methods This was a substudy of the multicenter, cluster-randomized DIFOCCULT-3 (Time for a Diagnostic Paradigm Shift From ST-Elevation/Non-ST-Elevation to Occlusion/Non-Occlusion Myocardial Infarction-3) trial. Consecutive adult patients without diagnostic STE on the admission electrocardiogram were included and managed according to either the conventional STEMI/NSTEMI or the OMI/NOMI approach. Very-high-risk NSTEMI was defined according to current guidelines. Outcomes included immediate invasive management (within 2 hours) and adjudicated ACO. Results Among 4,398 patients, very-high-risk NSTEMI criteria identified a small proportion of patients and were inconsistently translated into early intervention. The OMI/NOMI approach selected more patients for early invasive management compared with the STEMI/NSTEMI framework (45.4% vs 13.6%; P Conclusions An occlusion-focused diagnostic approach was associated with substantially higher rates of immediate invasive management and earlier identification of patients with adjudicated ACO.

Acute Coronary Occlusions in NSTEMI Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention
items.abstract: Background Patients may present with acute coronary occlusions (ACOs) without manifesting electrocardiographic criteria for ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Objectives The aim of this study was to examine the incidence, clinical characteristics, and in-hospital outcomes of non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) with ACO. Methods The study included patients with STEMI and NSTEMI in the CathPCI Registry who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention between April 1, 2018, and June 30, 2023. ACO was defined as 100% stenosis deemed acute. The cohort was stratified into STEMI (including STEMI equivalents), NSTEMI-ACO, and NSTEMI-no-ACO. The primary outcome was a composite of in-hospital stroke, myocardial infarction, or cardiovascular mortality. A sensitivity analysis with ACO defined as 100% acute occlusion or TIMI flow grade 0 or 1 in the culprit artery was performed. Results Of 1,198,544 patients, 26.1% had STEMI, 11.0% had NSTEMI-ACO (15% of whom had NSTEMI), and 62.9% had NSTEMI-no-ACO. Compared with those with NSTEMI-no-ACO, NSTEMI-ACO patients had more cardiogenic shock (9.0% STEMI vs 3.8% NSTEMI-ACO vs 1.9% NSTEMI-no-ACO; P Conclusions ACO occurs in a substantial proportion of patients with NSTEMI and is associated with worse in-hospital outcomes relative to those with NSTEMI-no-ACO. Further studies of early identification and reperfusion practices for NSTEMI-ACO are warranted.

items.title: Immediate Versus Staged Complete Revascularization in Multivessel Disease and STEMI
items.abstract: Background For patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and multivessel disease, complete revascularization is recommended. The timing of nonculprit lesion intervention, either immediately during the index procedure or staged at a later time, has been investigated in randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Objectives This study sought to perform a meta-analysis of RCTs comparing immediate vs staged complete revascularization in patients with multivessel disease presenting with STEMI. Methods We conducted a frequentist, pairwise meta-analysis. Studies were selected based on the following inclusion criteria: multicenter RCTs comparing immediate vs staged nonculprit revascularization in patients presenting with STEMI; exclusive use of second-generation (or newer) drug-eluting stents; a follow-up duration of ≥1 year; and publication in a peer-reviewed journal. The primary outcome of interest was all-cause mortality, whereas secondary outcomes included myocardial infarction (MI), cardiac death, and unplanned revascularization. Summary estimates were computed using random-effects models with inverse-variance weighting based on trial-level HRs and 95% CIs. The study protocol was registered on PROSPERO (CRD420251124207). Results After a systematic search, 4 randomized trials comprising 2,651 patients were included in the meta-analysis. The risk of all-cause death at 1-year was higher with immediate complete revascularization (HR: 1.50; 95% CI: 1.02-2.21; P = 0.04; prediction interval [PI]: 0.80-2.81; I 2 = 0%; t 2 = 0). Immediate complete revascularization reduced the risk of recurrent MI when using the protocol specified definitions which included procedural MI (HR: 0.58; 95% CI: 0.36-0.94; P = 0.02; PI: 0.22-1.54; I 2 = 0%; t 2 = 0.034) but did not reduce risk of spontaneous MI (HR: 0.91; 95% CI: 0.55-1.48; P = 0.90; PI: 0.41-2.00; I 2 = 0%; τ 2 = 0.00). The risk of cardiac death and unplanned revascularization was comparable between the treatment groups. Conclusions In STEMI and multivessel disease, immediate complete revascularization may be associated with an increased risk of all-cause death at 1-year when compared with staged complete revascularization. The treatment effect on mortality should be interpreted cautiously because of the relatively low number of deaths across the 4 trials and the statistical fragility of the findings. The findings from this analysis do not support an immediate complete revascularization strategy in these patients.

items.title: Impact of Extent of Coronary Artery Disease in Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Coronary artery disease is present in one-half of patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). The recent randomized controlled PRO-TAVI (Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Before Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation) trial indicated that deferral of percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is safe in patients with concomitant coronary artery disease at 1-year follow-up. The SYNTAX (Synergy between Percutaneous Coronary Intervention with TAXUS and Cardiac Surgery) score quantifies the extent of coronary artery disease, which may guide individualized revascularization strategies. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to evaluate the association between SYNTAX score (SS) and clinical outcomes in patients undergoing TAVR. METHODS: This study was a substudy of the PRO-TAVI trial, including 466 patients with significant coronary artery disease undergoing TAVR randomized to deferral of PCI or PCI before TAVR. SS was calculated from preprocedural coronary angiograms, and patients were stratified by SS quartiles. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke, and major bleeding at 1 year. An ischemic composite outcome of all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, and stroke was also assessed. RESULTS: The primary composite outcome did not differ across SS categories between the deferral and PCI groups at 1-year follow-up, which was completed by all but 1 patient. In patients with SS >17, the ischemic composite outcome occurred more often in the deferral group (30.9% vs 14.8%; adjusted HR: 2.43; 95% CI: 1.04-5.64; P = 0.04), driven primarily by all-cause mortality and stroke. Bleeding events were less frequent in the deferral group across all SS subgroups. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with concomitant coronary artery disease undergoing TAVR, deferral of PCI reduced bleeding risk and appeared safe across all SS categories. Deferral of PCI in patients with more complex coronary artery disease (SS >17) was associated with higher risk for the ischemic composite outcome. These post hoc findings require confirmation in randomized trials. (Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Before Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation [PRO-TAVI]; NCT05078619).

items.title: Intraprocedural Cardiac Arrest in Patients Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Interventions in the United States
items.abstract: Background Cardiac arrest (CA) during percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI) is a catastrophic procedural complication. Contemporary rates of CA during PCI are unknown. Objectives This study sought to understand contemporary rates of CA, associated mortality, and identify predictors of CA during PCI. Methods Patients with CA during PCI from 2018 to 2023 were identified from the National Cardiovascular Data Registry CathPCI Registry. Trends in intraprocedural CA (IPCA) incidence and in-hospital death were evaluated. Predictors of IPCA and risk-adjusted mortality were identified. Results A total of 36,755 IPCA occurred during 3,956,840 PCIs (0.93%), including in 0.24% of elective PCIs, 0.32% of PCIs for stable coronary artery disease, and 1.28% of acute coronary syndrome interventions. The incidence of IPCA increased over time (0.62% in 2018 to 1.07% in 2023; P Conclusions IPCA complicates 0.93% of contemporary PCI. Despite an increasing incidence of risk-adjusted IPCA, there were slight declines in risk-adjusted in-hospital mortality in the study period. Several patient and procedural characteristics were independently associated with intraprocedural CA.

Frequency and Prognosis of Alternative Definitions of Occlusion Myocardial Infarction Across the Whole Spectrum of Acute Coronary Syndromes
items.abstract: Background Occlusion myocardial infarction (OMI) refers to a myocardial infarction caused by a persistent or transient, complete or near-complete coronary artery occlusion. Multiple definitions have been proposed, yet their frequency and comparative prognostic relevance remain unclear. Objectives This study sought to evaluate the frequency and prognosis of previously proposed OMI definitions across the whole spectrum of acute coronary syndromes (ACS) from the MATRIX trial. Methods Five alternative OMI definitions were assessed: 1) culprit artery (CA) TIMI flow grade 0; 2) CA-TIMI flow grade 0-1; 3) CA-TIMI flow grade 0-2; 4) CA-TIMI flow grade 0-2 or TIMI flow grade 3 with cardiac troponin >30× upper reference limit; and 5) CA-TIMI flow grade 0-2 or CA-TIMI flow grade 3 with cardiac troponin >100× upper reference limit. The endpoint of interest was 1-year all-cause mortality. Results Among 6,558 patients with ACS, OMI frequency ranged from 37.8% for definition 1 to 76.1% for definition 4. OMI was independently associated with higher 1-year mortality according to definitions 1-4 (adjusted HR: 2.08 [95% CI: 1.56-2.78], 1.97[1.47-2.63], 1.70 [1.25-2.32], 1.47 [1.01-2.12], respectively) but not according to definition 5 (adjusted HR: 1.26 [0.90-1.75]). OMI definitions exclusively based on impaired CA flow (ie, definitions 1-3) improved discrimination, reclassification, and model fit when added to the conventional STE/NSTE-ACS classification. One-year mortality did not differ among patients with NSTE-ACS with OMI definition 1 or 2 compared with ST-segment elevation MI (STEMI) patients. Conclusions OMI defined by impaired CA flow confers prognostic implications beyond the presence or absence of ST-segment elevation in a broad ACS population and identifies patients without ST-segment elevation with 1-year mortality similar to that of STEMI.

items.title: Conduction System Versus Right Ventricular Pacing in Patients Undergoing TAVR
items.abstract: Background Pacemaker implantation after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is common and has been associated with adverse clinical outcomes. Cardiac physiological pacing (CPP) may preserve ventricular synchrony and reduce heart failure (HF) events compared with right ventricular pacing (RVP). Objectives This study sought to compare long-term clinical outcomes of CPP vs RVP in patients requiring permanent pacing after TAVR. Methods Registro de Estimulación Fisiológica-TAVR is a retrospective, multicenter nationwide registry including patients undergoing TAVR and pacemaker implantation within 30 days. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed using baseline clinical and echocardiographic variables, yielding 466 matched pairs. The primary endpoint was the composite of cardiovascular death or HF hospitalization. Cox proportional hazards models were used for time-to-event analyses. Median follow-up was 24 months. Results In the propensity score-matched cohort, CPP was associated with a lower incidence of the primary endpoint than RVP (9.7% vs 17.6%; HR: 0.57; 95% CI: 0.39-0.83; P = 0.003). This difference was driven by fewer HF hospitalizations (7.9% vs 13.9%; HR: 0.57; 95% CI: 0.37-0.86; P = 0.008). No significant differences were observed in cardiovascular death or all-cause mortality between groups. Conclusions In this multicenter propensity score-matched study, CPP after TAVR was associated with a lower risk of the primary endpoint, driven by fewer HF hospitalizations. These findings support the need for further randomized clinical trials to evaluate the role of CPP in post-TAVR patients requiring ventricular pacing.

Feasibility and Restenosis Predictors of Optical Frequency Domain Imaging-Guided Drug-Coated Balloon Treatment for Femoropopliteal Lesions
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: The clinical utility of optical frequency domain imaging (OFDI) for guiding endovascular therapy in femoropopliteal lesions has not been established. Additionally, the prognostic value of OFDI findings during drug-coated balloon (DCB) treatment for femoropopliteal lesions has never been evaluated. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to clarify the feasibility of OFDI-guided DCB treatment and investigate the OFDI findings associated with restenosis after DCB treatment in femoropopliteal lesions. METHODS: This multicenter, prospective, observational study included patients with symptomatic, nonseverely calcified femoropopliteal lesions who underwent DCB treatment under OFDI guidance. Procedural success was defined as residual stenosis of less than 30% without flow compromise and without any procedural complications. The primary outcome was restenosis of the target lesion, defined as a peak systolic velocity ratio of ≥2.5, as measured by duplex ultrasound at rest or target lesion revascularization. RESULTS: A total of 202 lesions were initially enrolled, of which 35 (17.3%) were excluded primarily because of severe calcification or inadequate OFDI data. Among the 167 analyzable lesions included in the present analysis, the procedural success rate and 1-year freedom from restenosis were 91.6% and 85.5%, respectively. In the procedural OFDI findings, a calcified nodule in the target lesion (subdistribution hazard ratio: 3.25; 95% CI: 1.01-10.42; P = 0.048) was associated with restenosis. CONCLUSIONS: OFDI-guided DCB treatment is feasible in selected femoropopliteal lesions. An OFDI-detected calcified nodule is associated with an increased risk of restenosis after DCB treatment for femoropopliteal lesions.

Immediate Complete Revascularization During Index Admission in Older Patients With ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction
items.abstract: Background Whether age affects the comparative treatment effect of immediate complete revascularization (CR) vs staged CR during the index admission in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction and multivessel disease remains unknown. Objectives This study aimed to assess how age influences clinical outcomes in patients with with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction and multivessel disease randomized to immediate or in-hospital staged CR. Methods This is a secondary analysis of the OPTION-STEMI (Optimal Timing of Fractional Flow Reserve-Guided Complete Revascularization for Non-Infarct-Related Artery in ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction with Multivessel Disease) trial, which included 994 patients randomized to immediate or in-hospital staged CR. The primary endpoint at 1 year, defined as a composite of all-cause death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or any unplanned revascularization, was analyzed according to age and CR strategy. Results A significant interaction was found between age, as a continuous variable, and CR strategy for the primary endpoint (interaction P = 0.015). The HR for the primary endpoint was initially higher in the staged CR arm until approximately 67 years, after which it increased steadily in the immediate CR arm. In the binary analysis, a significantly higher incidence of the primary endpoint was observed in the immediate CR arm compared with the staged CR arm in patients ≥70 years (45 of 202 [22.3%] vs 29 of 210 [13.8%]; HR: 1.68; 95% CI: 1.06-2.69; log-rank P = 0.029), but not in patients Conclusions This post hoc analysis of the OPTION-STEMI trial demonstrates that older patients experience significantly worse clinical outcomes with immediate CR than with in-hospital staged CR. These findings suggest that age modifies the treatment effect of the CR strategy and warrant confirmation in adequately powered trials (Timing of FFR-guided PCI for Non-IRA in STEMI and MVD [OPTION-STEMI]; NCT04626882).

items.title: Complete, But Not All at Once
Snare-Guided Repositioning of a Vascular Plug Device for Device-Related Hemolytic Anemia
Impact of Recurrent Mitral Regurgitation Following Mitral Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair on Long-Term Outcomes
items.abstract: Background Residual mitral regurgitation (MR) after mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER) is a major determinant of outcome. However, the prognostic impact of recurrent mitral regurgitation (recMR) after initially successful M-TEER remains unclear. Objectives This study aimed to evaluate the association between recMR after successful M-TEER and long-term mortality across degenerative mitral regurgitation (DMR) and functional mitral regurgitation (FMR). Methods This retrospective cohort included 461 consecutive patients with MR undergoing successful M-TEER (residual mitral regurgitation ≤2+ at discharge) between 2008 and 2021. recMR was defined as ≥1-grade increase in mitral regurgitation severity at follow-up compared with discharge. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality. Results Among 461 patients with MR undergoing M_TEER (mean age 75.0 ± 9.1 years; 60.7% male [280 of 461]; 29.3% [135 of 461] had DMR), recMR occurred in 31.7% (146 of 461) (FMR in 31.9% [104 of 326]; DMR in 31.1% [42 of 135]). The median follow-up time was 3.44 years (Q1-Q3: 1.51-3.99 years). In a 12-month landmark analysis, absence of recMR was associated with improved survival (log-rank, P = 0.0088). At 4 years, all-cause mortality was 44.8% (95% CI: 38.7%-50.3%) in patients without recMR and 56.3% (95% CI: 47.2%-63.9%) in those with recMR. In multivariable Cox regression, recMR independently predicted higher mortality (HR: 1.43; 95% CI: 1.06-1.93; P = 0.019). The survival difference was significant in patients with DMR (log-rank, P = 0.014) but not with FMR (P = 0.11). Conclusions recMR is common and independently associated with increased mortality after M-TEER, with a more pronounced effect in patients with DMR. Identification of patients at risk may inform closer surveillance and timely reintervention.

items.title: Dynamic Common Iliac Vein Compression by the Adjacent Intestine Revealed by Intravascular Ultrasound
Morphology-Dependent Dose-Response of Intravascular Lithotripsy on Coronary Calcium Fracture
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) uses ultrasonic acoustic pressure waves to modify calcification to enable optimal balloon and stent expansion in calcified lesions. However, the dose-response relationship for creating fractures within calcified lesions of different calcium morphologies is unknown. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to evaluate the dose-dependent effects of IVL on calcium fracture overall and in the setting of calcification arc <180° vs ≥180°. METHODS: Micro-computed tomography images were acquired before and after 10, 20, 40, 60, 80, and 120 pulses of IVL treatment (Shockwave Medical) in an ex vivo study of 5 cadaveric human hearts (15 coronary lesions). A total of 30 cross-sections of micro-computed tomography (2 sections per lesion) were analyzed for this study. RESULTS: Cumulative fracture occurrence increased progressively with the number of IVL pulses delivered, with fractures observed in 33% of sections after 10 pulses, 50% after 40 pulses, and 60% after 120 pulses. Calcification arc ≥180° exhibited a higher fracture occurrence compared with arc <180° (P = 0.028). After adjustment for pulse number, calcification arc ≥180° was associated with significantly higher fracture counts compared with arc <180° (rate ratio = 6.1, P = 0.003). CONCLUSIONS: Fracture occurrence following IVL increased with cumulative pulse delivery and differed significantly according to calcification concentricity. Calcification arc ≥180° demonstrated a higher and earlier likelihood of fracture occurrence than arc <180°, independent of pulse number. These findings establish a clear dose-dependent relationship between IVL pulse delivery and fracture formation and highlight calcification concentricity as a key determinant of fracture response.

items.title: Pulmonary Index of Microcirculatory Resistance
Two-Year Outcomes of the Prospective THRILLER Registry on Popliteal and Infrapopliteal Endovascular Interventions for CLTI
items.abstract: Background Over 70% of patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) present with below-the-knee disease, and there is a growing trend towards endovascular revascularization. Objectives The Dutch Chronic Lower Limb-Threatening Ischemia Registry (THRILLER) aimed to provide real-world data on outcomes after popliteal and infrapopliteal endovascular revascularization to guide revascularization strategies. Methods This prospective multicenter registry included consecutive CLTI patients undergoing popliteal or infrapopliteal endovascular revascularization in seven Dutch hospitals. Primary outcomes were limb salvage and amputation-free survival (AFS) at 24 months, estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. Results Between February 2021 and December 2023, a total of 1,119 interventions in 1,060 limbs (938 patients) were included, treating 551 popliteal, 1,352 tibial, and 239 pedal lesions. The median follow-up was 43.6 months (Q1-Q3: 35.5-52.7 months). Overall, 78.4% (831/1,060) of the limbs were Rutherford 5 and 8.1% (86/1,060) were Rutherford 6; 41.3% (382/926) were WIfI (Wound, Ischemia, and foot Infection) stage 4. Technical success was achieved in 92.3% (1,033/1,119). Limb salvage and AFS decreased significantly after technical failure and with increasing WIfI stage and Rutherford category. Compared to Rutherford 5, Rutherford 6 limbs had significantly worse limb salvage (HR: 3.07; 95% CI: 1.89-4.99; P Conclusions Endovascular revascularization for popliteal and infrapopliteal disease in patients with CLTI is safe and effective in preventing limb loss and mortality at 2 years, although patients with Rutherford 6 limbs face significantly worse outcomes, particularly in the first 3 months.

items.title: Calcium Fracture Detection by Optical Coherence Tomography Versus Intravascular Ultrasound Following Intravascular Lithotripsy
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Calcium fracture is a metric used to assess lesion preparation success. We have shown previously that optical coherence tomography (OCT) misses approximately half of these fractures. Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) is the most commonly used intravascular imaging modality. The sensitivity of IVUS for detecting calcium fractures after intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) is unknown. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to assess the frequency and characteristics of calcium fracture observed on IVUS in comparison to OCT and gold standard micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) using heavily calcified coronary artery cadaveric vessels. METHODS: In an ex vivo study of 5 cadaveric hearts (15 coronary lesions), OCT, IVUS, and micro-CT were obtained before and after IVL coronary artery treatment. Fracture detection rates and appearance patterns were compared across modalities. Receiver operating characteristic analyses evaluated OCT-measured fracture width thresholds for IVUS detectability. RESULTS: Compared with micro-CT, OCT and IVUS significantly underestimated fracture occurrence, but OCT demonstrated higher detection sensitivity than IVUS (P < 0.05 by McNemar's test). Narrow linear nondisplaced fractures identified on OCT were frequently undetectable on IVUS or appeared as subtle hyperechoic shadows. Fracture width was strongly associated with IVUS detectability; fracture width >115 μm on OCT were identified by IVUS with excellent diagnostic performance (area under the curve: 0.99 [95% CI: 0.98-1.00], sensitivity 100%, specificity 92%). CONCLUSIONS: OCT and IVUS underestimate the occurrence of IVL-induced calcium fractures compared with micro-CT, with IVUS demonstrating lower sensitivity than OCT. IVUS detectability is strongly dependent on fracture width. Absence of visible fracture on either OCT or IVUS does not exclude calcium modification.

items.title: Beyond Procedural Success
Periprocedural Pulmonary Hypertension and Outcomes After Mitral Valve Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair
items.abstract: Background Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is common in patients undergoing mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER), but the prognostic significance of periprocedural PH changes remains uncertain. Objectives This study sought to evaluate the association between periprocedural PH patterns and clinical outcomes after M-TEER and to identify predictors of residual and new-onset PH. Methods The OCEAN-Mitral registry prospectively enrolled 3,764 patients with severe mitral regurgitation treated with M-TEER. Among 3,484 patients with paired echocardiographic tricuspid regurgitation pressure gradient (TRPG) data, PH was defined as TRPG >31 mm Hg. Patients were classified as having no PH, normalized PH, new-onset PH, or residual PH according to pre- and postprocedural PH status. The primary endpoint was 2-year cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of residual and new-onset PH. Results No PH was observed in 1,432 patients (41.1%), normalized PH in 763 (21.9%), new-onset PH in 298 (8.6%), and residual PH in 991 (28.4%). The 2-year incidence of the primary endpoint differed significantly across groups (17.6%, 18.1%, 27.2%, and 27.6%, respectively; P 50 mm Hg, and tricuspid annular dilation predicted residual PH, whereas residual mitral regurgitation and postprocedural transmitral gradients >5 mm Hg predicted new-onset PH. Conclusions Periprocedural PH dynamics provide robust risk stratification after M-TEER, identifying low-risk patients with PH normalization and high-risk subsets with residual or new-onset PH, requiring closer surveillance and procedural optimization. Registration Treatment and Prognosis of Heart Valve Registry; UMIN-ID: UMIN000023653.

items.title: Safety and Effectiveness of a Novel Laser-Based Intravascular Lithotripsy System for Coronary Calcium
items.abstract: ObjectivesThis study evaluated the safety and effectiveness of a novel laser- and optic-based quad-emitter IVL system in severely calcified de novo coronary lesions. MethodsFRACTURE was a prospective, multicenter, single-arm trial. The primary safety endpoint was 30-day freedom from major adverse cardiac events (MACE; composite of cardiac death, myocardial infarction, or target vessel revascularization). The primary effectiveness endpoint was procedural success (successful stent delivery with a final residual stenosis <50% and freedom from in-hospital MACE). Both endpoints were evaluated against prespecified performance goals. An optical coherence tomography (OCT) substudy was performed. ResultsA total of 420 patients (mean age: 71.2 ± 9.01 years; 74.0% male) were enrolled. Median calcified length was 34.4 mm (Q1-Q3: 21.3-52.5 mm). Among 106 patients with OCT, at the site of maximum calcification, the calcium arc was 271.89° ± 77.35° and the median thickness was 0.88 mm (Q1-Q3: 0.72-1.11 mm). OCT confirmed calcium fracture in 67% of lesions; the median minimal stent area was 6.51 mm2 (Q1-Q3: 4.85-7.78 mm2), and stent expansion was 94.2% ± 19.4% at the site of maximum calcification. The primary safety endpoint of 30-day freedom from MACE was 93.3% (373/400; with lower bound of 95% CI of 90.8%, exceeding the 86.2% performance goal [P < 0.0001]). The primary effectiveness endpoint of procedural success was 93.7% (374/399; with lower bound of 95% CI of 91.3%, exceeding the 85.8% performance goal [P < 0.0001]). ConclusionsThe quad-emitter IVL system is a safe and effective option to modify severe calcified coronary lesions and facilitate stent implantation. items.title: Beyond the lifestyle paradigm: environmental triggers and susceptible cardiovascular phenotypes
items.abstract: This commentary refers to ‘Air pollution before and during the COVID-19 pandemic: changes in risk of acute myocardial infarction’, by M. Ishii et al., https://doi.org/10.1093/eurheartj/ehag102 and the discussion piece ‘Beyond clinical phenotypes: endotype-specific environmental cardiovascular susceptibility’, by M. Ishii et al., https://doi.org/10.1093/eurheartj/ehag814. We read with interest the nationwide study by Ishii et al.1 on short-term fine particulate matter (PM2.5) exposure and acute myocardial infarction (AMI) before and during the COVID-19 pandemic. The most striking finding, in our view, was not the pollution–AMI association itself but how it behaved across phenotypes: PM2.5-associated risk of myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA) fell during the pandemic, while no comparable change was seen for infarction with obstructive coronary disease.1 This selective attenuation raises a question that extends well beyond this dataset: can a single environmental exposure preferentially trigger different cardiovascular phenotypes, depending on the susceptibility of the individual exposed? MINOCA is not one disease but several—coronary vasospasm, microvascular dysfunction, thromboembolism, spontaneous coronary dissection, and other mechanisms.2 Each pathway could plausibly respond differently to the inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, autonomic imbalance, and prothrombotic tendency that air pollution is known to provoke.3 Read this way, the data from Ishii et al.1 support a susceptibility–trigger–phenotype model: pollution supplies the trigger, an individual's vascular or coronary substrate determines the susceptibility, and the clinical event is the resulting phenotype—a different starting point from treating PM2.5 as a generic risk factor that simply raises AMI incidence across the board.

items.title: Beyond clinical phenotypes: endotype-specific environmental cardiovascular susceptibility
items.abstract: This commentary refers to ‘Air pollution before and during the COVID-19 pandemic: changes in risk of acute myocardial infarction’, by M. Ishii et al., https://doi.org/10.1093/eurheartj/ehag102 and the discussion piece ‘Beyond the lifestyle paradigm: environmental triggers and susceptible cardiovascular phenotypes’, by S. Saeed et al., https://doi.org/10.1093/eurheartj/ehag813. We thank Saeed et al.1 for their thoughtful commentary on our study and for proposing a susceptibility–trigger–phenotype framework for environmental cardio vascular risk. We agree that this perspective may help move the field beyond viewing fine particulate matter (PM2.5) as a uniform cardiovascular risk factor. Our study showed that the association between short-term PM2.5 exposure and acute myocardial infarction varied according to clinical phenotype. Attenuation of the PM2.5-associated risk for myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA) during the COVID-19 pandemic was observed, whereas no significant change was observed in myocardial infarction with obstructive coronary artery disease.2 However, these observational data do not indicate that changes in PM2.5 exposure cause the temporal difference, nor can they identify the mechanisms underlying MINOCA. This distinction is important because MINOCA is an umbrella syndrome encompassing heterogeneous coronary mechanisms, including epicardial spasm, microvascular spasm, spontaneous coronary artery dissection, coronary thromboembolism, and other mechanisms.3

items.title: From individual markers to reformulable processing signatures in hypertension prevention
items.abstract: This commentary refers to ‘Markers of ultra-processed food and incident arterial hypertension in the UK Biobank’, by K. M. Krost et al., https://doi.org/10.1093/eurheartj/ehag614 and the discussion piece ‘Characterizing co-occurrence patterns of potentially disease-relevant markers of ultra-processed food’, by K. M. Krost et al., https://doi.org/10.1093/eurheartj/ehag843. Krost et al.1 should be commended for moving the ultra-processed food debate from a binary label towards ingredient-level markers. In 101 560 UK Biobank participants, they identified four marker-of-ultra-processing (MUP) categories associated with incident arterial hypertension and, importantly, showed that several other categories were not.1 Their key translational opportunity may lie one level above individual MUPs: constructing processing-marker signatures that can be linked to food reformulation. The Marker Likelihood Index (MLI) converts each reported food item into marker-bearing food mass according to the marker’s frequency across matched commercial products.1 Consequently, flavour, colouring agent, sweetener, and varieties of sugar may encode a recurring product phenotype rather than four separable exposures. Supplementary Figure 2 makes this co-occurrence empirically visible.1 The resulting percentage of total food intake represents marker-bearing food exposure rather than the ingested dose of the marker itself: a 50-g portion with an MLI of 0.6 contributes 30 g of marker-bearing food, not 30 g of additive.1 We view these features not as weaknesses, but as an opportunity to ask a more policy-relevant question: which combinations of markers characterize foods whose replacement is associated with lower hypertension risk?

items.title: Characterizing co-occurrence patterns of potentially disease-relevant markers of ultra-processed food
items.abstract: This commentary refers to ‘Markers of ultra-processed food and incident arterial hypertension in the UK Biobank’, by K. M. Krost et al., https://doi.org/10.1093/eurheartj/ehag614, and the Discussion Forum contribution ‘From individual markers to reformulable processing signatures in hypertension prevention’, by Y. Z. Huang, https://doi.org/10.1093/eurheartj/ehag842. We thank Dr. Huang for his interest in our study on markers of ultra-processed food (MUPs) and incident arterial hypertension in the UK Biobank and his thoughtful comments. We agree that an important translational opportunity lies in moving beyond individual MUP analyses towards MUP patterns that can inform food reformulation. As MUPs co-occur within the same foods, associations observed for individual markers may partly reflect shared underlying product characteristics. We therefore consider the proposed investigation of MUP co-occurrence patterns an important direction for future research. An important step towards characterizing these MUP co-occurrences is to define potentially disease-relevant MUPs and distinguish them from MUPs without evidence of adverse health associations. Thus, identifying MUPs that are consistently associated with adverse health outcomes using Cox proportional hazards regression models can provide an important starting point for investigating the biological mechanisms that may underlie these associations. Together with our findings on incident arterial hypertension,1 evidence from two further UK Biobank studies on mortality2 and depression risk3 suggests that added flavour, colouring agent, and sweetener may represent potentially disease-relevant MUPs. Future studies should investigate whether these MUPs are also associated with further adverse health outcomes, including other cardiometabolic diseases and various types of cancer. The next step should include mechanistic studies investigating the pathways by which these disease-relevant MUPs might affect human physiology and health. Randomized controlled crossover trials, building on previous studies investigating the effects of ultra-processed foods (UPF),4 could further characterize these MUPs by comparing otherwise closely matched foods or diets with and without these MUPs and assessing relevant clinical outcomes.

items.title: Familial hypercholesterolaemia and thymic ageing in a Chinese cohort
items.abstract: Background and Aims Lifelong exposure to elevated low-density lipoprotein cholesterol in familial hypercholesterolaemia (FH) patients not only increases the risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, but also affects other organs beyond the cardiovascular system. In a large FH cohort, this study investigated the effects of hypercholesterolaemia on the thymic output and explored whether lipid-lowering therapy can reverse these effects. Methods According to the Dutch Lipid Clinic Network criteria, 562 heterozygous FH patients (236 treatment-naïve, 326 on lipid-lowering therapy) and 295 age-matched healthy controls (HCs) were enrolled. Thymic output was measured by circulating CD4+ recent thymic emigrants (RTEs) with flow cytometry, and T-cell receptor excision circles in sorted naïve CD4+ and CD8+ T cells. Repertoire diversity and clonal expansion were evaluated by T-cell receptor beta sequencing. Results Compared with HCs, treatment-naïve FH patients displayed a significantly reduced percentage of CD4+ RTE among naïve CD4+ T cells, particularly in those aged 18–30 years or carrying highly pathogenic LDLR variants. T-cell receptor excision circle analysis supported reduced thymic output in both CD4+ and CD8+ naïve T cells. Quantified thymic ageing further showed that FH patients reached the median CD4+ RTE percentage of HCs ∼6 years earlier (males: 19.12 vs 25.51 years; females: 19.18 vs 25.58 years). Consistent with reduced thymic output, FH patients showed skewing towards high-frequency T-cell receptor beta clones. Statin-treated FH patients, particularly females, showed higher circulating CD4+ RTE levels than statin-naïve FH patients. Conclusions Hypercholesterolaemia was associated with reduced thymic output, while statin-treated patients showed partially preserved circulating CD4+ RTE levels, supporting integrated metabolic and immunologic strategies for FH management.

items.title: Correction: Fifth Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction (2026): On behalf of the Joint European Society of Cardiology (ESC)/American College of Cardiology (ACC)/American Heart Association (AHA)/World Heart Federation (WHF) Task Force for the Universal Definition of Myocardial InfarctionEndorsed by the European Association for Cardio-Thoracic Surgery (EACTS) and the Society of Thoracic Surgeons (STS)Affirmation of Value by the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions (SCAI)
Acute heart failure in emergency settings
items.abstract: Acute heart failure (AHF) represents a major cause of emergency medical care worldwide and continues to carry a substantial burden of morbidity and mortality despite advances in chronic heart failure management. Most patients with AHF present to emergency departments (EDs), where the first hours of care are critical to determine prognosis. Of these, some have been previously evaluated and treated by prehospital emergency medical services before ED arrival. This consensus document summarizes the current evidence and provides practical advice to emergency physicians for the diagnosis, treatment, and disposition of patients with AHF in these emergency settings (emergency medical services and ED). It emphasizes the importance of a rapid phenotypic classification into acute decompensated heart failure, acute pulmonary oedema, isolated right ventricular failure, or cardiogenic shock, as a key tool to guide early management and triage decisions. It reviews evidence on prehospital and ED management, including the use of biomarkers, imaging, ventilatory support, diuretic and vasodilator strategies, and early initiation or continuation of guideline-directed medical therapy. It also discusses risk stratification and disposition decisions supported by validated tools. Finally, it identifies major knowledge gaps and future research priorities, including pragmatic trials to assess prehospital interventions, biomarker-guided therapy, and early initiation of disease-modifying treatments. Ultimately, this consensus document is aimed to contribute to the improvement of outcomes in AHF.

items.title: Correction to: 2026 ESC Guidelines on cardiac rehabilitation: Developed by the task force on cardiac rehabilitation of the European Society of Cardiology (ESC)Endorsed by the European Society of Physical and Rehabilitation Medicine (ESPRM) and World Organization of Family Doctors (WONCA)
Guidelines on rehabilitation and a focus on lifestyle-related cardiovascular prevention
items.abstract: For the podcast associated with this article, please visit https://academic.oup.com/eurheartj/pages/Podcasts. This Issue starts with an ESC Guidelines article entitled ‘2026 ESC Guidelines on cardiac rehabilitation’, by Maria Bäck from the University of Gothenburg, Sweden, and colleagues.1 These updated practical guidelines establish a comprehensive, patient-centred framework for cardiac rehabilitation, an important form of treatment frequently underutilized in daily clinical practice.2–4 The Issue continues with a focus on Epidemiology, prevention, and healthcare policies. Pregnancy represents a critical period during which the maternal cardiovascular (CV) system adapts to profound haemodynamic and metabolic demands. When these adaptive mechanisms are impaired, adverse pregnancy outcomes (APOs)—including hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, gestational diabetes, pre-term birth, small-for-gestational-age birth, and pregnancy loss—occur.5–8 In a State of the Art Review article entitled ‘Adverse pregnancy outcomes and long-term cardiovascular risk: lifelong connections’, Veronica Giorgione Nunes from St George's University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust in London, UK, and colleagues summarize current evidence with four aims: (i) to quantify the magnitude of CV risk after specific APOs; (ii) to outline shared pathophysiology linking APOs and CV disease (CVD); (iii) to chart the temporal course of the CV legacy from early post-partum CV findings to later organ damage; and (iv) to translate these insights into pragmatic strategies for prevention, covering optimal fourth-trimester care and the system gaps that impede its delivery.9 Extensive epidemiological evidence demonstrates that APOs are not isolated obstetric events but early clinical markers of cardiometabolic dysfunction that identify women at increased risk of coronary artery disease (CAD), heart failure, stroke, chronic kidney disease (CKD), and premature CV mortality. Shared mechanisms include endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, and insulin resistance, establishing a continuum between obstetric complications and later CVD. Early post-partum studies reveal persistent hypertension, adverse cardiac remodelling, and metabolic abnormalities that mediate much of the long-term excess CV risk. These findings redefine the ‘fourth trimester’ as a preventive window in which timely blood pressure surveillance, metabolic screening, and lifestyle optimization can yield durable CV benefit. Integrated cardio-obstetric care models, digital follow-up, and systematic transition to primary care are crucial for maintaining long-term prevention. Addressing persistent gaps in limited provider awareness, fragmented follow-up, and disparities across socially disadvantaged populations remains critical. Recognizing pregnancy complications as indicators of underlying CV vulnerability offers an opportunity to shift prevention upstream and promote lifelong CV health for women. A construct is only as actionable as the diagnostic pathway that supports it. Recent patient-led advocacy and policy initiatives—including the designation of March as Endometriosis Awareness Month—have strengthened public and professional recognition of this debilitating disease and promoted earlier clinical evaluation. In a Viewpoint article entitled ‘Endometriosis as a cardiovascular risk enhancer’, Benjamin Marchandot and Oliver Morel from the University Hospital of Strasbourg, France, aim to highlight endometriosis as a potential CV risk factor in women and propose a practical approach for incorporating it into atherosclerotic CVD (ASCVD) risk assessment and prevention.10 Endometriosis is a chronic, systemic neuroinflammatory disorder affecting an estimated ∼190 million people worldwide (∼1 in 10 women of reproductive age). Convergent epidemiological and mechanistic evidence links endometriosis to increased risk of ASCVD, yet contemporary risk frameworks rarely capture this contribution, and prevention pathways remain inconsistent. In parallel, the diagnostic landscape is shifting; alongside imaging and specialist centres, non-invasive molecular signature-based assays may compress the diagnostic interval from years to days, opening a practical window for earlier CV risk profiling. This viewpoint reframes endometriosis as a sex-specific, non-communicable CV risk enhancer and sets out a pragmatic, testable two-step prevention pathway. Step 1 prioritizes systematic identification and consistent documentation of endometriosis in symptomatic individuals, with explicit risk tagging to trigger CV assessment. Step 2 activates a guideline-aligned prevention strategy: structured baseline assessment; use of existing risk estimation tools with endometriosis documented as a risk enhancer; guideline-based management of traditional and lifestyle-related risk factors; and timed reassessment with escalation where warranted. A coordinated research agenda, spanning phenotypic stratification, risk prediction modelling, pragmatic intervention trials, and health-economic evaluations is outlined to test clinical benefit and scalability before guideline-level adoption. Ambient PM2.5 exposure is a known potent CV risk factor.11–13 Myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA) represents a subtype of acute MI (AMI) distinct from myocardial infarction with obstructive coronary disease (MI-CAD). In a Clinical Research article entitled ‘Air pollution before and during the COVID-19 pandemic: changes in risk of acute myocardial infarction’, Masanobu Ishii from Kumamoto University, Japan, and colleagues investigate changes in the association between short-term exposure to PM2.5 and AMI subtypes following the COVID-19 pandemic.14 Public health measures during the COVID-19 pandemic may have altered exposure patterns, offering a natural experiment. Using data from the nationwide JROAD-DPC database, this study analysed ∼270 000 first-admission AMI patients, including ∼23 000 with MINOCA, between April 2012 and March 2022. A time-stratified case-crossover design with conditional logistic regression estimated the odds ratio (OR) for each 10 μg/m3 increase in PM2.5 exposure at a 2-day lag. The study period was divided into pre-pandemic and post-pandemic phases using 7 April 2020 as the threshold. Sensitivity analyses used alternative pandemic onset dates. Each 10 μg/m3 increase in lag-2 PM2.5 was significantly associated with an increased risk of AMI. Although the ORs for overall AMI and MI-CAD remained largely unchanged between periods, a significant attenuation of the PM2.5-related risk for MINOCA was observed (pre-pandemic OR 1.303; post-pandemic OR 1.230; P for interaction = .017). Sensitivity analyses confirmed these findings. The authors conclude that short-term exposure to PM2.5 is associated with increased risk of AMI. The observed reduction in MINOCA risk following the COVID-19 pandemic suggests that public health interventions aimed at reducing air pollution exposure may reduce CV risk, particularly in specific AMI subtypes. The manuscript is accompanied by an Editorial by Gianluigi Guida, Giandomenico Disabato, and Massimo Piepoli from IRCCS Policlinico San Donato in Milan, Italy.15 These authors note that Ishii et al. must be congratulated for their study which once again has highlighted the significant impact of environmental factors, such as air pollution, on CV health, providing some insights into the implicated pathophysiological mechanisms, and demonstrating the effects of changes in exposure and behaviour. The pandemic provided a unique opportunity to observe these effects, emphasizing the potential for targeted interventions to reduce pollution-related heart disease. The observational nature of the study inherently limits causal interpretation, and residual confounding from unmeasured factors cannot be entirely ruled out. Future research should clarify which behavioural and environmental changes most impact MINOCA risk, explore subtype-specific susceptibilities, assess global applicability, and evaluate the role of co-exposures. Tailored interventions could offer significant benefits, especially for populations most sensitive to environmental triggers. Physical exercise is an important protective factor.16–18 While vigorous physical activity (VPA) is known to provide greater health benefits per unit time than moderate activity, the spectrum of these benefits across different chronic diseases and the relative importance of physical activity (PA) intensity vs volume remain unclear. In a Clinical Research article entitled ‘Volume vs intensity of physical activity and risk of cardiovascular and non-cardiovascular chronic diseases’, Jiehua Wei from Central South University in Changsha, China, and colleagues examine associations between the proportion of VPA (%VPA) relative to the total volume of PA and the incidence of multiple chronic disease outcomes.19 This prospective population-based cohort study included ∼96 400 participants (mean age 62 years, women: 56%) with device-measured data (wrist-worn accelerometers) and ∼375 700 participants (mean age 56 years, women: 52%) with self-reported PA data (IPAQ) from the UK Biobank. Main outcomes included incidence of eight chronic diseases: major adverse CV events (MACE), atrial fibrillation (AFib), type 2 diabetes (T2D), immune-mediated inflammatory diseases, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), chronic respiratory diseases (CRD), CKD, and dementia, as well as all-cause mortality. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals. In the device-measured data, non-linear inverse dose–response relationships were observed between %VPA and all outcomes (all P < .001), and these patterns remained consistent across strata of total PA volume. In multivariable models adjusted for total PA volume, participants with >4% VPA had 29%–61% lower risks of these outcomes compared with those with 0% VPA. Joint analyses and population attributable fraction revealed distinct disease-specific patterns: immune-mediated inflammatory diseases showed very strong intensity dependence with minimal contribution from PA volume (20% for intensity vs 1% for volume), while MACE (17.8% vs 6%), AFib (16.2% vs 5%), CRD (21% vs 5.6%), and dementia (32% vs 8.1%) demonstrated intensity predominance with modest contribution from PA volume, and T2D (27% vs 17.7%), MASLD (22% vs 16.6%), CKD (23% vs 15.3%), and all-cause mortality (31% vs 14%) showed more balanced contributions from both intensity and volume (Figure 1). Structured Graphical Abstract19 The authors conclude that a higher %VPA, independent of the volume of total activity, is inversely associated with eight major chronic diseases and all-cause mortality. Intensity consistently demonstrates a higher preventive potential than total PA volume. These findings support, whenever possible, prioritizing higher intensity activities in clinical and public health interventions aimed at preventing non-communicable diseases. The manuscript is accompanied by an Editorial by Fabian Schwendinger, Arno Schmidt-Trucksäss, and Henner Hanssen from the University of Basel, Switzerland.20 The authors underscore that across studies, a consistent finding emerges: higher intensity PA is associated with meaningful reductions in multiple health outcomes. Yet translation into routine clinical practice remains challenging. While intensity has become an increasingly refined construct in research, its implementation in primary and secondary prevention remains limited. While accumulating evidence supports PA intensity as a central component of prescription, most clinical recommendations continue to prioritize total PA rather than explicitly prescribing vigorous intensity as a primary therapeutic variable. Ultimately, PA and exercise prescription rely on shared decision-making. Primarily, recommendations to engage in PA need to match the fitness, health status, and biological age of the individual. For older frail individuals, for example, repeated sit-to-stand exercises may represent high relative intensity, whereas brisk or fast walking, or their combination as interval-type exercise, may be the most efficient trigger for cardiometabolic adaptations and improved individual health outcomes. This is because, even if the absolute intensity does not exceed the vigorous threshold (i.e. 6 METs), the intensity expressed relative to a person's exercise capacity may still be vigorous. In principle, the rule of thumb ‘the more the merrier’ for PA volume applies as a classic dose–response relationship, and potential side effects of higher doses of regular daily PA may be negligible. To simplify matters, any prescription of PA volume according to the general recommendation is an important cornerstone of a multi-modal treatment strategy to reduce the burden of CVD as well as overall chronic non-communicable disease. However, according to Wei et al., prioritizing higher intensity PA over volume, especially in the prevention of immune-mediated inflammatory disease, CRD, CVD, and dementia, may be key to achieve optimal health outcomes. This, however, must be shown in large, population-based randomized controlled trials. An optimal diet is important in CV prevention.21–23 Preservative food additives are substances added to prolong the shelf life of packaged products, protecting them against deterioration caused by microorganisms and/or growth of pathogens, and alterations caused by oxidation, such as fat rancidity and colour changes. In a Clinical Research article entitled ‘Preservative food additives, hypertension, and cardiovascular diseases: the NutriNet-Santé study’, Anaïs Hasenböhler from Sorbonne Paris Nord University and Paris Cité University, France, and colleagues aim to quantify the cumulative time-dependent exposures to total preservatives, total non-antioxidant and total antioxidant food additives and specific substances and examine their associations with the incidence of CVD and coronary heart and hypertension, in a prospective cohort with The associations between exposure to these and incidence of and CVD were in the NutriNet-Santé cohort were using repeated to including to food additives was multiple and assays in food between cumulative time-dependent exposures to food additives during and outcomes were using Cox 400 participants were included age with a of The of total substances by at non-antioxidant were associated with higher of higher vs lower and CVD while total antioxidant were associated with higher incidence of of the individual food additives by at of the study eight were associated with higher incidence of and with higher incidence of CVD, after multiple test The authors conclude that multiple associations between exposure to food additives used in and higher incidence of or CVD are observed in this prospective research is to into the underlying these data for the of the use of these additives to The manuscript is accompanied by an Editorial by and from IRCCS in The authors note that the NutriNet-Santé findings should not be as a that CVD, but provide a consistent in with mechanistic studies, and of for exposure be this study that specific food rather than on or a in CV is added to rather than only their may mechanisms linking diet to cardiometabolic disease.
