items.title: Beyond the gradient: patient-reported outcomes with aficamten in obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
Sex-based differences in chronic heart failure: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
items.abstract: Background Sex-based disparities in patient enrolment and treatment effects in heart failure (HF) randomized controlled trials (RCTs) have been reported. We aim to systematically analyse sex-based enrolment and treatment effect differences in HF RCTs over time. Methods RCTs enrolling patients with chronic HF were systematically searched on PubMed-MEDLINE. Eligible trials included pharmacological or device-based interventions with a hard primary endpoint (mortality and hospitalization) and reporting enrolment of women. Sex-specific treatment effects (hazard ratio [HR] or risk ratio [RR]) were extracted. Meta-analyses were performed using random-effects models, and pre-specified subgroup analyses were performed. Results A total of 56 RCTs (39 drug, 17 device) were included. The pooled proportion of women enrolment was 27.0% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 22.0%–32.4%) in drug trials and 25.3% (95% CI: 21.0%–29.9%) in device trials. Women were more underrepresented in HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) than in HF with preserved EF (HFpEF) trials (21.0% vs 49.6%, P < .001). Among drug trials reporting sex-specific effects, the pooled sex interaction for RCTs reporting HR was 0.94 (95%CI 0.89–1.01) and RR was 0.81 (95% CI 0.68–0.96), suggesting potentially greater benefit for women. No interaction was observed between HFrEF and HFpEF trials (HR: P = 0.44; RR: P = .95). The pooled interaction estimate on event counts was 0.90 (95%CI 0.84–0.96). For devices, the pooled sex interaction for RCTs reporting HR was 1.05 (95% CI 0.90–1.22) and RR was 0.68 (95% CI 0.50–0.93). Conclusion Women remain underrepresented in HF RCTs. Sex-stratified analyses suggest a potentially greater relative benefit of drug intervention in women, which might inform future RCTs. Further studies are required to investigate the mechanisms of these differences.

items.title: GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment and cardiovascular outcomes following aortic valve replacement: a nationwide observational study
items.abstract: Aims Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists reduce major adverse cardiovascular events among patients with diabetes, overweight and obesity. Whether these benefits extend to patients undergoing aortic valve replacement (AVR) for severe aortic stenosis (AS) remains unknown. Thus, we investigated the association between GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment and cardiovascular outcomes after AVR. Methods Nationwide population-based cohort study including consecutive patients with severe AS undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation or surgical aortic valve replacement in Western Denmark between January 2016 and April 2022. Patients were followed until death, emigration, crossover, or end of follow-up on 12 May 2026. Propensity score-matching was performed to balance confounding. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, or aortic valve reoperation. Secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, and aortic valve reoperation, with analyses accounting for the competing risk of death. Results Among 5259 eligible patients undergoing AVR, 292 propensity score-matched patients were included in the final analyses. During a mean follow-up of 4.8 ± 2.4 years, GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment was associated with a lower risk of the primary composite outcome compared with controls [hazard ratios (HR) .69, 95% confidence intervals (CI) .50–.96, P = .029]. GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment was also associated with lower risk of all-cause mortality (HR .66, 95% CI .46–.95, P = .025). In competing risk analyses accounting for death, lower risks were observed for heart failure hospitalization (HR .67, 95% CI .48–.93, P = .018), and aortic valve reoperation (HR .69, 95% CI .49–.98, P = .037). Conclusion Treatment with GLP-1 receptor agonists was associated with lower risk of cardiovascular outcomes, including mortality, following AVR among patients with severe AS.

items.title: Management of Heart transplant recipients for the non Heart Transplant health care provider. A Clinical Consensus Statement of the Heart Failure Association (HFA) and the Association of Cardiovascular Nursing & Allied Professions (ACNAP) of the ESC
items.abstract: Heart transplantation (HTx) remains the gold standard treatment for selected patients with advanced heart failure and survival after transplantation has substantially improved over recent decades. As a consequence, the number of long-term HTx recipients continues to increase, and these patients are now frequently encountered in routine practice outside specialized transplant centers. Their management remains complex due to the use of chronic immunosuppression, transplant-specific complications, and a growing burden of comorbidities in the perspective of increasing longevity. Non-transplant cardiologists, general practitioners, and other healthcare professionals are therefore increasingly involved in their care but often have limited experience of post-transplant management. This clinical consensus statement from the Heart Failure Association (HFA) and the Association of Cardiovascular Nursing & Allied Professions (ACNAP) of the ESC provides practical support and a structured framework for healthcare providers involved in the care of HTx recipients outside dedicated transplant centers. The document reviews key aspects of post-transplant management, including outlining principles of care according to time from transplantation, essential knowledge around immunosuppressive therapy and drug monitoring, recognition and initial management of rejection, infection prophylaxis and treatment, and surveillance of long-term complications such as cardiac allograft vasculopathy, malignancy, chronic kidney disease, and metabolic disorders. In addition, specific clinical situations frequently encountered in practice—including fertility and pregnancy, non-cardiac surgery, rehabilitation, and palliative care—are discussed. Particular emphasis is placed on the organization of shared-care models between transplant centers and community providers and on identifying clinical scenarios requiring early referral. Through providing practical recommendations and a structured framework for follow-up, this document aims to support non-specialist clinicians in the safe management of HTx recipients and to facilitate timely collaboration with transplant centers.

items.title: Sex Differences in Heart Failure Treatment: A Signal Worth Pursuing?
Short-term safety, feasibility, and performance of a novel soft robotic biventricular mechanical circulatory support device avoiding blood contact – The MISSION reBEAT trial
items.abstract: Aims Mechanical Circulatory Support (MCS) remains limited in advanced heart failure due to blood-contact complications and the absence of biventricular support. We report the first prospective clinical trial of a novel soft-robotic, biventricular, pulsatile technology placed externally around the heart without blood contact, designed to deliver individualized cardiac assistance (reBEAT®, AdjuCor GmbH, Munich, Germany). Methods and Results The system was temporarily applied in 10 end-stage heart failure patients immediately before elective LVAD implantation. Devices were custom-manufactured using preoperative CT scans to match individual cardiac anatomy. Safety, feasibility, and effects on haemodynamics were evaluated. Implantation was rapid (3±2 min), demonstrating procedural feasibility. We observed two procedure-related adverse events while no device- or procedure-related severe adverse events occurred. Absence of new ECG abnormalities, and no tissue injury confirmed safety. An iterative assessment on haemodynamics provided key insights into individualized cardio-circulatory support. While device presence reduced preload dependent haemodynamics in some patients, low average support pressures of 65–66 mmHg produced variable improvements towards baseline, predominantly on the pressure signal: mean arterial pressure (MAP; 67.5 ± 10.6 vs. 76.2 ± 11.7 mmHg, p<0.01), stroke work (SW; 347.8 ± 118.2 vs. 434.1 ± 131.0 mJ, p<0.01), and cardiac power output (CPO; 407.9 ± 108.2 vs. 503.7 ± 116.2 mW, p<0.01). Additionally, effects were observed on atrioventricular valve function and interventricular balance, which were not significant. Conclusion This soft-robotic biventricular MCS platform provides short term evidence of a safe and feasible approach to pulsatile biventricular support without blood contact. Significant increases in MAP, CPO, and SW towards baseline indicate functional effects. Continuous device-driven workflow improvement is mandatory and further data are required to refine individualized optimization strategies. This technology may offer a novel biventricular assist modality. Its reduced complexity may enable broader adaption for both temporary and durable support. Avoiding blood contact and enabling balanced biventricular assistance will be central drivers of its continued clinical development.

items.title: DPP3-positive circulatory shock: from targetable ICU endotype to Horizon Europe precision-therapy trial
Increasing cold ischemic time in mouse kidneys primes renal proximal tubular cells to undergo mitochondrial-induced necroptosis following transplantation
items.abstract: We developed a C57Bl/6 mouse kidney model of cold storage in UW solution prior to transplantation to assess cellular injury during cold ischemic time (CIT). Compared to warm storage, cold storage reduced proximal tubule cell (PTC) death assessed by terminal deoxynucleotidase dUTP nick end labeling (TUNEL). Many PTCs showed increases in nuclear phospho-mixed lineage kinase domain-like protein (pMLKL) with concomitant nuclear swelling and increases in phospho-receptor interacting protein kinase (pRIPK)3, Z-DNA, and Z-DNA binding protein (ZBP)1 but not phospho-RIPK1, caspase 3 cleavage or TUNEL staining. Nuclear pMLKL was reduced by small molecule Bax inhibitor, BAI1 suggesting a link between mitochondrial damage and pMLKL activation. Kidneys subjected to 16-24h CIT before syngeneic transplant showed more extensive PTC death, sloughing of remaining PTCs, TUNEL staining, cytosolic pMLKL, kidney injury molecule 1 (KIM1) expression, and infiltration of neutrophils and monocytes at the cortical medullary boundary compared to kidneys transplanted without CIT. Kidneys with prolonged CIT transplanted into nephrectomized syngeneic recipients had elevated BUN and recipient death. Bax inhibition during CIT reduced PTC injury but not immune infiltration, BUN, or improve survival. Overall, these results indicate that CIT causes Z-DNA/ZBP1 activation which primes PTCs through pMLKL for necroptosis following reperfusion of transplanted kidneys.

items.title: Successful bilateral lung transplantation in a patient with severe pulmonary blastomycosis
items.abstract: Severe pulmonary blastomycosis may progress to acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) necessitating prolonged extracorporeal support, and ultimately lead to irreversible pulmonary injury. Whether these patients should proceed to lung transplantation remains controversial. We report a 38-year-old man with type 2 diabetes mellitus who developed fulminant pulmonary blastomycosis following environmental exposure in Ontario, Canada. Despite prolonged treatment with liposomal amphotericin B and azole therapy, his course was complicated by respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation, and prolonged venovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO), with concomitant recurrent ventilator-associated bacterial pneumonias and treatment-related nephrotoxicity. Although microbiologic markers gradually improved, including declining urinary Blastomyces antigen levels and negative respiratory fungal cultures, lung function recovery failed to occur. Ongoing uncertainty persisted regarding uncontrolled infection versus irreversible pulmonary injury. The patient ultimately underwent successful bilateral lung transplantation while receiving antifungal therapy. Post-transplant recovery progressed slowly but smoothly, with liberation from ECMO and no evidence of recurrent fungal disease. This case suggests that concern for invasive fungal infection persistence should not automatically preclude lung transplantation as a means of survival for irreversible lung injury when assessment supports favorable microbiologic control.

items.title: Corrigendum to West Nile virus encephalitis posttransplantation: A case report and literature review [American Journal of Transplantation, Date: January 2026, Page: S15, Volume: Volume 26, Issue 1, Supplement 1]
Associations between OPOs’ Responses to Scrutiny about Out of Sequence Allocation and Changes in Deceased Donor Kidney Transplantation
items.abstract: U.S. organ procurement organizations allocate select deceased donor kidneys "out-of-sequence" (AOOS) by offering a kidney judged at risk of nonuse to a chosen center instead of according to the in-sequence allocation list. In 2025, AOOS practices were scrutinized by the media (February 26: high profile news article) and regulators (August 5: OPTN email deeming AOOS "not consistent with OPTN policy"). Using OPTN data from 1/1/24-2/26/25 ("pre-article") and 8/6/25-2/28/26 ("post-email"), we studied the association between OPO-level changes in AOOS and kidney transplant activity. Kidney transplant volume fell by 7% for the 33 OPOs with large AOOS reductions but rose by 1% for the other 22 OPOs, a statistically significant difference in changes (p=0.0007). Though DCD kidney recovery volume rose by just 1% for large-AOOS-drop OPOs, it rose by 14% among other OPOs (interaction p<0.0001). By contrast, cross-era changes in the probability of offered and recovered kidneys being transplanted did not differ between OPO groups. The non-use rate among recovered kidneys did not increase, suggesting any negative effects of restricting AOOS on kidney transplant volume were mediated by fewer kidney recoveries, not by increased difficulty in placing recovered kidneys. Scrutiny into AOOS practices may have led to fewer kidney transplants.

items.title: First Series of Purely Robotic Liver Transplantation in Children
items.abstract: Fully robotic liver transplantation, as defined by pure robotic donor hepatectomy as well as pure robotic liver transplantation, remains underexploited in pediatric recipients because of limited abdominal space and the absence of pediatric-specific robotic systems. To our knowledge, this study reports the first series of robotic liver transplantation in pediatric recipients. Consecutive pediatric recipients that underwent robotic liver transplantation between 30 May and 9 February 2026 using the DaVinci®Xi Surgical System were included. Seven pediatric robotic liver transplants were performed, including 6 (85.7%) partial graft implantations fully robotic and 1 (14.3%) whole liver implant via domino transplantation, retrieved with the open approach from a separate pediatric donor and implanted robotically. Median recipient age and body mass index were 12.5 years and 17 kg/m 2 , respectively. Median operation duration was 458min, median warm ischemia time 46min, and median blood loss 500 ml. Major postoperative complications (Grade≥3a) occurred in three recipients. No graft loss or mortality occurred during follow-up with a median of 15.8 months. Purely robotic liver transplantation in pediatric recipients is feasible in centers with extensive robotic liver surgery and pediatric transplantation experience. Further studies are required to evaluate long-term outcomes and define the role of robotic transplantation in pediatric patients.

items.title: Best Practices for Identifying In situ Normothermic Regional Perfusion and Ex Situ Machine Perfusion in OPTN/SRTR Data: A Validation Study
items.abstract: The Scientific Registry of Transplant Recipients(SRTR) is the primary source of national transplant data in the United States; however, advanced perfusion techniques, including normothermic regional perfusion(NRP) and normothermic machine perfusion(NMP), are not consistently captured. We performed a multicenter validation study comparing SRTR-derived algorithms with confirmed reference standard cases from Mayo Clinic Florida, Mayo Clinic Arizona, and Tampa General Hospital. Algorithms were developed to identify NRP, in-transit NMP, and back-to-base NMP using existing SRTR variables. Performance was assessed by sensitivity, specificity,positive predictive value,negative predictive value,and overall accuracy. The validation cohort included 310 NRP, 1,313 in-transit NMP, and 564 back-to-base NMP cases. The NRP algorithm demonstrated 90.0% sensitivity, 99.9% specificity, and 98.7% overall accuracy. Both in-transit and back-to-base NMP algorithms demonstrated sensitivities and specificities exceeding 90%, with overall accuracies exceeding 93%. Most misclassifications resulted from inaccurate donor death or clamp times for NRP or incorrect machine perfusion coding for NMP. The proposed SRTR-based algorithms identify NRP, in-transit NMP, and back-to-base NMP with high accuracy, providing a practical framework for national registry studies of advanced liver perfusion. Although modest misclassification remains, these validated algorithms support registry-based research while emphasizing the need for improved prospective capture of advanced perfusion techniques.

Long-term patient and graft survival for children and young adults after kidney transplantation and re-transplantation – results from the ERA Registry
items.abstract: Long-term outcomes after kidney re-transplantation in patients with childhood-onset kidney replacement therapy (KRT) are poorly characterized. Using European Renal Association Registry data, we studied 12,623 patients who started KRT before age 20 years and received one (n = 11,078), two (n = 2,962) or three (n = 718) kidney transplants (KTs) between 1978 and 2019. In this descriptive study, 5-, 10- and 15-year patient survival was 97, 94 and 90 % after first, 97, 95, 94 % after second and 96, 94, 92 % after third KT; corresponding graft survival was 79, 63, 50 %, 69, 52, 38 %, and 67, 51, 38 %, respectively. After first KT, mortality and graft failure risks were lower after pre-emptive transplantation (adjusted hazard ratio: 0.66 [95% CI 0.54-0.80] and 0.89 [0.82-0.97], respectively) and after living donor (LD) transplantation (0.71 [0.61-0.83] and 0.76 [0.70-0.81], respectively). Additionally, graft failure risk was higher between ages 10-24 years, and for patients with glomerulonephritis, metabolic diseases or recurrent nephropathies, and females. In re-transplants, LD and pre-emptive KTs (particularly for second KT) and prior graft survival > 5 years were associated with reduced graft failure. Overall, LD, pre-emptive transplantation, and durable prior grafts were associated with the best outcomes.

items.title: The Global Lung Initiative Race-neutral Equations and Lower Limits of Normal Refine Baseline Lung Allograft Dysfunction Risk Stratification after Lung Transplantation
items.abstract: Baseline lung allograft dysfunction (BLAD) contextualises peak post-transplant lung function, but the prognostic impact of GLI-2012 versus GLI-2022 and respective 80% predicted versus LLN classification remains unclear. In 1283 adult bilateral first lung transplant recipients from three European centres, baseline FEV 1 was defined as the mean of the two highest post-transplant values at one year after transplantation or beyond, with corresponding FVC values. Percent-predicted values and LLN were calculated using GLI-2012 and GLI-2022, and subnormal lung function was evaluated for graft survival, CLAD-free survival, and survival after CLAD diagnosis using Kaplan-Meier and adjusted Cox models. GLI-2022 classified fewer patients as below normal than GLI-2012. Using the 80% threshold, 412 patients (32%) were classified as BLAD by GLI-2022, while 112 (9%) were reclassified from BLAD to No BLAD compared with GLI-2012. Using LLN, 300 patients (23%) were Below LLN by GLI-2022, while 146 (11%) were reclassified from Below to Above LLN. Outcomes after normality reclassification varied by endpoint. Persistent BLAD and Below LLN were associated with worse graft and CLAD-free outcomes, with risk further refined by FEV 1 /FVC impairment patterns and BLAD severity. These findings support BLAD's prognostic relevance and the importance of using race-neutral equations and LLN-based definitions after transplantation.

items.title: Staged acellular perfusion, rewarming, and seamless transition to blood-based normothermic machine perfusion of the kidney: a paired porcine study
Outside Front Cover
Reply to 'Comment on “Effectiveness of respiratory syncytial virus vaccination in solid organ transplant recipients in the United States'
Impact of Donor Obesity on Outcomes in Living Donor Liver Transplantation: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
items.abstract: Background. Living donor liver transplantation increasingly faces the question of whether otherwise healthy candidates with a body mass index ≥30 kg/m 2 can be safely accepted. Available evidence is uneven: large registry datasets sit alongside heterogeneous single-center series, none quantifying the risk accepted by the donors themselves. We therefore synthesized contemporary comparative evidence in living donor liver transplantation, evaluating donor obesity against donor, recipient, and graft outcomes. Methods. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Cochrane Library, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar from January 2000 to June 30, 2026, for comparative cohorts of living liver donors reporting donor and recipient outcomes by donor body mass index (≥30 versus <30 kg/m 2 ). Random-effects meta-analysis used restricted maximum likelihood with Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman 95% confidence intervals (CIs); risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed with Risk Of Bias In Nonrandomized Studies of Interventions and Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation. Results. Nine comparative cohorts comprising 6652 donors from North America, Europe, and Asia were included. Donor obesity was not associated with overall complications (risk ratio [RR], 1.09; 95% CI, 0.89-1.34; P = 0.31) or major complications (RR, 1.02; 95% CI, 0.62-1.67; P = 0.93). However, obese donors had higher rates of wound complications (RR, 2.05; 95% CI, 1.25-3.37; P = 0.012) and hospital readmission (RR, 1.34; 95% CI, 1.07-1.69; P = 0.026). Recipient 1-y patient survival, graft survival, and biliary complications were comparable. Conclusions. In carefully screened candidates, obesity alone should not preclude living liver donation. The excess wound morbidity and readmission argue for enhanced prophylaxis and surveillance after discharge rather than for donor exclusion.

items.title: Are we Asking the Right Questions When Assessing Glomerular Filtration Rate in Living Kidney Donors?
Prolonged Donor Warm Ischemia in Pure Laparoscopic Donor Right Hepatectomy Is Associated With Increased Recipient Biliary Stricture Risk: A Retrospective Cohort Study
items.abstract: Background. Pure laparoscopic donor right hepatectomy has been increasingly adopted because of its minimally invasive nature and established donor safety. However, its impact on recipient biliary complications remains uncertain. This study aimed to evaluate biliary outcomes after pure laparoscopic donor right hepatectomy using accumulated single-surgeon experience and assess the effect of donor warm ischemic time (DWIT). Methods. We reviewed 264 living donor liver transplantations performed by a single surgeon between 2011 and 2023. Donor hepatectomies were categorized as open (group O; n = 103) or laparoscopic, which was subdivided into early (group EL; n = 49) and late (group LL; n = 112) periods. All recipients were ABO-compatible, underwent duct-to-duct reconstruction, and were followed up for ≥1 y. DWIT was defined as the interval between hepatic artery ligation and cold perfusion. The primary outcome was biliary strictures requiring intervention. Results. Biliary stricture-free survival did not differ significantly between groups ( P = 0.278). Receiver operating characteristic analysis identified a DWIT cutoff of 12.5 min as a potential reference point for increased biliary stricture risk (area under the curve, 0.543; P = 0.043). In the multivariate analysis, DWIT ≥13 min was an independent predictor (hazard ratio, 1.88; P = 0.020). Conclusions. Prolonged DWIT appears to increase the risk of recipient biliary strictures, suggesting that minimizing DWIT in laparoscopic donor hepatectomy could help optimize outcomes.

items.title: Deciphering Myocardial Energy Metabolism in the Transplanted Heart
Immunosuppression and Long-term Survival After Single Living-donor Lobar Lung Transplantation From the Same Donor as Prior Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation: An All-Japan Study
items.abstract: Background. Single living-donor lobar lung transplantation (LDLLT) from the same donor as prior hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) represents a unique immunologic setting because of donor-cell chimerism. However, data regarding immunosuppressive management and long-term outcomes in this setting remain limited. Methods. We conducted a retrospective multicenter observational study of all patients in Japan who underwent single LDLLT from the same donor as in their prior HSCT. Between November 2006 and December 2024, 9 patients underwent this procedure at 5 centers. Results. All recipients received immunosuppressive therapy for at least 3 mo after LDLLT. During follow-up, immunosuppression was successfully discontinued in 3 patients, whereas the remaining 6 were maintained on individualized reduced-dose maintenance immunosuppression. One patient died 39 mo after LDLLT, with respiratory dysfunction presumed to be associated with severe malnutrition. At a median follow-up of 154 mo for the entire cohort, 8 patients were alive with acceptable graft function. Conclusions. In this highly selected case series, acceptable long-term survival was observed after single LDLLT from the same donor as prior HSCT under reduced immunosuppression, and immunosuppression was successfully withdrawn in 3 patients.

items.title: Meta-analysis of short-term clinical and survival outcomes of full-left-full-right split liver transplantation for two recipients: Erratum
Universal Prophylaxis or Preemptive Treatment for Trypanosoma cruzi–Seropositive Donors: Comparing Strategies Requires Comparable Endpoints
National Evaluation of the Updated ISHLT Early Graft Dysfunction Framework in Adult Heart Transplantation: Diagnostic Migration, Attrition, and Prognostic Implications
items.abstract: Background. The International Society for Heart and Lung Transplantation recently published a revised consensus on graft dysfunction after heart transplantation, introducing substantial modifications, including a shift toward more stringent conjunctive physiologic criteria. How these changes affect disease incidence, diagnostic migration, and prognostic interpretation when applied to a national registry remains unknown. Methods. Using adult heart transplant data from the United Network for Organ Sharing (September 2023 to June 2025), we applied the previous primary graft dysfunction (PGD) and updated early graft dysfunction (EGD) criteria with registry-adapted operationalization, quantified diagnostic migration between frameworks, and compared post-transplant outcomes across reclassified groups using Kaplan–Meier analyses. Results. Among 2482 recipients, left ventricular dysfunction was identified in 334 (13.5%) under the previous PGD framework versus 11 (0.4%) under the updated EGD framework, representing a 96.7% relative reduction. Only 8 cases retained identical severity grading across both frameworks. Most discordant cases failed to meet hemodynamic criteria despite a left ventricular ejection fraction ≤40%. Notably, 184 recipients previously classified as severe PGD-left ventricular (LV) no longer met EGD-LV criteria yet had significantly higher mortality than recipients without graft dysfunction (20.1% versus 6.2%; P < 0.001). Right ventricular (RV) dysfunction incidence changed modestly (PGD-RV: 32 [1.3%]; EGD-RV: 28 [1.1%]). Conclusions. The updated EGD framework reclassified most previous PGD-LV cases as non-EGD, yet many reclassified recipients remained at elevated risk for graft failure and mortality. These findings reveal a substantial gap between the updated consensus criteria and current registry data, driven largely by failure to satisfy concurrent physiologic criteria required for EGD-LV classification.

items.title: Clinical Outcomes of Patients With Inflammatory Bowel Disease After Liver Transplantation for Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
items.abstract: Background. The clinical course of primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC)-associated inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) after liver transplantation (LTx) varies significantly across studies. This meta-analysis aims to provide a comprehensive estimation of incidence rates (IR) for IBD-related outcomes and PSC recurrence. Methods. Online databases (January 2000-June 2025) were searched for studies on PSC patients with or without IBD at LTx. Studies reporting posttransplant outcomes of interest were included. The pooled IR were calculated with the “meta” package (R Studio [V.4.3.2]) using a random effects model. Results. A total of 34 studies (3828 patients; 67% with IBD at transplantation) were included. The IR of preexiting IBD exacerbation was 36.1 per 1000 person-years (95% confidence intervals [CI], 23.0-56.5). Medically refractory IBD requiring colectomy occurred at an IR of 12.4 per 1000 person-years (95% CI, 8.9-17.4). The IRs of colorectal neoplasia and advanced neoplasia were 10.3 (95% CI, 6.4-16.7) and 7.7 (95% CI, 5.6-10.7) per 1000 person-years, respectively. Among posttransplant PSC-only patients, the IR of newly diagnosed IBD was 20.0 (95% CI, 12.0-33.4). PSC recurrence occurred more frequently in PSC-IBD patients (31.9; 95% CI, 25.0-40.5) than in PSC-only patients (21.4; 95% CI, 11.3-40.6), corresponding to an incidence rate ratio of 2.16 (95% CI, 1.72-2.72; P < 0.001). Conclusions. After LTx for PSC, patients remain at substantial risk of colorectal neoplasia and de novo IBD. PSC-IBD is associated with a higher risk of disease recurrence. These findings support continued endoscopic surveillance and close monitoring of IBD activity.

items.title: A Single Amino Acid Polymorphism Within the α2 Domain of HLA-DQα Regulates the Assembly and Expression of HLA DQ Alleles and the Potential Clinical Impact
items.abstract: Background. Single antigen bead testing is currently accepted as standard practice for evaluating HLA alloantibodies. However, it is well established that the expression of HLA antigens, on beads, is not representative of actual cellular expression. It is well recognized that the cellular surface expression of certain HLA loci are expressed at relatively low levels. As such, single antigen bead data may overrepresent the impact of HLA antibodies for certain loci. Importantly, for clinical assessments, the cell surface expression of target donor HLA antigens is not routinely considered unless it is a known null allele. Methods. Using a panel of variably reactive DQ4 allosera, we have evaluated DQ4 antigen assembly and surface expression on cell lines and in transfectants carrying DQ4 variants. Results. A single amino acid change at residue 137 in the α2 domain of the DQα chain can significantly affect the stability of the αβ heterodimer and result in the reduced surface expression of the affected DQ antigens, resulting in changes in anti-HLA antibody reactivity. Conclusions. A single amino acid residue in the DQα chain can influence the expression of a DQ4 molecule. Importantly, such surface expression variability does significantly impact allo-antibody reactivity. As a result, amino acid sequence variations in the α2 and β2 domains of the HLA class II serological groups and alleles within serological groups should be further investigated to understand the scope of allelic expression variability. Identifying low surface expressing HLA antigens/alleles might facilitate the understanding of certain discordant clinical observations.

items.title: Effect of Kidney Allocation Policy Changes and Organ Donor Hospital Geographic Location on Deceased Donor Kidney Nonuse
items.abstract: Background. Deceased donor kidney recovery and transplantation is a multistep, time-sensitive process, and recovering organs from donors in distant regions may pose logistical challenges. The effect of donor hospital location on kidney utilization outcomes, and whether allocation policy modifies this effect, remains unknown. Methods. We used Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network data to assemble a cohort of deceased kidney donors recovered between January 1, 2010, and December 31, 2024. We categorized the cohort into 3 eras based on allocation policy: before kidney allocation system (pre-KAS) in January 1, 2010–December 4, 2014, December 5, 2014–March 14, 2021 (KAS), and March 15, 2021–December 31, 2024 (KAS250). Our main exposures included estimated driving time, categorized into quartiles, between organ procurement organization (OPO) headquarters and donor hospital, and the allocation era. Results. The final cohort comprised 153 551 deceased kidney donors. The median travel time from OPO headquarters to hospitals was 41 min (interquartile range, 15.1–111.8). In contrast to our hypothesis, nonuse of kidneys from donors in the farthest quartile (versus the closest) was lower when compared with the nearest quartile (odds ratio, 0.94; 95% confidence interval, 0.90-0.98). The adjusted odds ratio of kidney nonuse was slightly higher in KAS250 (odds ratio, 1.03 versus KAS; 95% confidence interval, 1-1.06), but this decreased by 2024 to its lowest level since 2010. Conclusions. In summary, the geographic location and driving time between the donor hospital and the OPO headquarters were not associated with an increased risk of kidney nonuse. The adjusted odds ratio of kidney nonuse continues to decline and is at the lowest level since 2010.

items.title: On the Transplant List Waiting for Godot: Survival Benefit of High KDPI Kidneys
From Phenotypes to Trajectories: Rethinking Risk Stratification in Heart Transplantation
How I Do It: Managing Human Parvovirus B19 Infections in Solid Organ Transplant Recipients
Myocardial External Efficiency and Energetic Adaptation After Heart Transplantation: An Exploratory Study
items.abstract: Background. Mitochondrial dysfunction and impaired myocardial energetics may contribute to graft dysfunction after heart transplantation (HTX). We aimed to characterize early posttransplant myocardial external efficiency (MEE) and its relationship with mitochondrial capacity. Methods. In this prospective single-center study, 22 HTX recipients underwent [ 11 C]acetate positron emission tomography, echocardiography, biomarker testing, and high-resolution respirometry of endomyocardial biopsies once between week 1 and 3 and at 6 mo post-HTX. Temporal changes in positron emission tomography–derived MEE, cardiac output, and myocardial oxygen consumption were evaluated within patients and compared with those of 20 control participants. Mitochondrial capacity was assessed only in HTX recipients. Results. MEE increased from 18 ± 5% to 21 ± 5% at 6 mo post-HTX ( P = 0.003) but remained lower than in control participants (26 ± 6%, P < 0.0001). Cardiac output, myocardial oxygen consumption, and mitochondrial oxidative capacity did not change significantly over time. At 6 mo, both MEE and mitochondrial oxidative capacity correlated with left-ventricular global longitudinal strain ( r = –0.49, P = 0.002; r = –0.58, P = 0.010, respectively). Furthermore, MEE was inversely associated with troponin I ( r = –0.49, P = 0.030) and N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide ( r = –0.35, P = 0.029). Conclusions. MEE improved significantly from 1–3 wk to 6 mo after HTX. Both MEE and mitochondrial respiratory function were associated with left-ventricular contractile performance. Overall, these findings suggest alterations in myocardial energetics during early graft recovery and support a link between oxidative metabolism and graft performance.

items.title: Governance Before Technology: Building Japan’s National Pathway for Controlled Donation After Circulatory Death
How I Do It: Recurrent IgA Nephropathy After Transplant—Integrating Emerging Therapies Into Practice
Combination of Serum Leucine-rich Alpha-2-Glycoprotein 1 and Citrulline as Biomarkers of Graft Monitoring and Response to Antirejection Treatment in Intestinal Transplantation
items.abstract: Background. Intestinal transplantation (ITx) has the highest rejection rate among solid organ transplantations. Nevertheless, convenient, reliable, and noninvasive biomarkers for rejection surveillance are lacking. Leucine-rich alpha-2-glycoprotein 1 (LRG-1) has been developed as a new serum biomarker of disease activity in numerous gastrointestinal inflammatory pathologies. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the utility of serum LRG-1 as a biomarker for predicting post-ITx rejection, using citrulline as a known marker. Methods. Serum LRG-1 (n = 77) and citrulline (n = 64) samples were obtained from 5 post-ITx patients. We analyzed the correlation between these serum levels and the “villi appearance, erythema, capillary network, crypt widening, and heterogeneity (VENCH)” score according to the endoscopic findings of the intestinal graft evaluated on the same day as serum sample collection, as well as histopathological diagnosis. Results. We observed a negative correlation between serum LRG-1 and citrulline levels. LRG-1 values in the VENCH score ≥4 group were significantly higher than those in the VENCH <4 group ( P < 0.0001). The area under the curve of the citrulline/LRG-1 (C/L) ratio for detecting endoscopic abnormalities was 0.896 (sensitivity: 0.87; specificity: 0.89). In addition, LRG-1 values in the pathological rejection group were significantly higher than those in the nonrejection group ( P < 0.0001). The area under the curve of the C/L ratio for detecting rejection was 0.992 (sensitivity: 1.0; specificity: 0.94). Conclusions. The present data support the hypothesis that LRG-1 is an attractive noninvasive biomarker of rejection after ITx, especially as an indicator, such as the C/L ratio. Routine serum LRG-1 monitoring may help to reduce the frequency of invasive endoscopic surveillance.

items.title: Glucagon-like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists in Heart Transplant Recipients With Type 2 Diabetes: A Multicenter Study
items.abstract: Background. Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is frequent after heart transplantation (HT) and is exacerbated by immunosuppressive therapy. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) may improve metabolic control, but data in HT recipients are limited. Methods. We performed a retrospective, multicenter study including HT recipients with T2DM from 14 Spanish centers. In patients treated with GLP-1 RAs, we assessed antidiabetic and immunosuppressive therapies, adverse events, and changes in metabolic parameters, insulin dose, and immunosuppressant trough levels during the first year after GLP-1 RA initiation. Results. Among 734 HT recipients with T2DM (2011–2021), 108 (14.7%) received GLP-1 RAs (mean age 55.4 ± 9.0 y; 79.6% male), initiated 4.0 ± 3.1 y post-HT. At baseline, 64.8% had obesity. Semaglutide was used in 59%, dulaglutide in 27%, liraglutide in 13%, and tirzepatide in 1%; 41.7% achieved the maximum therapeutic dose. After 1 y, significant reductions were observed in body weight (–6.2 kg; 95% confidence interval [CI], –7.7 to –4.5 kg), fasting glucose (–27 mg/dL; 95% CI, –41 to –7 mg/dL), glycated hemoglobin (–0.74%; 95% CI, –1.12% to –0.35%), total cholesterol (–12 mg/dL; 95% CI, –19 to –6 mg/dL), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (–8 mg/dL; 95% CI, –14 to –2 mg/dL), triglycerides (–29 mg/dL; 95% CI, –53 to –5 mg/dL), and systolic blood pressure (–3.6 mm Hg; 95% CI, –6.4 to –0.9 mm Hg). Tacrolimus trough levels decreased modestly (–0.7 ng/mL; 95% CI, –1.4 to –0.1 ng/mL; P = 0.025), without episodes of acute rejection. Gastrointestinal adverse events occurred in 12.0%, leading to discontinuation in 3.7%. Conclusions. In HT recipients with T2DM, GLP-1 RAs were associated with improved glycemic and cardiometabolic parameters and were generally well tolerated. These findings support the use of GLP-1 RAs as a valuable therapeutic strategy for the management of T2DM after HT.

items.title: Incidence and Risk Factors of Hepatic Artery Thrombosis and Stenosis After Pediatric Liver Transplantation: Results From the HEPATIC Registry
items.abstract: Background. The incidence and risk factors of hepatic artery complications (HACs), including thrombosis (HAT) and stenosis (HAS), after pediatric liver transplantation (pLT) are not well characterized. This study aimed to assess the incidence and risk factors of HACs after pLT and quantify the screening effort required to identify a single HAC. Methods. We performed a retrospective multicenter analysis using the HEPATIC registry, including pLTs from 32 centers over a 20-y period. HAC incidence was assessed across subgroups defined by pLT indication, recipient age, donor type, transplant era, and annual center volume. Timing of HAC occurrence and the number needed to screen were analyzed. Results. Among 11 443 pLTs, HACs occurred in 4.8% (HAT 3.6%; HAS 1.2%). Most HACs developed within the first-month posttransplant (82.4%), with HAT peaking in the first 2 wk, whereas HAS was more evenly distributed. The overall incidence increased in 2012–2021 (5.3%), with rising HAS and stable HAT rates. Modifiable factors included living donor transplantation (3.4%) and high-volume centers (3.8%), both associated with lower HAC rates, whereas whole grafts in infants <1 y with biliary atresia (15.3%) were associated with higher incidence (all P < 0.001). Patient-related risk factors included retransplantation following previous HACs (11.3%) and noncirrhotic metabolic diseases (7.6%, both P < 0.001). The number needed to screen ranged from 173 to 1907 and was lower in high-risk groups. Conclusions. HACs occurred in 4.8% of pLTs, with recent increases driven by HAS. Infants <1 with biliary atresia receiving whole grafts and patients undergoing retransplantation after prior HACs were at the highest risk.

items.title: Beyond FEV1: Alveolar Nitric Oxide Within an Integrated, Noninvasive Model for CLAD Surveillance
items.abstract: Background. Chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD) remains the major limitation to long-term survival after lung transplantation. Fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO) is a noninvasive marker of airway inflammation, but its clinical role after lung transplantation remains uncertain. This study investigated whether multiple-flow FeNO parameters may support CLAD risk stratification in lung transplant recipients. Methods. We performed a retrospective observational study of 114 lung transplant recipients. At the time of FeNO assessment, 45 patients had CLAD, 9 had acute cellular rejection, and 60 were clinically stable. FeNO was assessed at multiple expiratory flows to derive proximal and distal nitric oxide parameters. Results. Alveolar nitric oxide concentration (CalvNO) was significantly higher in patients with CLAD than in clinically stable recipients and showed the best discrimination among FeNO-derived variables for prevalent CLAD (area under the curve [AUC], 0.849; optimal cutoff, 7.7 ppb). A model combining CalvNO, diffusing capacity of the lung for carbon monoxide, residual volume/total lung capacity, and forced expiratory volume in 1 s showed good diagnostic performance (AUC, 0.88). Among initially stable recipients, 9 developed CLAD during follow-up. Baseline CalvNO was associated with incident CLAD in exploratory time-to-event analysis (hazard ratio, 1.35 per 1 ppb increase), with an AUC of 0.889 and a cutoff of 7.12 ppb. Microbiological status modified FeNO interpretation, particularly for proximal indices, whereas CalvNO remained more consistently associated with CLAD in colonized and microbiologically negative patients. Conclusions. Multiple-flow FeNO-derived CalvNO is a biologically plausible and clinically promising noninvasive biomarker for CLAD risk stratification. Its most defensible application is as part of integrated surveillance combining FeNO-derived parameters, pulmonary function, lung volumes, diffusion capacity, and structured assessment of infection or other reversible conditions.

items.title: Cell Therapy Protocol Recommendations (Liver) From the Salzburg Regulatory Cell Therapy in Organ Transplantation Expert Meeting
Beyond Abstinence: How Integrated Multidisciplinary Management Improves Long-term Post Liver Transplant Outcomes
items.abstract: Background. Alcohol-associated liver disease is the leading indication for liver transplantation (LT). We assessed long-term alcohol relapse after LT within a program using an integrated multidisciplinary team for relapse monitoring and prevention before and after transplantation, without requiring a predefined abstinence period. Methods. In 2018, we established a prospective program in which all patients with associated liver disease were evaluated and followed before and after LT by a multidisciplinary team embedded within the transplant program. We reviewed long-term outcomes as part of this program between 2018 and 2023. Results. A total of 165 recipients were transplanted since the inception of the program. Posttransplant alcohol relapse occurred in 21 patients (12.7%), of whom 57.1% had mild alcohol consumption, 4.8% moderate, and 33.3% severe. Median time to relapse was 9.4 mo (5.9–30.2). Ethyl glucuronide positivity confirmed relapse in 20 of 21 patients, and 17 endorsed alcohol use. All patients had access to addiction psychiatry follow-up and relapse prevention therapy embedded within their posttransplant care. Those who relapsed were offered intensification of relapse prevention therapy and 16/21 engaged in regular follow-up. Only 6 patients (3.6%) reported ongoing alcohol consumption at last follow-up, while all others reestablished abstinence. No significant differences in outcomes were observed between groups. No alcohol-related deaths or graft losses occurred. Conclusions. A multidisciplinary fully integrated team along with individualized approach to candidate evaluation with follow-up pre- and post-LT is critical to successful outcomes and results in a much lower rate of relapse at long-term post-LT.

items.title: The Benefit of Modulating Costimulatory Signals to Boost Transplant Survival: Hitting two Birds With one Stone?
MASLD Liver Transplant: Evolution of Frequency, Age Trends, and Factors Associated With Outcomes
items.abstract: Background. Metabolic dysfunction–associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has rapidly emerged as a leading indication for liver transplantation (LT) in the United States. There remains a need to understand the evolution of transplant volumes and recipient profiles and outcomes. In this study, we aim to analyze current MASLD LT trends to aid in identifying opportunities for this patient population. Methods. We analyzed UNOS data for primary liver transplants (2010–2024), identifying MASLD by diagnosis codes and stratifying transplants into three eras (2010–2014, 2015–2019, and 2020–2024). Analyses included annual MASLD transplant counts and proportions, era-specific annual percent change, comparisons of donor, operative, and recipient characteristics, Kaplan–Meier curves, multivariable Cox regression for overall post-LT mortality, and competing-risk regression for waitlist outcomes. Results. In total, 18 153 MASLD LT recipients were included (Era 1: 2734; Era 2: 6127; Era 3: 9292). Annual MASLD LT volume increased from 461 in 2010 to 2090 in 2024. Annual percent change was +10.6% (Era 1), +20.1% (Era 2), and +5.9% (Era 3). In Era 3, recipients were as young as 8 y. Era 3 waitlist candidates had significantly higher likelihood of transplant (sHR 1.52; 95% CI, 1.46–1.58) and lower risk of waitlist mortality (sHR 0.44; 95% CI, 0.40–0.48). Recipient survival increased from 97.0% to 98.3% at 30 d, and 90.5% to 92.6% at 1 y (both P < 0.01). Conclusions. From 2010 to 2024, MASLD LT rose markedly but relative growth plateaued. Increasing age diversity, including pediatric recipients, highlights the need for earlier recognition and optimized management.

items.title: Beyond Conventional Immunosuppression: Targeting the Peptidylprolyl Isomerase A-CD147 Axis in Porcine Cardiac Xenotransplantation
Analysis of Preformed Anti-DQα Donor-specific Antibodies in the Context of the Intact HLA-DQ Heterodimer
From Ischemic Thresholds to Dynamic Assessment: How NRP Is revolutionizing DCD Liver Transplantation
Building a National Heart Transplant Program in the United Arab Emirates: Organization, Challenges, and Lessons Learned
A Review: Handbook of Clinical Transplantation. Editor: Gabriel M. Danovitch
Uterus Transplant Living Donor Evaluation and Selection: An Approach to Optimizing Donor and Recipient Outcomes
items.abstract: Background. Since the first live birth from uterus transplantation (UTx) in 2014, there has been an ever-growing interest in the technique from patients and transplant programs worldwide. The Dallas UTx program first reported a live birth in the United States in 2017 and has subsequently completed 40 transplants with a living-donor–predominant approach. To date, the published scientific literature has focused on recipient and newborn outcomes, with relatively limited discussion surrounding living donor evaluation. Methods. The aim of this study was to describe the methodology, evolution, and outcomes from living donor evaluation at the Dallas UTx program. Results. Over a 9-y period, 1329 women volunteered for living donation evaluation. A total of 72 women proceeded to full evaluation, with 38 deemed eligible (37 nondirected donation, 97%). Six women withdrew following evaluation, and 28 were deemed ineligible. Thirteen were declined for vasculature concerns (the main reason for exclusion), and 8 because of other abnormalities found on imaging. Two potential candidates were deemed ineligible because of medical comorbidities, and a further 3 on psychological evaluation. An additional 2 candidates were ineligible following committee review. Twenty-seven (68%) recipients have delivered a child, 4 have delivered 2 children, and 6 are currently pregnant. Conclusions. Successful living donor UTx requires thorough donor evaluation. Favorable donor, recipient, and newborn outcomes were observed within the context of this comprehensive donor evaluation and selection process.

items.title: Reply: Addressing the Role of Glucagon-like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists in Liver Transplant Recipients
Offered Deceased Donor Kidneys With Little or No Chance of Being Transplanted
items.abstract: Background. With a broadening deceased donor pool and recent allocation policy changes, US transplant programs have reported challenges managing an influx of suboptimal kidney offers. We hypothesized that the number of offered kidneys with a minuscule chance of being transplanted has risen. If so, targeted innovations may be needed to reduce administrative burden and improve system efficiency. Methods. Using Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network data on kidneys offered in 2016–2024, we developed a multivariable model to predict the probability that an offered kidney was transplanted (PrTx). We examined trends in the number and proportion of offered kidneys having PrTx ≤2%, ≤5%, and ≤10%. Results. Donor factors most predictive of PrTx were age, donation after circulatory death, serum creatinine (terminal, peak, nadir), presence and duration of diabetes and hypertension, infectious disease test results, and body mass index. From 2016 to 2024, the annual number of kidneys offered with PrTx ≤2%, PrTx ≤5%, and PrTx ≤10% increased 13-fold (from 18 to 236), 12-fold (84 to 1055), and 10-fold (299 to 2856), respectively. Of the 236 offered kidneys with PrTx ≤2% in 2024, none was transplanted. The 2856 kidneys with PrTx ≤10% accounted for 7.9% (n = 1 208 883) of manually refused offers but just 1.1% (n = 239) of transplanted kidneys. Organ procurement organizations and centers varied substantially in offering and transplanting low-PrTx kidneys. Conclusions. The number of offered kidneys with extremely low predicted transplant probability has risen sharply, most notably in 2024. Innovations, such as improved offer filtering capabilities and standardized expedited allocation pathways, are needed to improve kidney placement efficiency.

items.title: Septal dysfunction and Abnormal Systolic Stretch Are Associated with Right Ventricular Dysfunction in Repaired Tetralogy of Fallot
items.containerTitle: Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography
items.abstract: Aims Right ventricular (RV) dysfunction is a major determinant of outcomes after Tetralogy of Fallot repair (rToF). Although right bundle branch block is present in most patients and electro-mechanical dyssynchrony (EMD) has been associated with RV dysfunction, only a subset of patients ultimately develops RV dysfunction. We hypothesized that septal dysfunction is a key feature associated with the development of EMD-induced RV dysfunction in rToF. Methods We retrospectively studied 126 pediatric rToF patients (median age 14.7 years) with contemporaneous ECG, echocardiography, and cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) between 2019-2025. Septal mechanics were quantified by strain-derived systolic rebound stretch (SRS) and further combined with RV free-wall mechanics into a systolic stretch index (SSI). RV mechanical dyssynchrony was visually classified, with septal contraction abrogation and systolic stretch as key features. Multivariable models evaluated associations between systolic stretch parameters and RV dysfunction (CMR-derived RV ejection fraction (EF) ≤ 46%), adjusting for relevant covariates. Results RV dysfunction was present in 24.6% of patients. Patients with >moderate RV outflow tract obstruction (peak gradient >40 mmHg) were excluded, median pulmonary regurgitant fraction was 35% (IQR, 26-44%). Median SSI was higher in patients with RV dysfunction than in those without (8.9% (IQR 3.2-11.3) vs 2.9% (IQR 1.5-5.5), p 4%. SSI demonstrated excellent intraobserver and interobserver reproducibility (ICC 0.996 and 0.997, respectively). Conclusions In pediatric rToF, RV dysfunction was associated with abnormal septal contraction and systolic stretch. RV-SSI, integrating inefficient RV mechanics via septal and RV free-wall systolic stretch, was independently associated with RV dysfunction beyond QRSd, RV volumes and pulmonary regurgitation severity. These findings may help characterize RV electromechanical phenotypes and provide a rationale for future studies evaluating RV resynchronization therapy.

items.title: Early Cardiac Dysfunction in Pediatric Becker Muscular Dystrophy: A Prospective Cross-sectional Echocardiographic Study
items.containerTitle: Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography
items.abstract: Background Becker muscular dystrophy (BMD) is an X-linked disorder characterized by progressive muscle weakness and cardiac involvement, with cardiomyopathy being the leading cause of mortality. While cardiac dysfunction in adult BMD patients is well documented, the early cardiac phenotype in pediatric populations remains poorly understood. This prospective cross-sectional study aimed to characterize age-stratified differences in cardiac function among children with BMD, children with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), and healthy controls. Methods This prospective cross-sectional study included male children aged 3-18 years who were enrolled from June 2020 to December 2023 and met strict inclusion criteria: genetically confirmed BMD or DMD diagnosis, no prior cardiac medications, and absence of comorbid conditions affecting cardiac function. Participants were stratified into three age-matched groups: 3 to under 7 years (youngest group), 7 to under 10 years (middle group), and 10 to under 18 years (oldest group), with comparable mean ages across BMD, DMD, and healthy controls within each age stratum. Comprehensive echocardiographic assessments were performed, including conventional parameters, tissue Doppler imaging, and speckle-tracking echocardiography. Statistical comparisons were made between groups within each age range. Result The study comprised 86 BMD patients, 86 DMD patients, and 74 controls across three age groups. After normality testing and Bonferroni-corrected post hoc comparisons, BMD patients showed early left ventricular involvement, including lower LVEF (60.54±8.09% vs 65.56±3.04%, p Conclusion Pediatric BMD patients exhibit subclinical, age-associated cardiac dysfunction detectable across pediatric age groups. Because abnormalities in LVEF, LV GLS, RV FAC, and RV GLS were already present in the youngest group, the findings support early and regular cardiac surveillance incorporating advanced echocardiographic techniques from preschool age. Longitudinal studies are needed to determine whether these subclinical differences predict clinically overt cardiomyopathy or treatment response.

items.title: Impact of the extent, pattern, and location of replacement myocardial fibrosis on clinical outcomes in aortic regurgitation
items.abstract: Aims The prognostic significance of late gadolinium enhancement (LGE)-detected replacement myocardial fibrosis in aortic regurgitation (AR) remains incompletely understood. This study aims to explore the association between the extent, pattern, and location of LGE and clinical outcomes in patients with chronic AR. Methods and results Between 2010 and 2024, consecutive patients with moderate-to-severe AR and no significant coronary artery stenosis who underwent contrast-enhanced cardiac magnetic resonance were included. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as cardiovascular mortality, heart transplantation, or rehospitalization for heart failure. The association between LGE characteristics and MACE was evaluated. Overall, 363 patients (mean age 52.6 ± 14.2 years; 54 females) were included. Over a median follow-up of 56.6 months, 73 patients experienced MACE. LGE was present in 200 patients (55.1%). An LGE extent threshold of 2.6% provided robust risk stratification, yielding the highest C-index of 0.797, a likelihood ratio chi-square of 97.30, and the lowest Akaike information criterion of 681.06. Furthermore, predominant subendocardial-involved LGE was present in 13.5% of LGE-positive patients and was independently associated with MACE after adjusting for LGE extent (HR 3.028; 95% CI 1.216–7.539; P = 0.017). Kaplan–Meier analysis demonstrated that patients with both LGE extent >2.6% and predominant subendocardial-involved LGE pattern were at the highest risk of MACE. Conclusion In AR, an LGE extent > 2.6% predicts MACE better than LGE presence alone. Furthermore, non-ischaemic predominant subendocardial-involved LGE is independently associated with MACE. The coexistence of both features further amplifies the risk of MACE.

items.title: Of bicuspid aortic stenosis, women, and fibrosis: At last, new computed tomography-derived insights into 2-sinus bicuspid aortic valve stenosis
Where the Differences Lie: Sex and Plaque Burden
Right Atrial Phasic Function Improves CMR-Based Prognostication in Patients with Heart Failure with Mildly Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Multicenter Study
items.abstract: Aims In multiple cardiovascular diseases, right atrial (RA) function can serve as an independent predictor for the clinical status and prognosis. However, the prognostic value of RA strain in patients with heart failure with mildly reduced ejection fraction (HFmrEF) remains considerably unknown. This study aims to explore the relationships between RA strain derived from cardiac magnetic resonance imaging-feature tracking (CMR-FT) and adverse outcomes in patients with HFmrEF. Methods and Results This retrospective study enrolled patients with HFmrEF who were referred for echocardiography and CMR at two tertiary medical centers from April 2016 to September 2024. The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause mortality, HF-related hospitalization and cardiac transplantation. The findings were validated in a cohort of patients with HFmrEF enrolled from two additional tertiary care centers (January 2019 to January 2025). The development cohort included 1317 patients, and the validation cohort comprised 385 patients. During a median follow-up period of 2.8 years and 2.1 years, respectively, 243 and 72 patients in the development cohort and validation cohort reached the primary endpoint, respectively. Cox regression analysis showed that RA conduit strain was an independent predictor of the primary outcome (HR: 0.86 [0.82, 0.90]; P < .001). The full model integrating clinical variables, traditional imaging, and RA strain achieved the best predictive performance (C-index: 0.80 in development, 0.81 in validation cohorts). Conclusion RA conduit strain derived from CMR is an independent predictor of adverse outcomes in patients with HFmrEF, providing incremental prognostic value beyond traditional clinical and imaging-derived risk markers.​

items.title: Association of Lipoprotein(a) and Low-Attenuation Plaque Burden With Future Myocardial Infarction
Look Beyond the Trabeculae
Identifying the High-Risk Arrhythmic Mitral Valve Prolapse Phenotype by Imaging
items.abstract: Within arrhythmogenic mitral valve prolapse (AMVP), a distinct subset of mitral valve prolapse (MVP), there is a small group that carries a higher risk of malignant ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death called malignant MVP. The malignant MVP phenotype is over-represented in young women with unexplained sudden cardiac death on autopsy. AMVP is defined by myxomatous, often bileaflet MVP with mitral annular disjunction, abnormal valvular-myocardial mechanics, complex ventricular ectopy, and nonsustained ventricular tachycardia. Excessive mechanical force from systolic annular expansion, papillary muscle traction, and basal inferolateral "curling" promotes focal replacement and diffuse interstitial fibrosis, creating an arrhythmogenic substrate. Premature ventricular contractions act as triggers, whereas autonomic modulation influences the timing of ventricular arrhythmia initiation and progression to ventricular fibrillation or sustained monomorphic ventricular tachycardia. Baseline evaluation with an electrocardiogram and transthoracic echocardiography is necessary to identify AMVP, exclude severe mitral regurgitation, and identify high-risk markers. If no premature ventricular contractions are found on a resting electrocardiogram, exercise stress testing and extended rhythm monitoring can help bring out ventricular premature contractions, which are triggers of ventricular arrhythmias. Cardiac magnetic resonance provides incremental prognostic value with late gadolinium enhancement reflecting replacement fibrosis and T1 mapping identifying diffuse fibrosis, even in those with no late gadolinium enhancement. Machine-learning analysis may further refine risk stratification by integrating high-risk features such as mitral annular disjunction, fibrosis extent, and location that outperform symptom-based assessment. As transcatheter and surgical mitral interventions expand, accurate phenotyping of AMVP is increasingly important, as hemodynamic correction of mitral regurgitation alone does not eliminate the underlying arrhythmogenic substrate. Comprehensive multimodality imaging and integrated rhythm assessment are therefore central to individualized risk stratification and management in this vulnerable population.

items.title: Bending the Curve
Calcium Density as a Marker of Coronary Plaque Stabilization in Primary Prevention
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite primary prevention statin treatment, a substantial proportion of individuals remain at residual risk for cardiovascular events. Coronary computed tomographic angiography (CTA) enables the quantification of compositional changes in calcified plaque. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to examine whether increases in coronary calcified plaque volume and density associated with statin therapy could be used as a marker of plaque stabilization in asymptomatic individuals undergoing serial coronary CTA. METHODS: In the CAUGHT-CAD trial, asymptomatic, statin-naive, intermediate-risk individuals were randomized to a primary prevention strategy (including statin treatment) vs usual care. Participants underwent coronary CTA at baseline and 3 years. In this post hoc analysis, volumes of 5 plaque subtypes were quantified: noncalcified (≤350 HU), low-density calcium (351-500 HU), intermediate-density calcium (501-700 HU), high-density calcium (701-1000 HU), and very high density calcium (>1,000 HU). The primary outcome was the per-lesion level change in volumes of calcified plaque subtypes. RESULTS: Eight hundred forty lesions were included from 338 participants (mean age: 58.3 ± 6.9 years, 57.1% men, 161 [47.6%] statin treated). Statin treatment was associated with greater progression in intermediate-density (β = 0.89, SE = 0.39; P = 0.02) and high-density (β = 0.79, SE = 0.24; P = 0.001) calcium, alongside regression of noncalcified plaque (β = -9.83, SE = 1.64; P < 0.001), following adjustment for cardiovascular risk factors, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) level, and baseline plaque volume. Among statin-treated participants, LDL-C reduction ≥30% was associated with greater progression of high-density (β = 1.11, SE = 0.49; P = 0.03) and very high density (β = 1.68, SE = 0.85; P = 0.04) calcium. CONCLUSIONS: In asymptomatic, intermediate-risk individuals, statin treatment was associated with a shift toward higher density calcium within coronary plaques, most marked with effective lowering of LDL-C. (Coronary Artery Calcium Score: Use to Guide Management of Hereditary Coronary Artery Disease [CAUGHT-CAD]; ACTRN12614001294640).

items.title: Optimizing Echocardiographic Evaluation of Chronic Mitral Regurgitation
items.abstract: Background The ASE (American Society of Echocardiography) guidelines recommend the presence of at least 4 specific criteria to confirm a diagnosis of definite severe mitral regurgitation (MR). However, the performance of these criteria, particularly when Objectives This study aims to evaluate and optimize the ASE native MR guidelines by comparing them with quantitative cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), considered the reference standard for MR assessment. Methods In this prospective study, 177 patients underwent near-simultaneous CMR and transthoracic echocardiography for the assessment of MR. MR severity was classified using a 4-grade scale based on CMR-derived regurgitant volume, which was calculated as the difference between total left ventricular (LV) stroke volume and aortic forward flow. MR severity was similarly graded using the ASE algorithm, with quantification performed when necessary, by averaging the regurgitant volume from 3 methods: 1) the proximal isovelocity surface area method; 2) the biplane LV volumetric method; and 3) the mitral valve volumetric method. Results The study cohort had a median age of 61.7 years, with 55% being men. Primary MR was the predominant pathology (73% of patients), with 42% having mitral valve prolapse and 25% presenting with flail leaflets. There was exact agreement between transthoracic echocardiography and CMR MR grading in 51% of cases, whereas agreement within 1 grade was observed in 89%. Patients who met any of the ASE severe MR criteria were predominantly classified as having grades 3 to 4 MR by CMR. The following ASE parameters demonstrated high specificity for identifying grade 4 MR by CMR: pulmonary vein systolic flow reversal (specificity 88%), enlarged LV with normal systolic function (specificity 85%), proximal isovelocity surface area radius ≥1.0 cm (specificity 83%), and vena contracta width ≥0.7 cm (specificity 80%). Combining color Doppler with either pulmonary vein systolic reversal or enlarged LV with normal function resulted in 91%-95% specificity for severe MR. Importantly, reliance on fewer ASE criteria reduced the need for quantification from 86% (4 criteria) to 73% (3 criteria) and 59% (2 criteria), thereby enhancing diagnostic efficiency. Conclusions Certain ASE criteria, especially when used in combination, are highly specific for diagnosing severe MR, even when <4 criteria are present. This study suggests that in many cases, the reliance on extensive quantification may be reduced, streamlining the diagnostic process and improving clinical workflow.

items.title: Left Ventricular Filling Pressure Classification by Electrocardiogram, Echocardiography, and Catheterization
items.abstract: Background Left ventricular diastolic filling pressure (LVFP) is a hallmark of heart failure. Although pulmonary artery wedge pressure (PAWP) measured during right heart catheterization (RHC) is the reference standard, echocardiography is more commonly used in practice. Objectives The authors previously developed an artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiographic (AI-ECG) algorithm, trained on echocardiographic assessment, to classify LVFP. The aim of this study was to evaluate the prognostic implications of LVFP classification by AI-ECG, echocardiography, and PAWP among patients undergoing temporally proximate testing. Methods Adults who underwent echocardiography with electrocardiography within 14 days and RHC within 30 days were included. Elevated LVFP was defined as PAWP ≥15 mm Hg, grade 2 or 3 diastolic dysfunction by echocardiography, or elevated LVFP as classified by AI-ECG. Associations with all-cause mortality and major adverse cardiovascular events were assessed. Results Among 4,168 patients (median age: 64 years; 47.7% women), elevated LVFP was classified by AI-ECG in 2,383 patients, by echocardiography in 1,643, and by PAWP in 1,841. AI-ECG showed good discrimination for echocardiographic LVFP (AUC: 0.879; 95% CI: 0.867-0.891) and moderate discrimination for PAWP (AUC: 0.711; 95% CI: 0.695-0.727). Over 7.7 years, 1,433 deaths occurred. Elevated LVFP classification by AI-ECG (adjusted HR [aHR]: 1.80; 95% CI: 1.55-2.09) and echocardiography (aHR: 1.74; 95% CI: 1.51-2.02) showed stronger associations with mortality than PAWP (aHR: 1.18; 95% CI: 1.05-1.31); in discordant cases, AI-ECG better predicted survival. Similar associations were observed for major adverse cardiovascular events. Conclusions Despite moderate agreement with PAWP, echocardiography and AI-ECG showed stronger associations with clinical outcomes, suggesting they capture prognostically relevant myocardial information beyond resting hemodynamic status.

items.title: Assessment of Severity of Chronic Aortic Regurgitation
Toward Improved Risk Association
Patient-Level Perivascular Adipose Tissue Density Aggregation and Plaque Progression
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) density on coronary computed tomography angiography (CTA) reflects pericoronary inflammation, but measurements adjacent to existing plaques may be confounded by local inflammatory signaling from the plaque itself-a form of reverse causation. Whether systematically comparing patient-level PVAT aggregation approaches (including measurements restricted to plaque-free segments) can identify a more robust inflammatory biomarker has not been evaluated. OBJECTIVES: The authors aimed to compare the predictive performance of 4 patient-level PVAT aggregation approaches for coronary plaque progression. METHODS: From the PARADIGM serial coronary CTA registry, 412 patients with baseline coronary plaque who underwent serial coronary CTA at identical tube voltages were included (mean age: 61.1 ± 9.3 years; 61.7% male; mean interval: 3.2 ± 1.2 years). Four patient-level PVAT measures were compared: proximal right coronary artery (pRCA), whole-coronary, plaque-free, and plaque PVAT. Multivariable regression models were constructed for annualized plaque volume (PV) progression with adjustment for clinical risk factors and imaging covariates. RESULTS: Annualized increases in pRCA PVAT (β = 0.804; P = 0.033), whole-coronary PVAT (β = 1.142; P = 0.022), and plaque-free PVAT (β = 1.419; P = 0.007) were each independently associated with total PV progression, whereas plaque PVAT did not reach significance (β = 0.755; P = 0.083). For noncalcified PV progression, plaque-free PVAT was the only significant measure (β = 1.086; P = 0.026). None of the 4 baseline PVAT measures were significantly associated with plaque progression (all P > 0.50). Pairwise comparisons revealed no significant differences among the 4 measures. CONCLUSIONS: Changes in pRCA, whole-coronary, and plaque-free PVAT were each independently associated with total PV progression. For noncalcified PV progression, plaque-free PVAT change was the only significant measure. (Progression of AtheRosclerotic PlAque DetermIned by Computed TomoGraphic Angiography Imaging [PARADIGM]; NCT02803411).

items.title: Electromechanical Window Negativity and Arrhythmic Risk in Arrhythmogenic Mitral Valve Prolapse
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Mitral valve prolapse (MVP) is generally a benign valvular heart disease, but a subset of patients is at particular risk of malignant ventricular arrhythmias (AMVP). OBJECTIVES: The authors evaluated the electromechanical window (EMW) as an arrhythmia-risk marker in (A)MVP (the sum of all MVP and AMVP patients). METHODS: Healthy controls, patients with MVP without ventricular arrhythmia (MVP/-VA), and patients with AMVP with nonsustained (AMVP/nsVA) or sustained ventricular arrhythmia (AMVP/VA) (ventricular arrhythmia >30 seconds) were retrospectively included from 3 centers (derivation cohort). An independent validation (A)MVP cohort was recruited from 2 centers. EMW was calculated blinded from apical Doppler echocardiography by subtracting the QT time from the simultaneous Q-to-aortic-valve closure time (QAoC). RESULTS: In the derivation cohort (31 controls, 31 MVP/-VA, 29 AMVP/nsVA, 14 AMVP/VA), patients with (A)MVP displayed a borderline shorter QAoCc (P = 0.06) and significantly longer QTc than controls (P < 0.0001), resulting in a more negative EMW (-18 ms [-47 to -8 ms]; P < 0.0001). EMW was most negative in patients with AMVP/VA (-71 ms [-177 to -30 ms]). These findings were reproduced in the validation cohort (n = 76 with [A]MVP), albeit at different absolute values. In a pooled receiver-operating characteristic analysis, EMW identified patients with AMVP/VA with an area under the curve of 0.82 (95% CI: 0.73-0.91), significantly outperforming QTc and QAoCc. An EMW threshold of -30 ms was the optimal cutoff (sensitivity: 0.71; specificity: 0.83). EMW was independently associated with AMVP/VA status and improved model performance in addition to established risk parameters. CONCLUSIONS: EMW is markedly negative in patients with AMVP/VA, reflecting electromechanical discordance. Thus, EMW emerges as a promising risk-associated marker in (A)MVP.

Liver Extracellular Volume in Patients With Tricuspid Regurgitation
items.abstract: Background Liver extracellular volume (L-ECV), a novel cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) parameter of systemic venous congestion, might help to stratify tricuspid regurgitation (TR) patients at higher risk, but its role in this context is unexplored. Objectives The aim of this study was to assess the incremental prognostic relevance of L-ECV in a large TR cohort. Methods Data were collected from patients with TR referred to CMR between 2019 and 2024 who had parametric mapping analysis for L-ECV quantification. The primary endpoint was the composite of all-cause mortality and heart failure (HF) hospitalization, under medical management. Results In 462 patients included (median age: 67 years; 43% female), median left ventricular ejection fraction was 51% (Q1-Q3: 40%-59%), median tricuspid regurgitant fraction was 21% (Q1-Q3: 14%-33%), and median L-ECV was 31% (Q1-Q3: 28%-35%). When dividing the cohort according to median L-ECV value, patients with high L-ECV (≥ median) showed worse baseline status with more clinical and imaging signs of right HF and (after a median follow-up of 2.1 years) poorer survival free from the primary outcome (P Conclusions In our large real-world TR cohort, L-ECV appeared as a novel, powerful CMR marker of right HF with an independent and incremental prognostic value to stratify patients with TR at higher risk of events.

items.title: Post-market device experience reports of dorsal root ganglion stimulation: a 10-year retrospective analysis of the FDA MAUDE database
items.abstract: Background Dorsal root ganglion stimulation is an established therapy for focal neuropathic pain, including complex regional pain syndrome. Post-market adverse event data spanning the full post-approval decade are lacking. Methods We retrospectively analyzed dorsal root ganglion stimulation-related U.S. Food and Drug Administration Manufacturer and User Facility Device Experience (MAUDE) reports (January 2016–May 2026). Records underwent multi-stage deduplication, combining a blinded manual review by four independent investigators with a custom two-stage algorithmic protocol to merge complex residual duplicates. Thematic analysis was performed using NVivo V.15. Results Following deduplication, 10 532 reports were included. 10 334 were reported as serious injuries. Among reports with documented sex (n = 4796), 60.2% were female. Age was reported in 4329 records, and the median was 44 years (IQR: 36–50). The USA contributed 88.4% of geographically identified reports. Most reported patient-related issues were “inadequate pain relief” (n=7135), followed by “failure of implant” (n=781), “implant pain” (n=548), and “cerebrospinal fluid leakage” (n=274). “Migration” was the most prevalent device problem code (n=2426), followed by “high impedance” (n=1560), “therapeutic or diagnostic output failure” (n=1167), and “fracture” (n=1160). Implant-year data were right-truncated. Conclusion Reported dorsal root ganglion stimulation events are dominated by lead migration, impedance abnormality, and fracture frequently co-presenting with persistence of symptoms. These patterns support engineering attention to lead fixation and structured hardware surveillance within routine follow-up. Because MAUDE lacks denominator data, results are signal generating. Prospective registries with implant-level denominators are needed to define true complication rates and distinguish hardware failure from programming-related efficacy loss.
