items.title: Evening Phone Use and Sleep Outcomes Among Youth
items.abstract: Importance Smartphone use has been associated with poor sleep, but existing evidence primarily relies on self-reported, cross-sectional data. Objective To examine within-person and between-person associations between passively sensed evening smartphone use and objectively measured sleep outcomes in adolescents. Design, Setting, and Participants This intensive longitudinal cohort study assessed passively sensed data from US youths in the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development Study. Participants were Android users with at least 14 days of concurrent Effortless Assessment Research System application data and Fitbit-measured sleep. Data were collected between November 30, 2020, and February 5, 2024, and analyzed from February 2 to June 1, 2026. Analysis used within-between decomposition in multilevel models to separate within-person from between-person associations. Exposures Smartphone use after each hourly cutoff from 8 pm to midnight (cumulative) and within 5 to 30 minutes before sleep onset (proximal) were quantified. Main Outcomes and Measures Fitbit-derived sleep measures were assessed, including total sleep time (TST), onset, offset, and sustained and total wake after sleep onset (WASO). Results A total of 425 participants (mean [SD] age, 14.8 [1.1] years; 216 [50.8%] female) contributed 7591 person-nights of data. On nights when adolescents used their phones more than their own evening average (after 10 pm ), they slept a mean (SD) of 20.05 (49.42) minutes less and fell asleep a mean (SD) of approximately 64.73 (50.95) minutes later. Adjusting for covariates, within-person analyses revealed that each additional minute of smartphone use after 10 pm above a participant’s own average was associated with sleep onset that was 0.87 (95% CI, 0.84 to 0.90) minutes later, sleep offset that was 0.37 (95% CI, 0.33 to 0.41) minutes later, and a TST change of −0.43 (95% CI, −0.47 to −0.39) minutes (all P &lt; .001). Estimates increased monotonically across cutoffs from 8 pm to midnight. Proximal use was associated with greater sustained WASO, largest in the final 5 minutes of use before sleep onset (0.74 [95% CI, 0.50 to 0.98] additional minutes of wakefulness; P &lt; .001) and negligible when looking at the final 20 minutes of use before sleep onset. This association was concentrated in the first 30 minutes after sleep onset. Conclusions and Relevance This cohort study found that greater cumulative late-evening phone use was associated with later sleep onset, delayed sleep offset, and shorter TST. Smartphone use immediately before sleep onset was associated with greater WASO, primarily during the first 30 minutes after sleep onset. These findings suggest that reducing evening smartphone use, particularly after 10 pm and immediately before bedtime, may help improve sleep health in adolescents.

items.title: Mobile Subthreshold Exercise Program (MSTEP) for Youth With Prolonged Concussion Recovery
items.abstract: Importance Research suggests that aerobic exercise improves recovery for youth with concussion; however, prior studies primarily focused on acute concussion and required multiple in-person visits. Objective To determine whether a virtually delivered aerobic exercise program improves recovery following concussion compared to a stretching control and examine potential moderators. Design, Setting, and Participants A randomized clinical trial was conducted from 2021 to 2025 comparing the Mobile Subthreshold Exercise Program (MSTEP) to a stretching control for 11- to 18-year-olds with concussion up to 1 year from injury. Participants were recruited from a variety of outpatient locations in 4 US states (Washington, Utah, Wisconsin, and Oregon). Recruitment and data collection occurred from March 2021 until October 2025, and data analysis occurred from November 2025 to April 2026. Interventions Youth randomized to MSTEP were provided activity trackers and an aerobic exercise program initiated at 60% of heart rate maximum. Exercise was advanced in intensity and duration over 6 weeks through weekly videoconferencing calls. Youth in the control group were given stretching exercises and similar weekly calls. Main Outcomes and Measures Primary outcomes included (1) concussive symptoms and (2) health-related quality of life (HRQoL). Secondary outcomes included sleep, depression, and anxiety. Moderation by sex, age, and time since injury was examined. Patients were followed up for 6 months. Results The sample included 210 participants, among whom 122 (58.1%) were female, mean (SD) age was 15.1 (2.2) years, and mean (SD) time since injury was 73.3 (63.3) days. Covariate-adjusted regression analysis showed significant improvement in concussive symptoms and HRQoL at all time points, with greater improvement in MSTEP compared to control at the 3-month time point for both concussive symptoms (β, −3.15; 95% CI, −6.05 to −0.25; adjusted P = .04) and HRQoL (β, 4.15; 95% CI, 0.64-7.66; adjusted P = .04). No significant differences by group were seen at 6 months. Nonlinear mixed-effects modeling with exponential decay showed significantly faster symptom recovery in MSTEP compared to control (difference in rates, −0.68; 95% CI, −2.22 to −0.04; P = .002). Secondary outcomes (sleep, depression, and anxiety) improved in all participants but were not different by group. Benefit of the intervention was only significant for individuals less than 3 months from injury (concussive symptoms: β, −4.44; 95% CI, −7.99 to −0.90; unadjusted P = .01; HRQoL: β, 6.64; 95% CI, 2.55-10.72; unadjusted P = .002). No evidence was found for moderation by other factors. Conclusions and Relevance Per the results of this randomized clinical trial, an aerobic exercise program improves speed of recovery following concussion for youth compared to stretching and can be delivered remotely. However, this type of program appears to be most beneficial for individuals with acute or subacute injury (&lt;3 months since injury). Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04688255

items.title: Ambulatory Electrocardiography Modalities in Pediatric Arrhythmia Detection and Management
items.abstract: Importance The diagnostic efficacy of different ambulatory electrocardiographic monitoring modalities in this patient population remains unclear. Objective To compare the diagnostic yield and clinical utility of 3 ambulatory electrocardiographic modalities in pediatric patients. Design, Setting, and Participants This single-center study took place at an outpatient clinic and an inpatient ward of National Taiwan University Children’s Hospital. Patients younger than 18 years who underwent ambulatory electrocardiographic monitoring between December 2022 and January 2025 were included. These data were analyzed February 2025 to March 2026. Exposure A continuous 7-day Holter device that functioned as an event recorder was used. Recordings from the first 24 hours were defined as the 24-hour Holter results. Main Outcomes and Measures Arrhythmias were categorized as major (tachyarrhythmia or bradyarrhythmia) or minor (extrasystolic arrhythmia). All patients were followed up for 1 year; the final arrhythmia diagnosis was used as the reference standard. The primary and secondary outcomes were detection of arrhythmia and a change in clinical management attributable to monitoring findings, respectively. Results In total, 435 children (235 female [54%] and 200 male [46%]; mean [SD] age, 12.3 [3.9] years) were included. The mean (SD) duration of analyzable ambulatory electrocardiographic data was 4.9 (1.7) days. Of 411 children who activated the event recorder, 10.7% had symptom-correlated arrhythmias. The 7-day Holter monitoring demonstrated a significantly higher rate of major arrhythmias (6.2%) than the 24-hour Holter or 7-day event recordings (2.3%; rate difference 95% CI, 1.9%-6.0%; P &lt; .001). Seven-day Holter monitoring showed superior sensitivity (7-day Holter monitoring: 73%; rate difference 95% CI, 54.1%-84.6%; 24-hour Holter monitoring: 27%; rate difference 95% CI, 13.4%-43.1%; and 7-day event recorder: 27%, rate difference 95% CI, 13.4%-43.1%; P &lt; .001) and a high negative predictive value (97.5%, 95% CI, 95.2%-98.6%). Tachyarrhythmias were associated with higher rates of management changes; management changed in 7.1% of patients with 7-day Holter monitoring, 1.6% with 24-hour Holter (rate difference 95% CI, 3.0%-7.6%; P &lt; .001) and 2.8% with a 7-day event recorder (rate difference 95% CI, 2.0%-6.2%; P &lt; .001). Conclusions and Relevance In this study of pediatric patients without structural heart disease who underwent electrocardiographic monitoring, 7-day continuous ambulatory electrocardiographic monitoring was associated with a significantly higher diagnostic yield than 24-hour Holter and 7-day event recording. Continuous monitoring may be preferred to detect tachyarrhythmias likely to influence clinical management.

items.title: No Caffeine for Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy
Maternal Autoimmune Diseases During Pregnancy and Offspring Type 1 Diabetes
items.abstract: IMPORTANCE Maternal autoimmune diseases during pregnancy may influence the long-term risk of immune-mediated diseases in offspring, but the relative contributions of prenatal and familial factors to offspring type 1 diabetes (T1D) remain unclear. OBJECTIVE To investigate the association between a broad spectrum of maternal autoimmune diseases during pregnancy and offspring T1D, and to compare the associations of maternal and paternal autoimmune diseases with offspring T1D. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS This population-based cohort study included children identified from national health registers who were born in Sweden between 2001 and 2014, and were followed up from birth until T1D diagnosis, death, emigration, or December 31, 2023. These data were analyzed from November 2025 to June 2026. EXPOSURE Parental autoimmune diseases diagnosed before or during pregnancy, identified from national health registers. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES The primary outcome was incident T1D in offspring. Hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% CIs for offspring T1D were estimated using Cox proportional hazard regression models. Associations of maternal and paternal autoimmune diseases before childbirth with offspring T1D were directly compared, and cousin analyses were performed to assess the potential role of shared familial factors. RESULTS During a median follow-up of 15.3 years, 10 273 (0.71%) of the 1 455 645 included individuals (51.4% male and 48.6% female; median [IQR], age 15.3 [11.9-19.0] years) developed T1D. Maternal autoimmune disease during pregnancy was associated with an increased risk of offspring T1D (adjusted HR, 1.57; 95% CI, 1.46-1.68); paternal autoimmune disease before childbirth showed a similar association (adjusted HR, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.37-1.67). No overall difference was observed in maternal-paternal comparisons (ratio of HR, 1.04; 95% CI, 0.92-1.17), but heterogeneity was observed across specific disease categories. A clear gradient in T1D risk was observed according to parental T1D status, with the highest risk among offspring with both parents affected, followed by paternal T1D only and maternal T1D only. In cousin analyses, the association with maternal autoimmune disease was attenuated but persisted (HR, 1.27; 95% CI, 1.08-1.50). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE In this population-based cohort study, maternal autoimmune diseases during pregnancy were associated with an increased risk of offspring T1D. Comparable associations of maternal and paternal autoimmune diseases with offspring T1D suggest a role of shared familial susceptibility, while disease-specific differences indicate that some conditions could have parental-specific effects, suggesting contributions from shared familial susceptibility and potential intrauterine mechanisms.

items.title: Prenatal Exposure to Wildfire PM 2.5 and Risk of ASD and ADHD in Children Enrolled in Medicaid
items.abstract: Importance Wildfires are an increasing source of fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ), yet evidence on prenatal wildfire smoke exposure and long-term neurodevelopmental outcomes remains limited. Objective To examine whether prenatal exposure to wildfire-related PM 2.5 is associated with risk of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in children. Design, Setting, and Participants This was a population-based cohort study of the US nationwide Medicaid population using Medicaid Analytic Extract (MAX) data from 2007 to 2014 with follow-up through childhood. Included were mother-child pairs with continuous enrollment and stable residential zip code during pregnancy. Exposure Weekly wildfire smoke–attributable PM 2.5 at 1-km 2 resolution, aggregated to the zip code level across pregnancy. Main Outcomes and Measures Incident ASD and ADHD identified using validated claims-based algorithms. Associations were estimated using Cox proportional-hazards models with distributed lag nonlinear models. Results A total of 893 212 mother-child pairs (mother mean [SD] age, 24.7 [5.9] years) were included in this analysis. Children entered the cohort at birth (452 218 [50.6%] male). Mean (SD) observed follow-up was 6.3 (2.4) years for children diagnosed with ASD and 7.1 (1.9) years for children diagnosed with ADHD. Among 893 212 children, 8357 were diagnosed with ASD and 22 302 with ADHD. The cumulative incidence until age 8 years was 1.9% for ASD and 10.4% for ADHD. An IQR increase in cumulative wildfire PM 2.5 exposure (0.75 µg/m 3 ) during pregnancy was associated with increased risk of ASD (hazard ratio [HR], 1.30; 95% CI, 1.07-1.59) but not ADHD (HR, 1.03; 95% CI, 0.91-1.17). Associations for ASD were strongest during midpregnancy to late gestation compared with early gestation. Results were robust to sensitivity analyses. Conclusions and Relevance Results of this cohort study show that prenatal exposure to wildfire-related PM 2.5 may be associated with increased risk of ASD but not ADHD. These findings highlight the potential neurodevelopmental impacts of wildfire smoke and underscore the need for strategies to reduce exposure during pregnancy as wildfire activity intensifies.

items.title: Maternal Autoimmune Diseases and Offspring Type 1 Diabetes
Firearm Violence Worry and Firearm Access: Implications for Suicide Prevention
Adolescent Worry About Experiencing Firearm Violence and Its Association With Mental Health
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE To examine the associations between worrying about experiencing firearm violence, past-month psychological distress, and past-year suicide ideation among California adolescents. METHODS Cross-sectional analysis of a representative California adolescent sample (n = 2154), using 2021 and 2022 California Health Interview Survey data. The predictor is worrying about experiencing firearm violence, and outcomes are past-month psychological distress and past-year suicide ideation. RESULTS Thirty-nine percent of California adolescents reported worrying about experiencing firearm violence, which was positively correlated with several characteristics: female, diverse gender identity, lower socioeconomic status, frequent social media use, perceiving unsafe neighborhood, having access to firearms, and knowing peers who have a firearm. In contrast, worrying about experiencing firearm violence was negatively correlated with having a firearm at home and ever using a firearm. Worrying about experiencing firearm violence was associated with 1.6 times greater odds of past-month psychological distress and 1.7 times greater odds of past-year suicide ideation. CONCLUSIONS Among California adolescents, worrying about experiencing firearm violence is relatively common and associated with a higher risk of psychological distress and suicide ideation.

items.title: Association of Caregiver Mental Health and a Childhood Parenting Intervention in China
items.abstract: OBJECTIVES This study examines whether and how caregiver mental health symptoms influence the impacts of a center-based parenting intervention on child development. METHODS We conducted a clustered randomized controlled trial across 100 rural villages in China between 2016 and 2019. Villages were randomly assigned to a treatment group that received weekly 1-on-1 parenting sessions through parenting centers or to a pure comparison group. A total of 2554 caregiver–child dyads with children aged 6 to 24 months were surveyed at baseline, and 2044 completed the endline survey after 1 year (follow-up rate: 80.0%). Child development was assessed using the Bayley Scales of Infant Development, Third Edition. Caregiver mental health was measured using the Depression Anxiety and Stress Scale-21. Ordinary least squares regressions with interaction terms were used for analysis. RESULTS The intervention significantly improved cognitive (β = 0.17 SD; 95% CI 0.045–0.29) and language development (β = 0.10 SD; 95% CI 0.00–0.21) among children whose caregivers did not exhibit depressive symptoms at baseline. Positive cognitive effects were also observed among children of caregivers with low anxiety (β = 0.13 SD; 95% CI 0.00–0.26) or low stress (β = 0.15 SD; 95% CI 0.03–0.27). In contrast, no significant effects were detected across developmental domains among children whose caregivers exhibited mental health symptoms. Heterogeneous impacts were driven by differences in stimulating parenting practices rather than program attendance or parenting beliefs. CONCLUSIONS The intervention primarily benefited children whose caregivers had no baseline mental health symptoms, suggesting caregiver mental health moderates intervention effects.

items.title: Supporting the Family Reported to Child Protective Services
Optimizing Antibiotic Duration for Pneumonia and Sinusitis in the Pediatric Emergency Department
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE Updates to national and international guidelines now recommend shortening antibiotic durations to 3 to 5 days for uncomplicated community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) and 5 to 7 days for acute bacterial rhinosinusitis (ABRS). We aimed to increase the percentage of children discharged home from the emergency department with CAP or ABRS who were treated with an optimal antibiotic duration from 13% to 70% by July 2025. METHODS We assembled a multidisciplinary team and used quality improvement tools, including cause-and-effect analysis, driver diagram, and prioritization matrix, to identify impactful interventions. We also surveyed prescriber comfort with shorter antibiotic durations. Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles included implementing new clinical pathways (CP), electronic health record (EHR) updates, and educating prescribers. Our outcome metric was the percentage of patients receiving recommended antibiotic duration for CAP and ABRS. Process metrics included use of CP Quick Response codes and CAP “Quick-Discharge” order sets. Balancing metric was the number of return visits with the same diagnosis within 14 days. RESULTS We saw shifts in the outcome metric center line in August 2023, February 2024, and November 2024 from 13.1% to 64.8%. These changes primarily reflected CAP duration because it was the more common diagnosis, although ABRS short antibiotic durations showed similar improvement during this time frame. Process metrics showed an increase over time. There was no change in balancing metric. CONCLUSION We significantly improved antibiotic prescription durations for CAP and ABRS through CP changes, EHR updates, prescriber education and feedback, and resource distribution.

items.title: Differential Take-Up of Supplemental Security Income in Florida for Very Low Birth Weight Infants
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE Supplemental Security Income (SSI) eligibility is automatically granted for the subset of very low birth weight (VLBW) infants born below 1200 g. We estimated the effects of automatic eligibility on SSI take-up among VLBW infants near the cutoff, both overall and for key subgroups. METHODS We analyzed Florida birth certificates merged with Social Security Administration records from 1990 to 2015. Our sample included 21 606 infants with gestational age under 32 weeks and birth weight between 1000 to 1400 g. Using a regression discontinuity approach, we tested whether SSI take-up by VLBW infants was higher under the 1200 g cutoff and whether take-up differed by individual characteristics. RESULTS Our results indicated that SSI take-up increased by 19.1 percentage points at the 1200 g cutoff. Baseline take-up rates were the highest for mothers who were Black, less educated, Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) participants, or low-income county residents. Increases in take-up at the SSI eligibility threshold were the largest for mothers who were non-Hispanic Black, other race and ethnicity, or WIC participants. CONCLUSION Our results suggest that the SSI 1200 g eligibility threshold matters—infants just below it were significantly more likely to participate in the program. Take-up among eligible infants varied by individual characteristics, in ways consistent with the program being well-targeted—reaching many infants with worse health and lower income—and yet take-up was far less than universal even for birth weight eligible infants, suggesting a need for additional outreach. Participation was even lower for VLBW infants who were not automatically eligible but could have benefited from the program.

items.title: An Adolescent With Neurosyphilis
items.abstract: Neurosyphilis is a central nervous system (CNS) infection that has become exceedingly rare in the postantibiotic era, especially in children and HIV-negative persons. It can develop during any stage of an untreated syphilis infection and is known as “the great imitator” for its highly variable clinical presentation with inconsistent lab and imaging findings. We describe the case of a previously healthy 17-year-old boy who presented with 2 weeks of right thumb and middle finger myoclonus followed by right upper extremity focal seizures with secondary generalization. Routine and confidential psychosocial history using the HEADSS (Home; Education, Eating, and Exercise; Activities; Drugs; Sexuality; Suicide and Sleep) assessment revealed that our patient was sexually active with one female partner, prompting sexually transmitted infection (STI) screening. The final diagnosis of neurosyphilis was made following a reactive rapid plasma reagin screen and confirmatory treponemal testing of the cerebrospinal fluid. In light of the recent rise in syphilis case incidence and the devastating consequences of CNS involvement, neurosyphilis should be considered in the differential diagnoses for all sexually active adolescents with unexplained neurologic symptoms. Additionally, this case highlights the importance of comprehensive and confidential social history taking in all adolescents, as well as regular STI screening for those at risk.

items.title: Association of Early Primary Care Follow-Up With Acute Care Use After ICU Discharge
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE To determine if early primary care follow-up after pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) hospitalization is associated with reduced acute care use. METHODS Using claims data from publicly and privately insured children, we identified a cohort of PICU hospitalizations from January 2016 to December 2019. We matched children with and without early primary care follow-up (within 7 days of hospital discharge) 1 to 1 on demographic and clinical characteristics. We compared the number of days of acute care use (emergency department or rehospitalization) during days 8 to 90 postdischarge using negative binomial regression and reported incidence rate ratios (IRR). RESULTS The sample included 180 516 PICU hospitalizations, including 158 544 for publicly insured children and 21 972 for privately insured children. Among PICU hospitalizations for publicly and privately insured children, 56 247 (35.4%) and 5156 (23.5%) were associated with acute care use with 8 to 90 days postdischarge. Hospitalizations of children with early primary care follow-up were less likely to be associated with acute care use than those without follow-up (public insurance: IRR, 0.93; 95% CI, 0.90–0.96; P < .001; and private insurance: IRR, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.63–0.77; P < .001). Subgroup analyses suggested early primary care follow-up was associated with larger decreases in acute care after hospitalizations of older children and children with sepsis. The association between early primary care follow-up and acute care use persisted in a secondary analysis using data from 2022 to 2023. CONCLUSIONS Early primary care follow-up was associated with lower acute care use after discharge from PICU hospitalization. Promotion of early primary care follow-up may be warranted after pediatric critical illness.

items.title: Characterizing In-Home Safety Challenges and Strategies for Children With Medical Complexity
items.abstract: OBJECTIVES Medical advances have allowed more children with medical complexity (CMC) to live at home, but previous research has linked implanted tubes to patient safety events. We aimed to characterize challenges and strategies parents use to deliver their children’s tube-related care at home and how parents communicate about their experiences to identify system-level intervention opportunities. METHODS We conducted a qualitative study using virtual contextual inquiry to asynchronously observe parents through self-submitted photos, text-based messages, or audio recordings with a national sample of English- and Spanish-speaking parents of CMC. Over 1 week, parents responded to twice-daily surveys soliciting messages about their child’s tube-related care. Parents were subsequently interviewed to discuss messages. Content analysis characterized parent challenges and strategies employed for safety. RESULTS We enrolled 21 parents from individual families, received 267 total messages, and completed 18 interviews. Overall, 13% (n = 36) of messages were challenges; 57% (n = 151) depicted strategies to care for CMC at home; and 26% (n = 70) were both. Challenges included supply issues (24%, n = 25), devices not working as intended (22%, n = 23), and irregularities in care experienced as normal (20%, n = 21). Strategies were personalized and creative and included supporting CMC’s activities of daily living (63%, n = 139), organization techniques (42%, n = 93), and tube-related preparation (40%, n = 89). Parents often did not share challenges and strategies with their child’s care team. CONCLUSIONS Parents of CMC navigate patient safety challenges during daily tube-related care and create strategies to mitigate safety risks. Challenges at home demand multipronged systemic intervention; findings highlight creative, independent, and resourceful parent-developed strategies.

items.title: Interventions to Support Parents Whose Babies Cry Excessively: Systematic Review
items.abstract: CONTEXT Parents report that around 10% to 20% of babies cry a lot without an apparent reason during early infancy. This “excessive” infant crying can lead to adverse outcomes, including parental depression, breastfeeding cessation, impaired parent–child relationships, and, in extreme cases, infant abuse. Cost-effective parent-support services are needed. OBJECTIVE To assess the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of interventions designed to support parents of excessively crying babies. DATA SOURCES MEDLINE, Embase, EconLit, Web of Science, Scopus, PsycINFO, CINAHL and CENTRAL were searched from inception to 8th April 2025. The NIHR CRN database and handsearching were used to identify further studies. STUDY SELECTION Comparative studies reporting parental outcomes for any intervention supporting parents of excessively crying infants aged ≤1 year were included. DATA EXTRACTION Two independent reviewers conducted data extraction and assessed risk of bias. Meta-analysis was performed when possible; otherwise, narrative synthesis was conducted. RESULTS Meta-analysis found that educational interventions significantly reduced parental stress or anxiety. Narrative analyses produced mixed findings, but components common to successful educational interventions were indicated. Meta-analyses of studies administering probiotics to infants found significant improvements in parents’ quality of life but not in parental depression. No safety data and limited economic evidence were found. LIMITATIONS Few studies measured similar enough parental outcomes to be pooled in meta-analysis. Risk of bias ranged from unclear to high risk. CONCLUSIONS Educational and probiotic interventions show promise for supporting parents of excessively crying babies. Additional controlled trials employing evidence-based interventions and outcome measures and cost-effectiveness analyses are needed to build on these findings.

items.title: Immune Immaturity and Eustachian Tube Function in the Otitis-Prone Child: A Conceptual Framework
Social Risk Screening and Referrals in the Pediatric Inpatient Setting
items.abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES Many professional organizations recently recommended inpatient screening for social risks. Although prior studies have explored social risk screening rates in children’s hospitals, many excluded community hospitals and lacked detail on screening practices. We aimed to describe national social risk screening and referral practices among hospitals caring for children. METHODS We conducted a cross-sectional survey (August 2023-November 2023) through the Pediatric Research in Inpatient Settings Network. One clinical leader per institution was surveyed on inpatient social risk screening and referral processes, populations, tools and data tracking, and barriers/facilitators to social care. Descriptive statistics summarized survey responses. RESULTS Of the hospitals contacted, 80.2% (77/96) completed the survey. Overall, 66.7% of hospitals reported screening for social risks in some capacity, most commonly performed by nurses. Screening tools and domains varied widely, with 21.9% using a published tool and 12.5% using internally developed questions. Food insecurity was the most frequently screened domain (91.9%), whereas screening for legal needs was least common (0%). Most hospitals had systems to refer patients to in-hospital (98.4%) and out-of-hospital (96.8%) services, primarily through social work consultations (96.5%) and printed handouts (54.4%). Fewer than 10% partnered with community-based organizations. Less than 45% of screening hospitals had a data-tracking system for referrals, and only 2.5% collected patient health care use data. Staffing was the most cited barrier to screening. CONCLUSIONS Social risk screening and referral practices vary widely among hospitals caring for children. Standardized policies and support mechanisms may reduce variability and promote equitable social care practices across hospitals.

items.title: The 2026 Joseph W St Geme Jr Leadership Award Speech: Now Is the Time
items.abstract: The following is an address given by the 2026 recipient of the Joseph W St Geme Jr Leadership Award, presented by the Federation of Pediatric Organizations at the Pediatric Academic Societies’ meeting on April 24, 2026.

items.title: Costs of RSV-Associated Hospitalizations in Young Children With Underlying Medical Conditions
Problematic Social Media Use and Depression Symptoms in Younger Teens: It’s a 2-Way Street
Problematic Social Media Use and Depressive and Anxiety Symptoms in Adolescents
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE Given limited longitudinal data on social media use and mental health, this study examined within-person lagged associations between problematic social media use and depressive and anxiety symptoms across 5 annual assessments among adolescents. METHODS This prospective cohort study used data from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development Study, years 2 to 6. The analytic sample included 11 279 participants (aged 12.01 ± 0.66 at year 2; 47.6% female) with at least 1 measure of problematic social media use and depressive or anxiety symptoms across years 2 to 6. RESULTS Across 5 years, random-intercept cross-lagged panel models (RI-CLPMs) indicated positive bidirectional lagged associations between problematic social media use and depressive symptoms from year 3 to year 4 and from year 4 to year 5. No significant cross-lagged associations were observed from year 2 to year 3 or from year 5 to year 6. For anxiety symptoms, no significant cross-lagged associations were observed across years. In multigroup RI-CLPMs, sex differences were observed in both models, but stronger cross-lagged associations among female than male participants were specific to depressive symptoms. CONCLUSIONS Problematic social media use and depressive symptoms showed year-specific bidirectional lagged associations, whereas within-person prospective associations between problematic social media use and anxiety symptoms were not observed. Sex differences were more apparent for depressive symptoms, for which lagged associations were stronger and more consistently bidirectional among female participants. Clinical and policy efforts should prioritize problematic features of social media use and consider developmental timing and sex-specific risk profiles in screening and intervention.

items.title: Oral Health for Adolescents: Technical Report
items.abstract: Excellent oral health is a fundamental need for all adolescents as they gain health independence and autonomy. Pediatricians already perform an essential and vital function by incorporating an oral health history, physical examination, and anticipatory guidance into adolescent well visits. This technical report provides support for this work, as highlighted in the clinical report, with an overview on adolescent oral health including growth and development, medical issues, and treatments for adolescents with complex medical needs.

items.title: Oral Health for Adolescents: Clinical Report
items.abstract: This clinical report marks a significant milestone in the United States, addressing oral health in the adolescent from the pediatrician’s perspective. Poor oral health can affect adolescents in many ways, including pain, missed school, overall health, and decreased social engagement. Oral health issues particularly pertinent to adolescents include oral sports injury prevention, orthodontic issues, and certain behaviors contributing to poor oral health outcomes. This statement will provide pediatricians: Evidence-based information on practice-based skills for the prevention and management of oral health issues in adolescent patients. Recommendations to incorporate these skills in the health supervision visit.

items.title: Driving Legislative Change for Access to Medications
items.abstract: An insurance company denied coverage for an inflammatory bowel disease medication, stating that the lack of a pediatric Food and Drug Administration indication made that treatment experimental. This was legally permissible. The patient’s pediatric gastroenterologist partnered with others to create a new state law that mandated insurance coverage for medications in children when the treatment was covered for adult patients and there were data to support pediatric efficacy and safety. Coalition building included support from a hospital system, community petitions, and interactions with legislators. Family and physician testimony supported passage of the law, in effect since 2023. The patient was able to obtain the necessary treatment, and the law has been used to help other children gain access to prescribed treatments. This process can serve as a model for similar advocacy in other states.

items.title: Prehospital Pediatric Ventilation Quality Following Use of a Feedback Device: A Randomized Study
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE Manual ventilation is a lifesaving intervention for children in respiratory arrest, yet the quality of pediatric ventilation delivered by emergency medical services (EMS) clinicians across geographically distinct sites is poorly characterized. We evaluated baseline EMS ventilation performance and whether a ventilation feedback device (VFD) improves adherence to national and international ventilation guidelines for ventilation rate, tidal volume, and mask seal. METHODS We conducted a single-anonymized, randomized, crossover study of EMS clinicians from 5 EMS agencies across 3 metropolitan sites in the United States. Using a simulated 3-year-old toddler manikin, participants completed 2 sequential 2-minute respiratory arrest scenarios separated by a 10-minute washout period. Participants performed ventilation with and without real-time VFD feedback in randomized order. The EOLifeX VFD recorded ventilation rate, tidal volume, and mask leak with each breath. Adherence to age-based guidelines was analyzed using generalized linear mixed-effects models with participants nested within sites. RESULTS We enrolled 123 participants across 5 agencies. With VFD feedback, guideline-recommended tidal volumes were achieved in 87% of breaths compared with 16.2% without feedback. Ventilation rate adherence improved from 65% to 88.6%. Mask leak of less than 30% occurred in 88.4% of ventilations with feedback vs 80% without feedback. CONCLUSION In our simulation study, EMS clinicians rarely met manual ventilation guidelines for pediatric patients in respiratory arrest. The use of a VFD substantially improved guideline adherence, suggesting broad potential to improve ventilation performance.

items.title: Paraneoplastic Autoimmune Multiorgan Syndrome: Diagnostic Lessons for Pediatricians
items.abstract: We report the challenging diagnosis of an 11-year-old boy, presenting with subacute erythroblastopenia, followed by a multisystemic immune-mediated syndrome characterized by polymorphic mucocutaneous manifestations, associated with severe myositis related to a dermatomyositis-like phenotype and mild hepatitis. A progressive lymphadenopathy led to a delayed diagnosis of T-lymphoblastic lymphoma associated with paraneoplastic autoimmune multiorgan syndrome. To achieve remission of this paraneoplastic syndrome, Janus kinase inhibitor was required in addition to antitumor therapy. This case highlights several key points: (1) Pediatricians should consider a paraneoplastic origin when facing juvenile dermatomyositis with atypical features, such as hematologic and mucosal abnormalities; (2) in uncertain cases, early collaboration with oncologists is needed to optimize diagnostic and therapeutic strategies; (3) the choice of immunomodulatory therapy is critical in addition to antitumor therapy.

items.title: Experiences of Ableism in Pediatric Healthcare
items.abstract: BACKGROUND There is growing evidence of ableism in pediatric health care, but our limited understanding of the experiences of ableism inhibits further evaluation and intervention. The study objective was to describe community perspectives of the experiences of ableism in pediatric health care for children with disabilities. METHODS Participants completed a group concept mapping study using web-based software to input experiences of ableism in health care. Following a formal statement reduction, participants sorted unique experiences into conceptual clusters. Data were mapped to generate a similarity matrix. A multidimensional scaling algorithm generated a point map, and a hierarchical cluster analysis grouped statements into clusters. Focus groups validated and labeled clusters. RESULTS Participants (n = 132) generated 658 statements about ableism experiences. After reduction, 145 experiences were categorized in 11 conceptually distinct clusters: 1) substandard care including withholding care, 2) dehumanizing language and behaviors, 3) negative assumptions, 4) inflexible organizational policies and practices, 5) inaccessible built environment and lack of accommodations, 6) lack of access to resources, 7) unfair standards and normalized inequity in health systems, 8) dismissal of the lived experience and caregiver expertise, 9) intersectional identities and judgements of worthiness to receive care, 10) restrictions driven by insurance coverage and policy, and 11) complexity in community and health services navigation. CONCLUSIONS Wide-ranging experiences of ableism occur in pediatric health care interactions. The lived experiences of ableism identified in this study provide insight for future research in pediatric health care.

items.title: Ableism is a Crisis in American Pediatric Health Care
A Neonate With Excessive Weight Loss and Electrolyte Abnormalities
items.abstract: A 7-day-old girl was brought to the hospital for excessive weight loss. Initial evaluation revealed electrolyte abnormalities, including hyponatremia and hyperkalemia. Stepwise assessment was undertaken to evaluate potential endocrine, renal, and metabolic causes, with supportive interventions initiated. Over the course of hospitalization, her electrolytes and weight gradually improved. Further workup, including imaging and genetic testing, was performed to clarify the underlying etiology. Our panel of experts first discuss the approach to weight loss in neonates and then review the assessment and management of neonatal electrolyte disturbances, highlighting endocrine, renal, and genetic considerations that may guide clinical care.

items.title: The Community Pediatrics & Advocacy Curriculum: Standardizing Advocacy Education in Pediatric GME
items.abstract: Pediatricians are essential advocates for their patients in many contexts. The evolving role of the pediatrician as an advocate has led to a distinct need for the development and standardization of advocacy curricula in pediatric graduate medical education. With an increased emphasis placed by the Accreditation Council on Graduate Medical Education and the American Board of Pediatrics on advocacy as an essential skill for general and subspecialty pediatricians, the authors provide a framework for pediatric advocacy education based on a new socioecological model of pediatrician advocacy. The authors highlight the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP)’s history of advocacy curriculum development and how it has shaped the approach to advocacy training in the field of pediatrics over the last 2 decades. A curricular framework, including goals, learning objectives, and exemplar activities, was developed from this previous work and compiled through expert consensus and further peer review by experts identified through the AAP’s Community Pediatrics Training Initiative. The current paper outlines the process of curating these tools, thereby creating an accessible and feasible baseline for programs.

items.title: Coverage Trends by Citizenship Status Among Medicaid Income-Eligible Children: 2012–2024
items.abstract: OBJECTIVES To evaluate coverage correlates and trends by citizenship status among a nationally representative sample of Medicaid income-eligible children. We also examined the associations of coverage policies, including the Affordable Care Act’s (ACA’s) Medicaid expansion and state-level expansions to children regardless of immigration status, with children’s coverage outcomes. METHODS This repeated cross-sectional study used multivariable logistic regression analysis and 2012 to 2024 American Community Survey data. The main sample included children aged 1 to 17 years in all US states with household incomes under the Medicaid income eligibility limit. Binary outcomes included uninsured, Medicaid, and private coverage. RESULTS From 2012 to 2024, uninsurance declined from 37.9% to 31.0% among noncitizen children and from 8.2% to 6.1% among citizen children; the coverage gap by citizenship consistently exceeded 20 percentage points. Factors associated with lower uninsured rates among noncitizen children included high parental English proficiency, higher socioeconomic status, living in a metropolitan area, and non-Hispanic Asian ethnicity. The ACA’s Medicaid expansion was associated with lower uninsured rates among citizen children, but associations were not statistically significant overall or among noncitizen children. State coverage expansions to children regardless of immigration status were associated with an 8.2 percentage-point reduction in the uninsured rate (95% CI −12.5 to −4.0) before and after their implementation among noncitizen children. CONCLUSIONS Significant and persistent coverage gaps by citizenship remain among Medicaid income-eligible children. Gaps were substantially ameliorated, although not completely eliminated, in states that expanded their Medicaid programs to cover children regardless of immigration status.

items.title: Vaccine-Induced Antibody and T Cell Immunity to Measles and Varicella in Children With ALL
Hydrocephalus: Treatment, Current Research, and Challenges
items.abstract: Hydrocephalus is a complex neurological condition characterized by derangements in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) dynamics including disrupted CSF flow/absorption and/or excess CSF production that leads to ventricular enlargement and presents both diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Its origins span from congenital anomalies to acquired cases following hemorrhage, infection, or tumors. Hydrocephalus is suspected in the setting of appropriate clinical signs/symptoms, and the diagnosis is confirmed with brain imaging and, in rare cases, invasive intracranial pressure monitoring. Surgical intervention is the mainstay of modern hydrocephalus management, with CSF diversion via an implanted shunt being the most common management strategy. However, for a subset of patients, endoscopic third ventriculostomy can also effectively manage hydrocephalus without the need for an implanted device. This article highlights both genetic and acquired forms of hydrocephalus, reviews the surgical interventions for managing hydrocephalus and commercially available shunt technologies, discusses the shortcomings of current management strategies, and explores the ongoing development of next-generation shunt technology including smart shunts and antifouling catheter coatings that aim to reduce shunt malfunction rates. Additionally, we review current bench research investigating the cellular/molecular mechanisms involved in hydrocephalus induction including studies on ventricular lining disruption and the role of aquaporins in hydrocephalus.

items.title: Frontline Staff Vaccine Communication During Pediatric Well-Child Encounters: A Mixed-Methods Study
items.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES Evidence-based vaccine communication from clinicians is associated with improved parental vaccine acceptance. However, vaccine communication practices of frontline staff, including medical assistants (MAs) and receptionists, remain largely unknown. We aimed to characterize these practices during well-child encounters in pediatric primary care. METHODS We conducted a mixed-methods study with direct observations of frontline staff in 2 pediatric practices in Denver, CO, during well-child encounters in the summer (no influenza vaccine available) and fall (influenza vaccine available) of 2024, recording the frequency and format of vaccine communication. Following the observations, we conducted semi-structured interviews with MAs to explore their vaccine communication practices, perceived roles, comfort, and training. RESULTS We observed 174 encounters (127 MA–parent, 47 receptionist–parent interactions). Vaccine communication occurred in at least 51% (95% CI, 43%–60%) of MA interactions vs 6% of receptionist interactions (P < .001). When vaccines were recommended, MAs used a presumptive format in 46% (95% CI, 34%–59%) of encounters overall, but far less during influenza season (21% vs 76%; P < .001). Interviews revealed that MA communication styles evolved through on-the-job experience and peer-to-peer learning rather than formal training, with influenza vaccines treated as optional rather than routinely recommended. CONCLUSIONS MAs frequently communicate with parents about vaccines during well-child encounters but underutilize evidence-based presumptive communication, particularly for influenza vaccines. Communication practices are learned informally through peer-to-peer learning, highlighting a significant opportunity for targeted training to support team-based vaccine communication in pediatric primary care.

items.title: Immunogenicity and Safety of PHH-1V COVID-19 Vaccine as a Heterologous Booster in Adolescents
items.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES PHH-1V, a protein-based, non-mRNA, bivalent, adjuvanted COVID-19 vaccine, has demonstrated strong immunogenicity and favorable safety as a booster in adults. This study evaluated PHH-1V as a heterologous booster in adolescents. METHODS HIPRA-HH-3 was a phase IIb, open-label, multicenter, noninferiority trial assessing the immunogenicity and safety of PHH-1V in 240 healthy adolescents (≥ 12 to < 18 years) primed with BNT162b2. Immunogenicity (N = 90) was assessed by measuring neutralizing antibodies against SARS-CoV-2 variants and total binding antibodies in adolescent participants vs young adults (≥ 18 to ≤ 25 years) (N = 81) from a previous trial, who had also been boosted with PHH-1V. T-cell responses at day 14 post booster were also evaluated. Antibody durability and adverse events (AEs) were assessed through day 336. RESULTS Neutralizing titers—against Omicron BA.1 (primary endpoint), WH1, Beta, and Delta variants—and total binding antibodies were significantly higher in adolescents than in young adults (P < .001), demonstrating noninferiority (margin < 1.5). T-cell responses against BA.1 and Beta also increased significantly (P < .001). Cross-variant antibody titers remained above baseline (day 0) through day 336. AEs were mostly mild/moderate, primarily injection-site pain and headache within 28 days. No related serious AEs were reported. CONCLUSIONS As a heterologous booster in adolescents, PHH-1V is safe and elicits cellular and sustained humoral responses with cross-variant immune recognition, which support the use of PHH-1V in adolescent vaccination strategies. Data in younger and specific risk groups are still needed.

items.title: Reasons for Nicotine Pouch Use Among US Youth: 2025
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE To document prevalence of reasons for nicotine pouch (NP) use and associations with use patterns among US youth. METHODS Data were from US youth reporting ever NP use in the nationally representative 2025 Monitoring the Future survey. We estimated (1) prevalence of 10 reasons for NP use (yes/no) and (2) association of each reason with past 30-day NP use (yes/no) and frequency (1–30 days). For comparison, we contrasted reasons for NP and e-cigarette use among youth reporting NP use (n = 57) or e-cigarette use (n = 397) on at least 10 of the past 30 days. RESULTS Among 484 respondents reporting ever NP use (6.1% of youth surveyed on NP use and reasons), the most common reasons were experimentation (32.3%), nicotine buzz (30.5%), relaxation (22.7%), appealing flavors (17.4%), convenience (16.5%), socializing (16.0%), boredom (11.7%), and ability to conceal use (11.0%). To quit smoking (6.2%) and feeling addicted (2.1%) were less common. Flavors, convenience, and feeling addicted were positively associated with both past 30-day NP use (prevalence ratios [PRs] range = 1.50–2.35) and frequency (incidence rate ratios [IRRs] range = 1.60–2.55). Nicotine buzz, relaxation, socializing, concealment, and to quit smoking were only associated with past 30-day use (PRs range = 1.57–1.85). Experimentation was inversely associated with frequency (IRR = 0.42). The prevalence of reasons overlapped between NPs and e-cigarettes, with relaxation, convenience, nicotine buzz, and flavors most prevalent among youth regularly using each product. CONCLUSIONS Prevention and regulatory strategies addressing NP use reasons, particularly flavors and convenience, are warranted. Existing effective strategies targeting youth nicotine vaping may be applicable to NP use.

items.title: Children and Families Affected by Parental Substance Use: Clinical Report
items.abstract: Children and adolescents whose parents have an alcohol or substance use disorder are at increased risk of short- and long-term sequelae, ranging from medical conditions to psychosocial, safety, and behavioral challenges. In the course of providing health care services to children, pediatricians and other pediatric clinicians are likely to encounter families affected by parental substance use and are in a unique position to support the well-being of both the child and family. The purpose of this clinical report is to briefly discuss the epidemiology of substance use during pregnancy and while parenting in the United States; highlight the influence of bias, racism, and other structural inequities on families affected by substance use; describe the known risks associated with prenatal and postnatal parental substance use; discuss use and interpretation of toxicology testing as part of a substance exposure evaluation; review approaches to screening for prenatal and parental substance use; propose key topics for anticipatory guidance in the pediatric clinic; identify and address concerning parental and child presentations related to parental substance use leading to concern for child abuse or neglect; and provide recommendations for pediatric clinicians involved in the care of children from families affected by substance use.

items.title: Pediatric Hospital at Home: A Scoping Review
items.abstract: CONTEXT Hospital at Home (HaH) is an acute care model that delivers hospital-level services to the patient’s home as a substitute for conventional inpatient admission. Although pediatric HaH programs are well established internationally, the evidence base remains limited. OBJECTIVE To map the operational characteristics, outcomes, and evidence gaps of pediatric HaH programs. DATA SOURCES A comprehensive literature search was conducted for studies published between January 1, 2000, and July 25, 2025. STUDY SELECTION Eligible studies included programs with patients aged 18 years or younger and aligned with the World Hospital at Home Congress definition. DATA EXTRACTION Data were extracted on study characteristics; implementation, infrastructure, and program design; clinical safety and effectiveness; cost-effectiveness and economic impact; and patient, caregiver, and/or clinician perspectives and experiences. RESULTS Thirty-four studies met eligibility criteria. Most were observational, with few randomized or nonrandomized controlled studies. Programs varied substantially in admission pathways, staffing, eligibility criteria, monitoring, and clinical populations. Studies demonstrated low escalation and readmission rates, infrequent serious adverse events, high caregiver satisfaction, and generally comparable or lower health care costs relative to conventional inpatient care. Few studies directly evaluated clinical effectiveness, included rigorous economic analysis, or incorporated child and clinician perspectives. LIMITATIONS The literature was limited by heterogeneous study populations, program designs, outcome reporting, and variable definitions and descriptions of HaH models, introducing potential for misclassification. CONCLUSIONS Pediatric HaH shows promise as a safe and family-centered alternative to conventional hospitalization, though the existing evidence remains limited and heterogeneous, highlighting the need for more rigorous evaluation.

items.title: Developmental Trajectories of Executive Function From 2 to 13 Years in Children Born Very Preterm
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE Children born very preterm (VP; <32 weeks’ gestation) are at risk of executive function (EF) difficulties, yet limited longitudinal research has examined how these evolve from early childhood to adolescence for this population. This study described developmental trajectories of parent-reported EF from ages 2 to 13 years in children born VP and full term (FT). METHODS Participants were from the Victorian Infant Brain Study (VIBeS) longitudinal cohort comprising 224 children born VP (<30 weeks’ gestation) and 77 born FT (≥37 weeks’ gestation). EF difficulties were measured at 2, 5, 7, and 13 years using the parent-rated Behavior Rating Inventory of Executive Function (BRIEF) and its preschool version. Trajectories were estimated using multilevel mixed effects models. RESULTS EF difficulties were 0.3 to 0.7 SD higher in the VP than FT group across all BRIEF scales at each follow-up, and this difference tended to be greater in boys and those with higher socioeconomic risk. For both VP and FT groups, Global Executive Composite (GEC) and Shift T-scores increased from 2 to 13 years, Inhibit and Working Memory T-scores remained largely stable, and Emotional Control and Plan/Organize T-scores increased between 2 and 7 before stabilizing between 7 and 13 years. CONCLUSION Children born VP showed persistent EF difficulties from early childhood into adolescence, with little evidence of developmental catch-up to FT peers. These findings highlight the need for early and ongoing monitoring and intervention throughout development. Further research is needed to understand the role of sex and socioeconomic risk in the developmental course of behavioral EF difficulties.

items.title: Zika-Related Microcephaly in the First 5 Years After Birth
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE To characterize clinical manifestations and complications of children with Zika-related microcephaly in the first 5 years after birth. METHODS A cohort of children with Zika-related microcephaly were observed up to age 60 months as part of the Microcephaly Epidemic Research Group Pediatric Cohort. RESULTS Among the 181 children, 43.1% were male and 77.2% were born at term. The median birth weight was 2700 g, with 64.8% classified as small for gestational age. Notably, 22.3% were diagnosed with microcephaly after birth, and 48.8% had severe microcephaly. Most common phenotypic characteristics were craniofacial disproportion (54.1%), arthrogryposis (35.9%), and exacerbated occipital protuberance (35.5%). Approximately one-third (33.1%) presented with dysphagia (n = 151 evaluated at median age of 28.2 months), and 13.3% of children had gastrostomies (median age of 24 months). Hearing anomalies were detected in 9.7% (n = 93 evaluated at median age of 30 months). In ophthalmological evaluation, 30.4% showed changes in the retina and 28.5% in the optic nerve; strabismus was observed in 53.4%. During neurological assessment (median age at first assessment of 15.9 months), 73.8% presented with abnormalities. Imaging examinations showed ventriculomegaly and cortical atrophy in 75.3% and 64.4% of the children, respectively. Electroencephalography was performed based on clinical indication in 84 children, of whom 92.9% had pattern alterations. Over the 5 years, 62.4% were hospitalized, mainly for respiratory problems and seizures. CONCLUSIONS The study highlights the severity of Zika-related microcephaly. Future research should prioritize continued systematic monitoring of these children to understand the frequency and timing of late-onset manifestations and complications, including death.

items.title: Dual Remission of Atopic Dermatitis and Frequently Relapsing Nephrotic Syndrome With Dupilumab
items.abstract: Nephrotic syndrome in children and atopic dermatitis (AD) share a common type 2 inflammatory substrate driven by interleukin (IL)-4 and IL-13 dysregulation. We report the case of a 9-year-old girl with AD and frequently relapsing steroid-sensitive nephrotic syndrome. Given the broad atopic phenotype and increasing relapse frequency despite dual immunosuppressive therapy, dupilumab 300 mg every 2 weeks was introduced. The patient achieved rapid and complete clearance of cutaneous lesions alongside sustained complete remission of nephrotic syndrome, maintained over nearly 2 years. Both corticosteroids and tacrolimus were fully discontinued within 2 months of dupilumab initiation, with no subsequent relapse of either condition. This case supports the hypothesis that dupilumab may represent an effective steroid-sparing therapeutic option in children with nephrotic syndrome arising in an atopic context.

Hemodynamic Patterns Relative to Vasopressin Initiation and Subsequent Septic Shock Progression in Children: A Retrospective Cohort, 2020–2023
items.abstract: Objectives: To describe the hemodynamic patterns associated with starting vasopressin in children with septic shock and to compare the early patterns based on subsequent progression of shock. Design: Retrospective cohort (2020–2023) study. Setting: Single-center, tertiary PICU in Australia. Patients: Children younger than 18 years with septic shock. Interventions: None. Measurements and Main Results: Hemodynamic variables collected at 1-minute intervals during a 1-hour observation period after starting vasopressin infusion were reviewed and collated according to whether shock subsequently progressed in the following 5 hours. In a cohort of 30 children (median age, 9 yr [interquartile range, 2–14 yr]), eight had shock progression, which was defined by echocardiography, lactate, and use of extracorporeal support. Cases with subsequent shock progression, as opposedto not, had an associated higher Phoenix score (7 [7–8] vs. 6 [5–6]; p = 0.01). The vasopressin starting dose in the shock vs. nonshock progression groups was 0.03 U/kg/hr (0.02–0.06 U/kg/hr) vs. 0.02 U/kg/hr (0.02–0.04 U/kg/hr; p = 0.72). We failed to find an association between ventricular dysfunction at baseline and the shock progression group vs. no shock progression (4/6 vs. 7/18; mean difference, 28%; 95% CI, –16% to 71%; p = 0.36). In the shock progression group, earlier pulse pressure continued on a decreasing trajectory following vasopressin initiation, despite increasing systolic and diastolic blood pressures. In those without shock progression, pulse pressure increased marginally. The difference between groups in the median pulse pressures during the observation period was 7.5 mm Hg. Conclusions: In this hypothesis-generating, retrospective study of children with septic shock treated with vasopressin, subsequent shock progression was associated with early decreasing pulse pressure. Further studies are needed to test whether early changes in pulse pressure after starting vasopressin can be used as a potential marker of subsequent shock progression.

Timing of the Adrenaline Administration in Witnessed Pediatric Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: Retrospective, National Cohort Study in Japan, Using a 2014–2020 Dataset
items.abstract: Objectives: We evaluated the association between the timing of initial adrenaline administration and outcomes in witnessed pediatric out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA). Design: A multicenter, retrospective cohort study addressing resuscitation time bias by performing a risk-set matching analysis using time-dependent propensity scores. Setting: Analysis of data from the Japanese Association for Acute Medicine OHCA (JAAM-OHCA) registry, which is a nationwide, multicenter, prospective collection of prehospital and in-hospital data involving Japanese patients with OHCA. Patients: Pediatric patients (< 18 yr) with witnessed OHCA who received adrenaline, during the period June 2014 to December 2020. Interventions: None. Measurements and Main Results: We compared patients who received adrenaline in specific time intervals (1–10, 11–15, 16–20, 21–25, or 26–30 min) after first contact with emergency medical services with those who still had not received adrenaline during the same time. The primary and secondary outcomes were survival and favorable neurologic outcome at one month, defined as a Pediatric Cerebral Performance Category score of 1–3. We identified a total of 259 OHCA patients who had received adrenaline at 1–10, 11–15, 16–20, 21–25, 26–30, and 31 minutes or later; at each respective time point, there were 15, 39, 62, 55, 37, and 51 patients. Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% CIs for 1-month survival at each time group compared with patients at risk were: 1–10 minutes, RR, 2.94 (95% CI, 0.38–22.81); 11–15 minutes, RR, 0.97 (95% CI, 0.30–3.12); 16–20 minutes, RR, 1.00 (95% CI, 0.29–3.48); 21–25 minutes, RR, 1.35 (95% CI, 0.54–3.40); and 26–30 minutes, RR, 1.71 (95% CI, 0.27–10.78). We failed to identify an association between time interval and greater or lesser probability of survival or neurologic outcome. Conclusions: In the JAAM-OHCA registry, with pediatric data from 2014 to 2020, we failed to identify an association between earlier adrenaline administration and greater probability of 1-month survival or favorable neurologic outcomes.

MYL9 silencing inhibits proliferation and migration of lung adenocarcinoma cells: a potential therapeutic target
items.abstract: Background: Myosin light chain 9 (MYL9), a regulatory light chain of myosin II, plays a crucial role in cytoskeletal dynamics and has been associated with tumor progression in multiple malignancies. However, its role in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains poorly characterized. Despite recent advances in treatment, the prognosis of LUAD patients remains poor, underscoring the need for novel therapeutic targets.Methods: Here, we systematically assessed MYL9 expression and its clinical relevance in LUAD by integrating transcriptomic data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and protein-level validation from the Human Protein Atlas (HPA) via immunohistochemistry. Functional investigations in H1299 cells indicated that silencing MYL9 significantly impeded cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, as corroborated by colony formation and Transwell assays. In vivo xenograft models further verified that MYL9 knockdown inhibited tumor growth and triggered apoptosis. Bioinformatic analyses, including the ESTIMATE algorithm, single-sample gene set enrichment analysis (ssGSEA), and drug sensitivity profiling, were also performed.Results: In addition to its oncogenic impacts, bioinformatic analyses demonstrated that elevated MYL9 expression is correlated with distinct immune infiltration patterns and diminished chemosensitivity, possibly through the modulation of the tumor microenvironment. These findings suggest that MYL9 may link cytoskeletal regulation with tumor progression, immune remodeling, and treatment response in LUAD.Conclusions: Collectively, these findings recognize MYL9 as a novel prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target in LUAD, providing insights into its multifaceted role in tumor biology and treatment response. Further studies are warranted to validate these findings in larger clinical cohorts and to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms.

items.title: Clinical and prognostic characteristics of concurrent small cell lung cancer in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis: a retrospective study
items.abstract: Background: Lung cancer (LC) is a comorbidity that seriously affects the prognosis of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) patients. Small cell LC (SCLC) accounts for the highest proportion of hospitalized LC patients with concurrent IPF at Peking Union Medical College Hospital (PUMCH). To enable effective and standardized management of patients with IPF and SCLC, this study aims to summarize the clinical and prognostic characteristics of IPF-SCLC patients to improve their prognosis.Methods: We retrospectively enrolled patients with IPF (diagnosed by 2022 ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT criteria)-SCLC (pathologically confirmed) admitted to PUMCH from January 2014 to December 2023. Clinical manifestation, chest computed tomography (CT) imaging, laboratory test, treatment and outcome data of patients with IPF-SCLC were collected and reviewed in detail with final follow-up on June 30, 2024.Results: Forty patients with IPF-SCLC were included with the average age of 68.2±6.3 years (range, 54 to 82 years). And there were 37 (92.5%) males. Median follow-up time was 12.0 months. Additionally, 35 (87.5%) patients had a smoking history. Twenty-eight (70.0%) IPF-SCLC patients were concurrent with one or more other underlying diseases. Emphysema was detected in 26 (65%) patients via chest CT. IPF and SCLC were diagnosed during the same period in 23 (57.5%) patients, whereas SCLC was diagnosed during the follow-up of IPF in the remaining 17 patients. However, pirfenidone and nintedanib were only prescribed to two patients, respectively. Most patients were diagnosed with late-stage SCLC: 17 (42.5%) patients had stage IV SCLC, and 15 (37.5%) patients had stage III SCLC. Furthermore, with respect to anticancer therapy, one (2.5%) patient received no chemotherapy, 2 (5%) patients received oral etoposide, 37 (92.5%) patients received intravenous chemotherapy, and 11 (27.5%) patients received pulmonary radiotherapy. Finally, 29 (72.5%) patients died during follow-up. The main causes of death were acute exacerbation of IPF (AE-IPF) (13 patients, 44.8%) and progression of SCLC (12 patients, 41.4%).Conclusions: The patients with IPF-SCLC included in our studies were mainly elderly males with a heavy smoking index, most of whom were diagnosed with late-stage SCLC. Antifibrotic medications for IPF were uncommon, and chemotherapy was the main cancer treatment. The progression of uncontrolled SCLC and AE-IPF were the main causes of death. Clinicians should consider early initiation of antifibrotic therapy alongside chemotherapy, monitor for the occurrence of AE-IPF, and adopt multidisciplinary management.

items.title: Development and internal validation of a prediction model for severe postoperative complications (Thoracic Morbidity and Mortality Grade ≥ III) after radical esophagectomy
items.abstract: Background: This study aimed to explore the independent predictors for severe postoperative complications [Thoracic Morbidity and Mortality (TM&M) Grade ≥III] after radical esophagectomy and to develop and internally validate an early risk-prediction nomogram. Methods: Clinical data from 606 consecutive patients (2019–2025) were analyzed. Severe complications were defined as TM&M grade ≥ III within 30 days after surgery. Candidate predictors, measured at baseline and from venous blood collected at 06:00 AM on postoperative day (POD) 1, included demographics, surgical variables, and inflammatory biomarkers. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression with 10-fold cross-validation was embedded within a 1,000-bootstrap internal validation framework to avoid data leakage, followed by multivariable logistic regression. Results: Severe complications occurred in 178 patients (29.4%). Age [adjusted odds ratio (OR) =1.04], operative time (OR =1.04 per 10-min increase), and non-middle tumor location (OR =1.58) were independent predictors (all P<0.05). Female sex (OR =0.60), neoadjuvant therapy (OR =0.52), and POD 1 lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratio (D1-LMR, OR =0.76) were protective factors. The nomogram yielded an apparent AUC of 0.685 (95% confidence interval: 0.635–0.735) and a bootstrap optimism-corrected AUC of 0.672. At the optimal cutoff of 0.28 determined by the Youden index, sensitivity was 68.5%, specificity 63.4%, positive predictive value 45.2%, and negative predictive value 82.1%. Calibration was excellent (calibration slope =0.942, intercept =0.018, Brier score =0.184). Adding D1-LMR significantly improved predictive performance over baseline clinical models (ΔAUC =0.034, net reclassification improvement =0.158, P=0.008). Decision curve analysis confirmed positive net clinical benefits across threshold probabilities of 2–45%. Conclusions: Integrating baseline features and D1-LMR, this nomogram provides an exploratory early risk-stratification tool on POD 1 to optimize perioperative management and intensive care unit resource allocation.

items.title: Association between early vein graft failure and long-term major adverse cardiovascular events following off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting: an exploratory retrospective cohort study
items.abstract: Background: Early vein graft failure (VGF) following coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) is far from rare and often clinically silent. While mid-to-late graft failure is established to predict adverse clinical events, the long-term prognostic impact of predischarge early VGF remains poorly defined. This study aimed to evaluate the association between early VGF and 10-year clinical outcomes following off-pump CABG.Methods: In this exploratory retrospective cohort study, adult patients undergoing elective isolated off-pump CABG using vein grafts with early postoperative coronary computed tomography angiography between July 2014 and December 2015 were consecutively included. Baseline, intraoperative, and postoperative data were collected from electronic medical records. VGF was defined as Fitzgibbon grade B (≥50% stenosis) or O (occlusion). Patients were stratified into the early VGF group (with at least one failed vein graft) and non-early VGF group (without failed vein grafts). Clinical follow-up was conducted through routine outpatient visits or standardized telephone interviews in accordance with institutional protocol. Primary outcomes included 10-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE, composite of all-cause death, myocardial infarction, stroke, or revascularization) and its individual components. Secondary outcomes included perioperative myocardial injury and perioperative myocardial infarction (PMI). Propensity score overlap weighting was applied to adjust for baseline confounders. Exploratory post-hoc landmark and piecewise Cox analyses were performed to address non-proportional hazards.Results: A total of 233 patients were included in the analyses (mean age 64.3±7.5 years; 18.4% female). Among them, early VGF was identified in 33 (14.2%) patients and 41 (5.9%) vein grafts. Early VGF numerically increased the risk of perioperative myocardial injury [45.5% vs. 30.5%, odds ratio (OR) 1.90, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.89–4.01; P=0.09] and PMI (12.1% vs. 6.0%, OR 2.16, 95% CI: 0.57–6.69; P=0.21), though without statistical significance. Over a median follow-up of 9.6 years, there was no statistically significant difference in 10-year MACE between the two groups [early VGF 51.5% vs. non-early VGF 48.2%; adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) 1.31, 95% CI: 0.76–2.24; P=0.33]. In exploratory landmark analyses addressing non-proportional hazards (P=0.03), early VGF was associated with a higher risk of MACE within the first 2 years post-surgery (aHR 2.18, 95% CI: 1.14–4.17; P=0.02), which attenuated beyond the 2-year landmark (aHR 0.56, 95% CI: 0.22–1.46; P=0.24). Additionally, early VGF was associated with a higher risk of repeat revascularization (18.2% vs. 7.7%; aHR 3.06, 95% CI: 1.13–8.31; P=0.03).Conclusions: Predischarge early VGF was not significantly associated with the overall 10-year risk of MACE following off-pump CABG. Exploratory findings regarding early risk clustering within 2 years and an increased risk of repeat revascularization remain hypothesis-generating. Further prospective studies are warranted to validate these observations.

items.title: Development and internal validation of a chest CT radiomics model for identifying pneumoconiosis
items.abstract: Background: Pneumoconiosis is a major occupational lung disease with an insidious onset, making early diagnosis challenging. We aimed to develop and internally validate a chest computed tomography (CT)-based radiomics model for objective identification of pneumoconiosis and to support subjective visual diagnosis in dust-exposed individuals.Methods: This retrospective study consecutively enrolled 474 patients with documented occupational dust exposure who underwent pneumoconiosis evaluation at The Third People’s Hospital of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region between January 2020 and December 2024. Eligible participants had high-resolution chest CT images and no history of pulmonary surgery or trauma; those with coexisting respiratory disease, severe systemic dysfunction, or poor image quality were excluded. The reference standard was expert-panel consensus according to GBZ 70-2015 criteria. Lung parenchyma was semi-automatically segmented using a region-growing algorithm in three-dimensional (3D) Slicer, and radiomics features were extracted with the Deepwise Multimodal Research Platform. From 2,153 features, Pearson correlation filtering (r≥0.9 excluded) and analysis of variance (ANOVA) F-test (P<0.05) selected the 10 most discriminative features. Data were randomly divided into training and test sets. A logistic regression model was constructed and evaluated using area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, calibration, and decision curve analysis (DCA).Results: Of 474 patients, 293 had pneumoconiosis (all stage I) and 181 were dust-exposed controls. The model achieved AUCs of 0.804 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.754–0.853] in the training set (n=331) and 0.759 (95% CI: 0.680–0.838) in the test set (n=143). At the optimal threshold, sensitivity and specificity were 76.2% and 68.3% in the training set and 61.8% and 67.1% in the test set, respectively. Calibration curves showed good agreement between predicted and observed outcomes, and DCA confirmed net clinical benefit across a range of threshold probabilities.Conclusions: This CT-based whole-lung radiomics model, without manual lesion delineation, shows promise for early pneumoconiosis identification in dust-exposed populations, with favorable diagnostic accuracy and clinical utility. However, the findings are preliminary and require external validation in independent multicenter cohorts before clinical implementation.

items.title: A matter of size: 20-Fr vs. 24-Fr chest drainage after uniportal video-assisted thoracoscopic lobectomy for non-small cell lung cancer—a randomized trial
items.abstract: Background: Chest drains are routinely used after pulmonary lobectomy to evacuate air and pleural fluid and promote lung re-expansion. However, the optimal chest tube caliber remains controversial, particularly in the context of minimally invasive surgery. Smaller-bore drains may reduce discomfort, whereas larger drains may provide more effective evacuation of air and fluid. The aim of this study was to compare 20-Fr and 24-Fr chest tubes after uniportal video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (uVATS) lobectomy for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), with particular focus on postoperative pain, pleural drainage-related outcomes, and recovery.Methods: This single-center prospective randomized study included 80 patients undergoing uVATS lobectomy for NSCLC, who were allocated 1:1 to receive either a 20-Fr or 24-Fr chest tube (n=40 per group). The primary outcome was postoperative pain at 24 hours, assessed using the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS). Secondary outcomes included NRS pain at 12 and 48 hours, prolonged air leak (PAL), chest tube duration, subcutaneous emphysema, analgesic requirements, respiratory physiokinesitherapy outcomes, and length of stay (LOS). Pneumothorax (PNX) and pleural effusion (PE) were evaluated as exploratory radiographic outcomes.Results: The 24-Fr group showed significantly lower rates of PNX on postoperative day (POD) 3 (27.5% vs. 60.0%, P=0.003) and PE on POD2 (50.0% vs. 77.5%, P=0.01). Conversely, patients with 24-Fr drains reported significantly higher NRS pain scores at 12 hours [4.0 (3.0–5.0) vs. 2.0 (2.0–4.0), P=0.001], 24 hours [5.0 (4.0–6.0) vs. 4.0 (3.0–5.0), P=0.002], and 48 hours [5.5 (4.8–6.2) vs. 4.5 (3.0–6.0), P=0.02].
