No significant differences were observed in PAL (27.5% vs. 47.5%, P=0.07), chest tube duration, subcutaneous emphysema, analgesic requirements, or LOS.Conclusions: After uVATS lobectomy, 24-Fr chest tubes were associated with better early radiographic pleural control but greater postoperative pain. These findings highlight a trade-off between drainage efficiency and patient comfort and support an individualized approach to chest tube selection.Trial Registration: The trial was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT07827885).

items.title: Factors associated with postoperative sleep disturbance in patients undergoing thoracoscopic radical resection for lung cancer: a retrospective cohort study
items.abstract: Background: Postoperative sleep disturbance (PSD) is common in patients following surgery, resulting in severe cognitive and mood disturbances, and even increase mortality risk. This study aimed to identify factors associated with PSD in patients undergoing thoracoscopic radical resection for lung cancer.Methods: We retrospectively identified sixty-two patients who underwent thoracoscopic radical resection of lung cancer at Tangdu Hospital, a tertiary teaching hospital in Xi’an, China, from June 2023 through October 2024. PSD was defined as a Richards-Campbell Sleep Questionnaire (RCSQ) score <60 on postoperative day 2 (POD2). Preoperative sleep quality was assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Pain was measured using the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) at rest and during coughing on POD1 and POD2. intraoperative fluid volume, and POD2 cough-induced pain, selected a priori based on clinical relevance and prior evidence. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors independently associated with PSD.Results: Of 62 patients (mean age 67.5 years; 45.2% female), 36 (58.1%) met the RCSQ-defined criteria for PSD on POD2. Three factors were independently associated with PSD: preoperative PSQI score [odds ratio (OR) =1.58, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.19–2.10, P=0.001], intraoperative fluid volume (OR =1.004 per mL, 95% CI: 1.001–1.007, P=0.02), and POD2 cough-induced pain (OR =2.23 per point, 95% CI: 1.36–3.66, P=0.001). The model demonstrated good calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow P=0.10) and discrimination (Nagelkerke R2=0.652).Conclusions: Preoperative sleep quality, intraoperative fluid volume, and POD2 cough-induced pain were independently associated with PSD in this cohort. These exploratory findings highlight the importance of closer assessment of potentially high-risk patients, but require validation in larger prospective studies before being translated into definitive preventive strategies.

items.title: Simplified synchronous division of pulmonary vessels and the horizontal fissure during thoracoscopic right upper lobectomy for lung cancer with incomplete fissure: a propensity score-matched study
items.abstract: Background: Incomplete horizontal fissure increases the technical difficulty of thoracoscopic right upper lobectomy and may increase parenchymal injury and stapler use. We evaluated a simplified synchronous disconnection of pulmonary vessels and the horizontal fissure (SSDPVH) for right upper lobe non-small cell lung cancer with incomplete fissure.Methods: This single-center retrospective cohort included 140 consecutive patients who underwent thoracoscopic right upper lobectomy, including 60 treated with SSDPVH and 80 treated with conventional video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (cVATS). Patients with incomplete or absent horizontal fissure were identified on preoperative high-resolution computed tomography (CT), with final intraoperative confirmation of anatomical suitability. Propensity score matching generated 50 well-balanced pairs. The primary endpoints were operative time, stapler cartridge use, postoperative air leak, and hospitalization cost, reported in Chinese yuan (CNY). Secondary endpoints included blood loss, postoperative stay, nodal yield, perioperative complications, and 18-month follow-up.Results: After matching, SSDPVH was associated with shorter operative time [60±5 vs. 74±18 min; mean difference −13 min, 95% confidence interval (CI): −19 to −8; P<0.001] and fewer stapler cartridges (3.8±0.6 vs. 5.6±1.1; mean difference −1.8, 95% CI: −2.1 to −1.5; P<0.001). Total hospitalization cost was lower in the SSDPVH group (32,487±850 vs. 36,145±945 CNY; mean difference −3,658 CNY, 95% CI: −4,022 to −3,294; P<0.001). Prolonged air leak occurred in 2 patients (4.0%) after SSDPVH and 6 patients (12.0%) after cVATS (risk ratio 0.33, 95% CI: 0.07–1.58; P=0.27). Blood loss, postoperative stay, and lymph node harvest were similar between groups. No postoperative bleeding, conversion to open thoracotomy, recurrence, or death was observed in either matched cohort during 18 months of follow-up.Conclusions: In this matched retrospective cohort, SSDPVH was associated with shorter operations, fewer stapler reloads, and lower hospitalization cost during thoracoscopic right upper lobectomy for lung cancer with incomplete fissure. The study was not powered to determine differences in postoperative complications or long-term oncologic outcomes.

items.title: Global burden of respiratory infections and tuberculosis and risk factors, 1990–2021: a systematic analysis of the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021
items.abstract: Background: Respiratory infections and tuberculosis (RIT) remain major contributors to global morbidity and mortality, with pronounced geographic and socioeconomic disparities. The emergence of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) has further disrupted existing control efforts, highlighting the need to reassess temporal trends, socioeconomic disparities, and risk-factor changes. This study aimed to quantify temporal trends, characterize geographic and socioeconomic disparities, and assess changes in risk-factor-attributable burden of RIT from 1990 to 2021. Methods: Using Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 data, we quantified incidence, prevalence, deaths, and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) of RIT across 204 countries from 1990 to 2021. Temporal trends were assessed using average annual percentage change (AAPC) and joinpoint regression. Associations with the Socio-demographic Index (SDI) were examined using Pearson correlation and generalized additive models (GAMs). Risk factor-attributable burdens were estimated using comparative risk assessment (CRA) methodology. Results: In 2021, RIT caused 11.25 million deaths and 349.68 million DALYs worldwide, accounting for 16.59% of total deaths and 12.15% of total DALYs. COVID-19 became the leading cause of RIT mortality (7.89 million deaths), followed by lower RIT. We identified four distinct regional burden trajectories, which reflected differences in health-system capacity and pandemic impact. SDI showed strong negative associations with age-standardized DALYs, deaths, and prevalence, but showed no significant association with incidence. From 1990 to 2021, environmental and behavioral risk factor burdens declined substantially, whereas metabolic risks rose, particularly in high-SDI regions. Conclusions: Despite declining age-standardized rates (ASRs), the absolute global burden of RIT continues to rise due to demographic transitions and the COVID-19 pandemic. Persistent socioeconomic disparities call for integrated strategies that combine vaccination, tuberculosis control, risk-factor reduction, and health-system strengthening to improve respiratory health equity.

items.title: Lymph node metastasis patterns and survival in patients with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma undergoing McKeown esophagectomy: a retrospective cohort study
items.abstract: Background: The distribution of lymph node metastases in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) varies with tumor location. We examined nodal metastasis patterns and factors associated with overall survival in patients undergoing McKeown esophagectomy.Methods: This single-center retrospective study analyzed hospital records of 909 patients with ESCC who underwent McKeown esophagectomy between December 2011 and July 2019, including total minimally invasive and hybrid procedures. Nodal involvement was summarized using node-based metastatic percentages and patient-level positivity among patients with evaluable regional records. Survival was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier methods and separate univariable Cox models for nodal status and recorded tumor length. Exploratory ABO analyses used Firth logistic regression for nodal positivity and a multivariable Cox model stratified by tumor location for overall survival. Analysis-specific exclusions were applied to missing or unresolved data.Results: The cohort included 535 men (58.9%), and the mean age was 64.2±7.2 years among 904 patients with recorded age. Tumors were located in the upper, middle, and lower thoracic esophagus in 200, 603, and 106 patients, respectively; 407 patients had pT3 disease. Nodal positivity was identified in 326 of 878 patients with evaluable nodal status (37.1%). Regional nodal involvement varied by tumor location. Reliable survival data were available for 895 patients, with 347 deaths and a median follow-up of 51 months. The nodal-status analysis included 864 patients and 320 deaths within 60 months; nodal positivity was associated with poorer survival [unadjusted hazard ratio (HR), 3.054; 95% confidence interval (CI): 2.446–3.821]. Recorded tumor length >3.79 cm was also associated with poorer survival (unadjusted HR, 2.693; 95% CI: 2.162–3.372). Both P values were <0.001. In exploratory adjusted analyses, the overall ABO association was significant for survival (P=0.01), but not for nodal positivity (P=0.21).Conclusions: Nodal involvement varied by tumor location. Nodal positivity and greater recorded tumor length were associated with poorer survival in univariable analyses. These findings do not establish the benefit of changing the extent of lymphadenectomy.

items.title: Ethical considerations in the management of complications after lung resection: a narrative review
items.abstract: Background and Objective: Complications following lung resection present complex clinical, ethical and interpersonal challenges that extend beyond technical management. Although substantial literature addresses the prevention and treatment of complications after lung resection, there is limited guidance regarding the ethical principles that should shape clinical decision-making as complications evolve. This review proposes a practical ethical framework for the management of complications following lung resection.Methods: Recommendations were developed based on clinical expertise and relevant published sources. A narrative literature search was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE and Embase, supplemented by targeted searches of relevant clinical resources and reference lists. English-language literature published within the last fifteen years was considered, with more recent evidence prioritized alongside foundational literature. Where lung resection-specific evidence was limited, related thoracic surgery, critical care, perioperative medicine, and surgical ethics literature was incorporated.Key Content and Findings: The developed framework is focused on six foundational ethical principles spanning patient-centered and provider-/systems-centered domains. Patient-centered principles include autonomy, shared decision-making and proportionate goal-concordant care, which help define patient values and integrate those values with clinical expertise to align treatment strategies with meaningful outcomes. Provider-/systems-centered principles include beneficence, nonmaleficence, justice, transparency and accountability, all of which guide professional responsibility, equitable care, honest communication and collaboration throughout recovery. The application of these principles is examined across the preoperative, intraoperative and postoperative phases of care.Conclusions: This framework emphasizes aligning treatment decisions with patient-defined goals, while balancing the potential benefits and burdens of intervention. Overall, these six ethical principles provide a structured and durable framework for navigating complications following lung resection.

items.title: Correlation between chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and comorbidities—a systematic analysis integrating global burden of disease and mendelian randomization study
items.abstract: Background: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) frequently coexists with multiple comorbidities. However, the long-term trends, regional disparities, and potential causal relationships in the global burden of these comorbidities remain to be systematically elucidated. This study aimed to characterize the disease burden of common comorbidities in patients with COPD and to assess the potential causal relationships between these comorbidities and COPD.Methods: This study integrated data from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 (GBD 2023) and conducted two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses. Based on GBD data from 1990 to 2023, we performed descriptive burden assessment, Das Gupta decomposition, Bayesian age-period-cohort modelling, exploratory correlation analysis, and formal age-interaction regression. Using summary statistics from the FinnGen consortium, we evaluated bidirectional genetic associations between COPD and various comorbidities primarily via the inverse variance weighted (IVW) method with false discovery rate (FDR) correction for multiple comparisons. The comorbidities of focus included asthma, anxiety disorders, major depressive disorder, pulmonary hypertension, hypertensive heart disease, ischemic heart disease, musculoskeletal disorders, osteoporosis, and respiratory tract cancers.Results: The absolute burden of comorbidities in COPD continued to increase, albeit driven by distinct factors. Population aging and growth were identified as the primary drivers for the rising burden of several COPD comorbidities, such as ischemic heart disease and musculoskeletal disorders. Significant regional inequalities were observed in disease distribution: high Socio-demographic Index (SDI) regions bore a heavier burden of musculoskeletal and mental disorders, whereas middle and low SDI regions exhibited more pronounced mortality and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) attributable to ischemic heart disease. Formal interaction models demonstrated significant age heterogeneity in the ecological associations between COPD prevalence and all eight comorbidities after Benjamini-Hochberg correction (all q ≤0.028). MR analyses provided evidence supporting bidirectional genetic associations between COPD and specific comorbidities. Genetically predicted COPD was significantly associated with an increased risk of asthma and depression (FDR <0.05), and conversely, genetic susceptibility to asthma and depression was associated with a higher risk of developing COPD (FDR <0.05).Conclusions: The comorbidity patterns between COPD and its key concomitant conditions are influenced by multiple factors, including demographic structure, regional development levels, and shared biological mechanisms. Our findings underscore the necessity of shifting from a single-disease management model towards integrated care strategies that emphasize comorbidity screening and holistic patient management.

items.title: Speckle perfusion dynamics as an objective marker of sympathetic interruption and its association with compensatory sweating after thoracic sympathectomy
items.abstract: Background: This study aimed to evaluate perioperative speckle perfusion dynamics as an objective marker of sympathetic interruption and to assess its association with compensatory sweating after thoracic sympathectomy. Methods: A retrospective cohort of 117 patients undergoing thoracic sympathectomy with perioperative speckle perfusion assessment was analyzed. Perfusion was measured at preoperative, pre-trigger, and postoperative time points. Percent changes from baseline were calculated. Associations with compensatory sweating and cold sensation were evaluated using logistic regression. Results: Perfusion increased from 120.9±30.7 preoperatively to 128.1±29.8 at the pre-trigger state and decreased to 102.7±23.3 postoperatively (all P<0.001). Percent pre-trigger change was associated with compensatory sweating (odds ratio 1.03, 95% confidence interval: 1.00–1.05; P=0.02). Heart rate correlated with pre-trigger response (r=0.21, P=0.02) but was not independently predictive. Cold sensation was related to body mass index. Conclusions: Speckle perfusion demonstrates measurable perioperative changes in cutaneous microvascular perfusion associated with thoracic sympathetic interruption, supporting its potential as an objective physiologic marker of the vascular response to sympathectomy. Greater pre-trigger perfusion response was associated with clinically significant compensatory sweating in univariable analysis, although this association was attenuated after multivariable adjustment and remains exploratory. These findings suggest that preoperative vascular reactivity may reflect an autonomic phenotype relevant to compensatory sweating and warrant prospective physiologic validation.

items.title: Clinical and prognostic analysis of unicentric mediastinal Castleman’s disease: a 10-year retrospective series study
items.abstract: Background: Castleman disease (CD) is a rare lymphoproliferative disorder, and unicentric mediastinal CD (UMCD) represents an uncommon thoracic manifestation for which surgical resection remains the mainstay of treatment.This study aims to: (I) characterize the anatomical distribution of UMCD in a single-center cohort; (II) evaluate the efficacy of video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) for UMCD resection and identify preoperative predictors of thoracotomy; (III) analyze prognostic outcomes in surgically managed UMCD patients. Methods: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 49 consecutive UMCD patients (26 males, 23 females; mean age 37.27±15.27 years) undergoing surgical resection at the department of thoracic surgery (Tangdu Hospital, Fourth Military Medical University) between May 2014 and October 2024. Demographic characteristics, anatomical distributions, and perioperative outcomes were systematically analyzed. Comparative analysis between VATS and thoracotomy groups was performed using independent samples t-tests. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression identified predictors of thoracotomy, with diagnostic performance evaluated via receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Survival outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier methodology. Results: The most frequent anatomical involvement occurred in station 3A lymph nodes (12 cases, 24.5%), followed by station 10 (11 cases, 22.3%) and station 4 (8 cases, 16.3%). Mean tumor size was 6.25±3.09 cm (intraoperative measurement). Histopathological subtypes included hyaline vascular variant (43 cases, 87.7%), plasma cell variant (4 cases, 8.2%), and mixed-type (2 cases, 4.1%). Compared to thoracotomy, VATS demonstrated shorter operative duration (P<0.05), reduced intraoperative blood loss (P<0.05), and shorter postoperative chest tube retention (3±2.81 vs. 5.52±3.54 days, P<0.05). Multivariate analysis identified tumor diameter >6.6 cm (P<0.05) and arterial-phase contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) attenuation >102 Hounsfield units (HU) (P<0.05) as independent predictors of thoracotomy. ROC analysis revealed an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.875 for the combined diagnostic model. With a median follow-up duration of 52 months, the VATS group maintained 100% recurrence-free survival. In the thoracotomy group, three patients succumbed to disease (two from local recurrence refractory to conservative therapy, one from postoperative pneumonia with respiratory failure following pneumonectomy). The overall survival (OS) rate for the cohort was 91.83%. Conclusions: Station 3A lymph nodes represent the predominant anatomical site of UMCD involvement. VATS resection confers significant advantages over thoracotomy, including reduced operative time, blood loss, and postoperative recovery duration. The diameter >6.6 cm and arterial-phase CT attenuation >102 HU of tumors serve as reliable preoperative indicators for thoracotomy. Early surgical intervention correlates with favorable prognosis, while postoperative complications and local recurrence demonstrate significant association with mortality.

items.title: Development and internal validation of a nomogram for predicting high-risk postoperative status after thoracoscopic pulmonary wedge resection: a single-center retrospective cohort study
items.abstract: Background: Routine placement of a chest tube after thoracoscopic pulmonary wedge resection may cause postoperative pain and delay recovery, yet safe implementation requires accurate identification of patients at low risk for significant drainage, air leak, and pneumothorax. This study aimed to identify independent risk factors for failure to meet early chest tube removal criteria after video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) pulmonary wedge resection, and to establish a validated nomogram for individualized risk stratification to inform postoperative chest tube management decisions.Methods: This retrospective single-center study included 680 patients who underwent VATS wedge resection between January 2023 and December 2025. Low-risk status was defined as chest tube drainage ≤200 mL within 24 hours, absence of air leak on coughing, and no significant pneumothorax on chest radiography. The cohort was randomly divided into a training set (70%) and an internal validation set (30%). Univariate and multivariate logistic regression were used to identify independent predictors of high-risk status. A nomogram was developed and internally validated using bootstrap resampling (500 replicates). Model performance was assessed by discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, AUC), calibration, and decision curve analysis (DCA).Results: Six independent predictors were identified: age [odds ratio (OR) =1.042, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.019–1.066, P<0.001], lower forced expiratory volume in 1 second percentage (FEV1%) predicted (OR =0.907, 95% CI: 0.883–0.928, P<0.001), neoadjuvant chemotherapy (OR =2.794, 95% CI: 1.244–6.340, P=0.013), operative duration (OR =1.033, 95% CI: 1.018–1.049, P<0.001), number of stapler cartridges used (OR =1.173, 95% CI: 1.106–1.258, P=0.041), and pleural adhesion degree (OR =3.649, 95% CI: 1.340–13.351, P=0.023). The nomogram showed good discrimination (training AUC =0.865; validation AUC =0.835) and excellent calibration (bootstrap-corrected calibration curve; Hosmer-Lemeshow P=0.62). DCA confirmed its clinical utility across threshold probabilities of 10–40%. No significant difference was observed between training and validation AUCs (ΔAUC =0.030, P=0.433).Conclusions: A six-variable nomogram incorporating age, FEV1% predicted, neoadjuvant chemotherapy, operative duration, number of stapler cartridges used, and pleural adhesion degree was developed to predict failure to meet early chest tube removal criteria after VATS wedge resection. This tool may assist in individualized risk stratification to inform clinical decision-making regarding chest tube management.

items.title: Clinical efficacy of minimally invasive cardiac valve surgery concomitant with radiofrequency ablation for atrial fibrillation: a single-center retrospective study
items.abstract: Background: Concomitant atrial fibrillation (AF) and valvular heart disease (VHD) present complex clinical challenges. Standard radiofrequency ablation (RFA) combined with valve surgery via median sternotomy offers robust rhythm correction but causes significant surgical trauma. Minimally invasive cardiac valve surgery with concomitant RFA (MICVS-RFA) is a promising strategy, but clinical data regarding its comprehensive safety, efficacy, and predictive risk factors for AF recurrence remain scarce. Thus, we aimed to evaluate the safety and clinical efficacy of MICVS-RFA and to develop an exploratory prognostic model for risk stratification. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 146 patients with concomitant VHD and AF who underwent MICVS-RFA between April 1, 2020, and August 1, 2025. Surgical cohorts included mitral valve replacement (MVR; n=34), mitral valve repair (MVr; n=19), MVR combined with tricuspid valve repair (MVR + TVr; n=57), and MVr combined with tricuspid valve repair (MVr + TVr; n=36). Pre-operative predictors for post-operative AF recurrence were identified using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) and elastic net regularization integrated within a multiple imputation framework to develop an exploratory model. Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) improvements were assessed dynamically. Results: Procedural success was achieved in all 146 patients, with an overall 30-day freedom from recurrent AF (FFAF) rate of 89.7% and no observed major adverse events (stroke, bleeding, or thromboembolism) within the first post-operative month. Length of stay (LOS) showed no statistical differences among surgical cohorts (P=0.71). Logistic regression modeling identified pre-operative metoprolol usage as associated with lower odds of AF recurrence [odds ratio (OR) =0.17; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.04–0.62], while pre-operative pulmonary hypertension (PH) showed a non-significant association with higher odds of AF recurrence (OR =3.07; 95% CI: 0.67–14.10). The predictive model showed moderate discrimination [bootstrap-corrected area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) =0.773] and apparent calibration. Patients with baseline LVEF <55% experienced superior functional recovery compared to those with LVEF ≥55% (ΔLVEF: 13.07%±2.56% vs. 0.18%±0.80%, P<0.001). Conclusions: MICVS-RFA was a feasible “dual minimally invasive” strategy that permits concomitant treatment of valvular pathology and AF through a minimally invasive approach, minimizing perioperative trauma. Comparative and long-term effects require further study.

items.title: An explainable machine learning model combining intratumoral and peritumoral computed tomography radiomics with maximum standard uptake value for predicting International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer grading and prognosis in stage I pure-solid lung adenocarcinoma
items.abstract: Background: The novel International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer (IASLC) grading system provides important prognostic information for lung adenocarcinoma; however, preoperative noninvasive prediction of this grading remains challenging. This study aimed to evaluate the predictive value of a combined intratumoral and peritumoral radiomics model based on computed tomography (CT) and maximum standard uptake value (SUV max ) for preoperative prediction of the novel IASLC grading and prognosis in stage I pure-solid invasive lung adenocarcinoma (LADC). Methods: Patients with stage I pure-solid LADC from The First Affiliated Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University were retrospectively included and randomly assigned to a training set (n=207) and a testing set (n=89) in a 7:3 ratio. There were 851 radiomics features extracted from the gross tumor volume (GTV) and the GTV incorporating peritumoral 3, 6, and 9 mm regions (GPTV3, GPTV6, GPTV9). A combined model based on an individual radiomics signature, SUV max , and clinical independent predictors was constructed. Recurrence-free survival (RFS) was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier survival method, while independent prognostic factors were identified through Cox proportional hazards models. Results: The GPTV3 model demonstrated a higher area under the curve (AUC) compared to other individual radiomics models, with AUCs of 0.804 and 0.715 in the training and testing sets. Tumor size was identified as an independent predictor of high-grade IASLC grading in the clinical model. The combined model showed AUCs of 0.837 and 0.767 for the training and testing sets, respectively, which were higher than those of the individual GPTV3 and SUV max models. The high-risk group was associated with poorer RFS (P<0.05). Pathological and predictive IASLC grade, smoking history, and tumor size were independent prognostic factors. Conclusions: The interpretable machine learning model can predict the novel IASLC grading and prognosis in stage I pure-solid LADC.

items.title: Multidimensional patient-reported recovery and early pain trajectories within 90 days after the Nuss procedure: a retrospective cohort study
items.abstract: Background: Postoperative assessment after the Nuss procedure often emphasizes pain intensity, although recovery also includes functional and procedure-specific symptoms. We characterized multidimensional patient-reported recovery during the first 90 postoperative days. Methods: This retrospective single-center cohort included 93 patients with at least three valid assessments on a 10-item Nuss-specific symptom and function scale. Records were summarized in five postoperative windows. Longitudinal domain patterns, pain-function discordance, and exploratory early pain trajectories were described. Internal consistency of the scale and the perioperative anesthesia and analgesia context were additionally evaluated. Results: The cohort contributed 1,729 records. Pain declined from a median of 5.50 [interquartile range (IQR), 4.25–6.50] during days 1–7 to 2.33 (IQR, 1.00–4.00) during days 15–30, whereas functional limitation was 4.82 (IQR, 3.86–5.94) and 3.00 (IQR, 1.71–4.70), respectively. During days 15–30, 11/88 patients (12.5%) had relatively low pain but persistent functional limitation under exploratory, distribution-informed thresholds. An exploratory two-class model yielded an improving class (79/89) and a persistent-high-pain class (10/89). Among 79 patients with trajectory and later outcome data, residual pain during days 31–90 occurred in 6/9 patients in the persistent-high-pain class and 11/70 in the improving class. Internal-consistency coefficients across windows ranged from 0.900 to 0.950 for the symptom domain and from 0.737 to 0.909 for the function domain. Conclusions: Recovery during the first 90 days after the Nuss procedure was multidimensional, with functional limitation and bar awareness improving more slowly than pain. Exploratory trajectory findings also indicated heterogeneity in early recovery. Multidomain follow-up may provide a more complete view of recovery, and prospective studies with standardized analgesia, neuropathic-pain measures, and longer follow-up are warranted.

items.title: From risk factors to individualized prediction: development and internal validation of a machine learning model for early identification of postoperative pneumonia after lung cancer surgery
items.abstract: Background: Postoperative pneumonia (POP) remains one of the most common infectious complications following lung cancer surgery and is associated with substantial morbidity. Although several risk factors for POP have been identified, clinically applicable approaches for early individualized risk stratification remain limited. This study aimed to develop and internally validate machine learning models for early prediction of POP using routinely available perioperative variables.Methods: In this prospective single-center cohort study, 258 consecutive patients undergoing pulmonary resection for non-small cell lung cancer or pulmonary carcinoid tumors were screened, of whom 200 were included in the final study cohort. POP was defined by newly developed postoperative radiographic abnormalities accompanied by clinical signs of infection requiring antibiotic therapy. Machine learning models, including logistic regression (LR), Naïve Bayes (NB), random forest (RF), and XGBoost (XGB), were developed to predict POP using demographic, clinical, laboratory, surgical, and postoperative day 1 radiographic variables. Model performance was assessed using nested leave-one-out cross-validation and quantified by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). A nomogram was constructed from the best-performing model to facilitate individualized risk estimation. Different decision thresholds were explored to evaluate clinically relevant trade-offs between sensitivity and specificity.Results: POP occurred in 47 of 200 patients (23.5%), while no POP-related mortality was observed. LR demonstrated the best predictive performance (AUROC 0.701±0.070), followed by NB (0.698±0.103), RF (0.656±0.217), and XGB (0.589±0.179). The most influential predictors included advanced age, perioperative changes in C-reactive protein concentration (ΔCRP), elevated preoperative CRP levels, prolonged operative duration, and abnormal postoperative day 1 chest radiographic findings. At a decision threshold of 25%, the model correctly identified 25 of 47 POP cases (53.2%), whereas increasing the threshold to 32.5% reduced false-positive classifications from 42 to 24 at the expense of missing an additional four POP cases.Conclusions: Machine learning models based on routinely available perioperative variables enabled early individualized prediction of POP following lung cancer surgery. LR provided the best balance between predictive performance, stability, and interpretability, allowing the development of an interpretable nomogram for individualized risk estimation. The model may have potential to support risk-adapted postoperative surveillance and more efficient allocation of healthcare resources; however, external validation is required before clinical implementation.

items.title: Interdisciplinary thoraco-plastic surgery for chest wall reconstruction: a single-center quality control project and clinical practice review
items.abstract: Abstract: Thoracic defects arise from a broad spectrum of causes, including tumours, congenital deformities, infections, and radiation-induced damage. Their surgical management is often challenging and typically requires close interdisciplinary cooperation, particularly between thoracic and plastic surgeons. This retrospective project included all patients who underwent thoracic wall resection and subsequent reconstruction at the University Hospital Basel between January 2013 and January 2025. During this 12-year period, 89 patients with chest, lung, pleura, and breast pathologies underwent thoracic reconstruction. The proportion of patients with an oncological diagnosis was 17% (n=15). Overall, there were 63 men (71%) and 26 women (29%). The mean age was 64±13 years. Pectoralis major flaps were used in 34 patients; latissimus dorsi (LD) flaps were used in 25 patients, with additional pectoralis major flaps in 2 patients and a combination of pectoralis flap reconstruction with a vertical rectus abdominis myocutaneous (VRAM) flap in 3 patients. Isolated VRAM reconstruction was performed in 4 patients, and in one patient, transverse rectus abdominis myocutaneous (TRAM) flap reconstruction was performed. In 2 patients, the serratus anterior muscle was used, and in one patient each, a vastus lateralis flap and an obliquus externus flap were applied for defect coverage. In 16 patients, the defect was covered plastically by local skin rotation. Chest wall reconstruction following extensive thoracic resection is safe and effective when guided by a structured, stepwise approach and close interdisciplinary collaboration.

items.title: Lactate dehydrogenase to albumin ratio as a potential indicator of pathological response and prognosis in non-small cell lung cancer patients undergoing neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy followed by surgery
items.abstract: Background: In recent years, neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy followed by radical resection has become a new treatment option for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, there remains a paucity of simple yet effective biomarkers for assessing pathological response and long-term prognosis. This study aimed to investigate the potential value of serum lactate dehydrogenase to albumin ratio (LAR) in this clinical setting. Methods: The clinicopathological data of 81 consecutive patients with NSCLC who received neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy and radical surgery at Xuanwu Hospital, Capital Medical University between January 2019 and December 2024 were retrospectively analyzed. Baseline LAR, post-treatment LAR, and the ratio of baseline to post-treatment LAR were calculated and evaluated for their associations with pathologic response and event-free survival (EFS). Results: Of the 81 patients, 48 (59.3%) achieved major pathological response (MPR). MPR patients had significantly lower post-treatment LAR and a higher baseline to post-treatment LAR ratio than non-MPR patients, whereas baseline LAR showed no significant difference. Post-treatment LAR and baseline to post-treatment LAR ratio discriminatedMPR with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.747 and 0.719, respectively. Multivariate logistic regression identified post-treatment LAR [odds ratio (OR) =0.498, P=0.02] and radiological response (OR =6.297, P=0.008) as independent factors associated with MPR. Multivariate Cox regression demonstrated that higher post-treatment LAR [hazard ratio (HR) =1.664, P=0.003] and non-MPR status (HR =3.498, P=0.004) were independent prognostic factors for poor EFS. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis further revealed a positive association between post-treatment LAR and EFS risk, with higher LAR corresponding to increased HRs. A nomogram based on these two EFS prognostic factors demonstrated good calibration at 24 months with internal bootstrap validation (C-index =0.769). Conclusions: Post-treatment LAR could serve as a potential indicator for response assessment and long-term prognostication in NSCLC patients undergoing neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy. Its simplicity, cost-effectiveness, and accessibility through routine laboratory testing render it a promising candidate for integration into clinical practice.

items.title: Risk factors and clinical implications of sternal dehiscence following clamshell incision in bilateral lung transplantation
items.abstract: Background: Clamshell incisions provide excellent exposure for bilateral lung transplantation (BLT) but carry an inherent risk of sternal dehiscence. This study aimed to identify the risk factors for sternal dehiscence and evaluate its impact on pulmonary function.Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 129 adult patients who underwent BLT via clamshell incision between 2007 and 2024. Sternal dehiscence was defined as radiographic nonunion of the sternum confirmed by chest computed tomography scan at least 3 months postoperatively, or any sternal dehiscence requiring surgical correction regardless of the time interval. Risk factors were identified using Firth’s penalized likelihood logistic regression analysis. Pulmonary function tests were compared between patients with and without dehiscence at 1 year postoperatively and the last follow-up.Results: Sternal dehiscence occurred in 15 patients (11.6%), of which 11 (8.5%) were classified as major cases. Multivariable analysis identified male sex as an independent risk factor associated with dehiscence [odds ratio (OR) 8.89, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.27–108.74, P=0.02], whereas perioperative tracheostomy was independently associated with a lower incidence (OR =0.12, 95% CI: 0.02–0.53, P=0.004). Surgical closure techniques, including wiring and parasternal fixation, were not significantly associated with dehiscence (P=0.73 and P>0.99, respectively). No significant differences in pulmonary function were observed between groups at 1 year postoperatively and last follow-up.Conclusions: Male sex was independently associated with sternal dehiscence following BLT, whereas perioperative tracheostomy was associated with a lower incidence; these findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating given the observational design. Pulmonary function during the follow-up period was not significantly associated with sternal dehiscence in this cohort. Surgeons may consider reinforced closure in male patients, while the protective role of tracheostomy warrants further study.

items.title: Neutrophil to lymphocyte ratio (NLR) predicts pathological response to neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy in resectable esophageal cancer: a retrospective study
items.abstract: Background: Neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy (nICT) has demonstrated promising efficacy in locally advanced esophageal cancer. The pretreatment neutrophil to lymphocyte ratio (NLR) has shown prognostic value across various solid tumors. This study aimed to evaluate the predictive value of pretreatment NLR for pathological response in patients with resectable esophageal cancer receiving nICT. Methods: A total of 295 patients with resectable esophageal cancer who underwent nICT followed by surgery were retrospectively analyzed. Pretreatment NLR was calculated from peripheral blood counts. Pathological response was assessed using the Becker tumor regression grading (TRG) system. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was conducted to evaluate the predictive performance of NLR. Multivariable logistic regression and bootstrap internal validation were performed to assess its independent predictive value. Results: Pretreatment NLR was significantly higher in non-pathological complete response (non-pCR) patients than in pathological complete response (pCR) patients (P=0.04). A weak positive correlation was observed between NLR and TRG (r=0.130, P=0.03). The area under the ROC curve (AUROC) of NLR for predicting non-pCR was 0.586 [95% confidence intervals (CI): 0.510–0.663, P=0.04], with an optimal cutoff value of 3.59 (sensitivity 37.6%, specificity 79.3%, positive predictive value 89.0%, negative predictive value 24.1%). The combination of NLR with clinical stage improved the AUROC to 0.633 for predicting non-pCR. In the esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) subgroup (n=271), NLR demonstrated improved predictive performance for both non-pCR (AUROC =0.609, 95% CI: 0.530–0.687) and non-major pathological response (non-MPR) (AUROC =0.570, 95% CI: 0.512–0.642). Integration with clinical T and N categories further increased the AUROC to 0.654 for non-pCR and 0.626 for non-MPR. Multivariable logistic regression confirmed that NLR was an independent predictor of non-pCR [odds ratios (OR) =1.325, 95% CI: 1.005–1.747, P=0.046], and bootstrap validation supported its robustness. Conclusions: Elevated pretreatment NLR is associated with poorer pathological response to nICT in patients with resectable esophageal cancer, particularly in ESCC. When combined with clinical staging, NLR may serve as an accessible adjunctive tool to identify patients with a low probability of pCR.

items.title: Noninvasive ventilation for non-expandable lung after pleural surgery: a single-center retrospective study
items.abstract: Background: Non-expandable lung (NEL) is a well-recognized complication of pleural surgery, characterized by failure of the lung to fully re-expand and appose to the parietal pleura, resulting in a persistent pleural space and substantial morbidity. Management of NEL remains challenging, and although the physiological rationale suggests that positive airway pressure could enhance alveolar recruitment and facilitate pleural apposition, the role of noninvasive ventilation (NIV) in treating this condition remains poorly studied. This study aimed to evaluate the potential benefit of NIV on radiological outcomes, as well as its feasibility and safety, for NEL following pleural surgery.Methods: This retrospective, single-center observational study included patients who received NIV for NEL following pleural surgery between May 2022 and February 2026. The primary outcome was lung re-expansion after NIV, assessed by chest radiography on day 1 (D1) and day 3 (D3), and at 4 weeks (W4) after discharge. Secondary outcomes included duration of chest tube drainage, length of hospital stay, pulmonary complications, NIV-related adverse events, recurrence of pleural effusion, 30-day mortality, home NIV prescription, and treatment adherence.Results: A total of 52 patients, with a median age of 73 years, were included in the final analysis. The etiology of pleural effusion was malignant in 71.2% of cases, and video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) was the predominant surgical approach. Complete re-expansion increased progressively, from 42.3% (22/52) at D1 to 73.1% (38/52) at D3 and 86.6% (45/52) at W4 after discharge, while the failure rate decreased correspondingly from 13.5% (7/52) to 3.8% (2/52) over the same follow-up period. Partial re-expansion also followed an inverse trend (44.2% at D1, 19.2% at D3, 9.6% at W4). The median durations of chest tube drainage and hospital stay were each 4 days. Pulmonary complications occurred in 2 patients (3.8%), recurrence of pleural effusion in 3 patients (5.8%), and no 30-day mortality was observed. NIV was well tolerated, with only minor adverse events; treatment adherence reached 94.2%, and 32.7% of patients were discharged with home NIV.Conclusions: In this preliminary, single-center, uncontrolled experience, NIV was feasible and associated with progressive radiological lung re-expansion in patients with established NEL following pleural surgery, with infrequent adverse events. These findings provide a preliminary proof of concept supporting NIV as a potential adjunct to standard postoperative care in this indication. Prospective, multicenter, randomized controlled trials, stratified by the mechanism of NEL, are needed to confirm this potential benefit and identify the patients most likely to benefit.

items.title: Real-world implementation of video-assisted thoracic surgery for lung cancer: a decade-long regional propensity score-weighted cohort study
items.abstract: Background: The perioperative advantages of video-assisted thoracic surgery (VATS) over thoracotomy are established, but the real-world introduction of a minimally invasive program is shaped by patient selection, technical maturation, conversion and secular change in care. We evaluated the decade-long implementation of VATS within a regional thoracic surgery service and estimated its association with early postoperative outcomes.Methods: This is a retrospective cohort study of anatomical lung resections performed over the first decade [2009–2018] of a VATS implementation program at two tertiary hospitals covered by a single thoracic surgery department. The primary exposure was the approach with which the operation was started under an intention-to-treat analysis strategy, and the outcomes were 90-day mortality, a composite of major morbidity and perioperative mortality, and 30-day readmission. Propensity score weighting used preoperative covariates, including calendar year and hospital. Covariate balance before and after weighting was assessed by absolute standardized mean differences. The average treatment effect (ATE), reported as risk difference with 95% confidence interval (CI), was the primary estimand, with average treatment on the treated (ATT) and average treatment effect on the overlap population (ATO) as sensitivity estimands. An exploratory analysis comparing conversion with upfront thoracotomy was carried out under the same prespecification.Results: A total of 964 out of 1,404 anatomical lung resections met the inclusion criteria. The series included 472 operations begun thoracoscopically, of which 97 were converted (20%), versus 492 upfront thoracotomies. Completed VATS rose from 16.7% of anatomical resections in 2009 to 53.7% in 2018, while conversion annual rates fell from 50.0% to 6.5%. Converted procedures had the highest crude rate of every adverse outcome. Under intention to treat, an intended VATS approach was not significantly associated with 90-day mortality (ATE −1.9 percentage points; 95% CI: −4.7 to +0.9; P=0.17), major morbidity and mortality (ATE −4.6 points; 95% CI: −9.4 to +0.2; P=0.06) or readmission (ATE −2.0 points; 95% CI: −5.9 to +2.0; P=0.33); for the composite outcome, the ATT (P=0.04) and ATO (P=0.047) estimands reached significance. In the as-treated analysis, all three outcomes were significant in favor of completed VATS. No statistically significant differences were detected between conversions and upfront thoracotomies in the exploratory analysis.Conclusions: Across a decade-long regional implementation trajectory, adoption of VATS rose and conversion fell. When conversions are analyzed in the arm in which the operation was begun, the association between an intended thoracoscopic approach and better perioperative outcomes is attenuated and no longer significant. These findings do not question the perioperative advantages of thoracoscopic lobectomy, but the benefit attributable to adopting a thoracoscopic strategy at service level is smaller and less certain than that observed among the operations it completes.

items.title: Long-term survival patterns and prognostic stratification in patients with unresectable locally advanced squamous cell lung cancer receiving definitive chemoradiotherapy: a 14-year single-center real-world cohort
items.abstract: Background: Real-world data with more than 10 years of follow-up among Chinese patients with unresectable locally advanced squamous cell lung cancer (SqCLC) treated with definitive chemoradiotherapy are scarce. This single-center cohort with complete 14-year longitudinal surveillance was constructed to map long-term survival kinetics, screen independent prognostic markers, and depict full disease trajectories, so as to facilitate stratified surveillance and personalized therapeutic management. Methods: This retrospective single-center real-world cohort enrolled 260 stage IIIA–IIIC unresectable SqCLC patients receiving definitive chemoradiotherapy between 2012–2019. Kaplan-Meier curves were used to estimate overall survival (OS), first progression-free survival (PFS1), and post-salvage second progression-free survival (PFS2); the log-rank test was applied for inter-group comparison. Multivariable Cox proportional-hazards regression (enter method) was utilized to screen independent prognostic factors, and a clinically-oriented 12-month PFS1 cutoff was used for risk stratification. Results: With maximum follow-up exceeding 14 years (data cut-off June 1, 2026), the 10-year OS rate was 35.0%. The survival curve exhibited a distinct three-phase trajectory: a high-risk phase during the first 3 years accounting for approximately half of all events, a decelerating decline from year 3 to 10, and a stable plateau beyond 10 years, with OS rates at 10 and 14 years both approximating 35%. Multivariable analysis identified age <65 years, peripherally located tumors, absence of radiation pneumonitis, objective response to first-line therapy, and PFS1 ≥12 months as independent protective factors for OS, among which PFS1 ≥12 months yielded the strongest effect [hazard ratio (HR) =2.70, P<0.001]. First disease progression occurred in 86.0% of patients, of whom 32.0% presented with oligometastatic lesions (defined as ≤5 metastatic lesions confined to limited anatomic sites without widespread disseminated disease); those receiving active local salvage therapy achieved a 14-year PFS2 rate of 48.0%. An interval of ≤3 months from diagnosis to radiotherapy initiation was associated with a significantly higher objective response rate (ORR) compared with >3 months (73.0% vs. 57.0%, P<0.05). Conclusions: A 10-year survival rate of 35% is achievable in patients with locally advanced unresectable SqCLC after definitive chemoradiotherapy, with substantially reduced risks of recurrence and all-cause mortality beyond the 10-year landmark. A PFS1 ≥12 months serves as a simple and robust prognostic biomarker for long-term survival, and active local salvage of oligometastatic lesions enables durable disease control. Surveillance schedules and consolidation strategies may be tailored according to patients’ progression-free status at 12 months.

items.title: The ligament of Marshall as a therapeutic target in atrial fibrillation: from anatomy to catheter-based and surgical management—a narrative review
items.abstract: Background and Objective: Long regarded as an inconsequential embryological remnant, the ligament of Marshall (LOM) is now recognized as a treatable component of the atrial fibrillation (AF) substrate. This review synthesizes the anatomical, electrophysiological and clinical evidence behind that shift and compares the two routes to the LOM: percutaneous retrograde ethanol infusion into the vein of Marshall (EIVOM) during catheter ablation, and direct division during thoracoscopic surgery. Both act on the same epicardial structure; only the route of access differs. Methods: A structured literature search of PubMed, Embase and Web of Science covered the embryology, anatomy, histology and electrophysiology of the LOM and clinical studies of both routes. Two authors screened and selected records independently. Given the heterogeneity of study designs, findings were synthesized narratively. Key Content and Findings: The LOM is a neuro-muscular remnant of the embryonic left superior vena cava that contributes to AF through three mechanisms: triggers arising from insulated myocardial “Marshall bundles”, autonomic modulation via adjacent ganglionated plexi, and preferential conduction across the mitral isthmus. Five randomized trials of EIVOM-based strategies have enrolled more than 1,100 patients; pooled analysis shows improved 12-month freedom from any atrial arrhythmia (risk ratio 1.16, 95% confidence interval: 1.04–1.29; number needed to treat 10) and less repeat ablation, without excess major complications (2.5% vs. 2.8%) but with more overall complications and longer fluoroscopy. Crucially, no trial has tested ethanol infusion in isolation; the observed benefit reflects composite lesion sets. Thoracoscopic division interrupts the entire ligament independent of venous anatomy but has never been a randomized variable; randomized evidence for thoracoscopic and hybrid strategies overall ranges from neutral (CASA-AF) to positive (CONVERGE, HARTCAP-AF). Guidelines recognize both as options in selected patients without mandating routine LOM division. Conclusions: The LOM is a reproducible, anatomically defined target reachable percutaneously or by surgical division within a comprehensive AF ablation strategy. The supporting evidence is markedly asymmetric: randomized data exist for EIVOM-based strategies but never for ethanol infusion alone, none at all for surgical division, and the two routes have never been compared head-to-head. Its incremental benefit beyond pulmonary vein and posterior wall isolation remains undefined.

items.title: Lung transplantation outcomes in patients with coal workers’ pneumoconiosis compared with non-occupational interstitial lung disease: a single-center cohort study
items.abstract: Background: Coal workers’ pneumoconiosis (CWP) is a lung disease caused by long-term coal dust exposure. Appalachian miners experience disproportionately high disease prevalence and mortality. Lung transplantation offers outcomes comparable to other interstitial lung diseases (ILDs), yet limited data exist on patients with CWP. This study examines regional disease burden and lung transplant outcomes for CWP at our institution compared with non-occupational ILD.Methods: A retrospective cohort study evaluated lung transplant recipients with CWP, autoimmune-ILD (A-ILD), and nonautoimmune-ILD (NA-ILD) at our center from 2017 to 2025. Patients were categorized by ILD etiology, and demographic, clinical, and post-transplant outcome data were collected from institutional records under institutional review board-approved protocols. Continuous variables were analyzed using one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) or the Kruskal-Wallis test. Categorical variables were compared using Pearson’s Chi-squared test or Fisher’s exact test. Survival was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis.Results: Among 67 lung transplant recipients, 23 had CWP, 11 had A-ILD, and 33 had NA-ILD. CWP recipients were exclusively male and had a lower body mass index (BMI). Transplant recipients across all cohorts were predominantly male. Rates of acute kidney injury (AKI), renal replacement therapy (RRT), and hospital stay were similar across groups. Bronchial stenosis post-transplant was significantly more common with cardiac-death donors. Survival analyses suggested similar survival between the cohorts.Conclusions: This study observed no statistically significant differences in survival or postoperative complications in patients with CWP compared to those with non-occupational ILD. Female underrepresentation was found despite modern increases in women in coal-mining fields. Post-transplant complications of bronchial stenosis requiring dilatation ± stent were more likely in those who received organ donation after circulatory death (DCD). Limited impact of pre-transplant comorbidities was also noted. Despite small, single-center design, results suggest lung transplantation as a feasible treatment option in carefully selected patients with advanced CWP and highlight the need for larger multicenter studies.

items.title: SNORD42A serves as an oncogenic biomarker in non-small cell lung cancer
items.abstract: Background: Despite substantial advances in therapeutic strategies, non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains the leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide. The poor prognosis of NSCLC is largely due to the limited efficacy of existing clinical treatments and the lack of reliable and effective molecular therapeutic targets. Studies have shown that small nucleolar RNAs (snoRNAs) play pivotal regulatory roles in multiple pathological processes involved in tumor formation and malignant progression. However, the specific biological functions and underlying molecular mechanisms of individual snoRNAs in the occurrence and development of NSCLC remain largely unclear, highlighting the need for systematic exploration. Methods: A reanalysis of genome-scale clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR)-Cas9 knockout screening data covering all annotated snoRNAs in NSCLC cell lines was performed. Colony formation assays confirmed the functional role of SNORD42A in NSCLC cells. A combined bioinformatic analysis of our internal sequencing data and public datasets further identified the molecular locus of SNORD42A in the pathogenesis of NSCLC. Results: Genome-wide screening identified SNORD42A as a key candidate snoRNA regulating NSCLC cell proliferation. Both the in-house snoRNA sequencing data and bioinformatics analysis of The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) cohort demonstrated that SNORD42A was significantly overexpressed in clinical NSCLC tissues compared with paired adjacent normal lung tissues, indicating its potential oncogenic role in NSCLC. Functional validation experiments further demonstrated that SNORD42A knockdown markedly inhibited the clonogenic capacity of NSCLC cells. Moreover, an integrative bioinformatics analysis of TCGA data revealed that SNORD42A expression was closely correlated with cell cycle regulation and cellular senescence signaling pathways, and its expression level was significantly associated with the clinical prognosis of patients with NSCLC. Conclusions: SNORD42A functions as a pro-tumorigenic factor that promotes NSCLC progression, with its effects potentially linked to alterations in cellular protein synthesis. This study revealed the functional importance of SNORD42A in NSCLC malignancy, suggesting that SNORD42A may serve as a novel prognostic biomarker and a promising therapeutic target for the treatment of NSCLC.

items.title: Peri-transplant airway microbiota and lung transplant outcomes: beyond infectious complications to alloimmune modulation
Pirfenidone fails to improve outcomes in progressive bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome post-lung transplant
Evaluating robotic-assisted bronchoscopy for bronchus-unconnected peripheral pulmonary nodules: diagnostic efficacy and safety
items.abstract: Background: Bronchus-unconnected peripheral pulmonary lesions (PPLs) pose diagnostic challenges due to lack of direct airway access and computed tomography (CT)-to-body divergence (CTBD). We evaluated robotic-assisted bronchoscopy (RAB) combined with the intraprocedural CT-guided navigation with ventilatory strategy for atelectasis (ICNVA) strategy.Methods: This prospective, single-arm study enrolled patients (18–75 years) with pulmonary nodules (6–30 mm) lacking a bronchus sign. All underwent RAB with the ICNVA strategy, integrating preoperative mapping, intraprocedural breath-holds to minimize atelectasis, and real-time CT confirmation. The primary endpoint was tool-in-lesion (TIL) rate. Secondary endpoints included diagnostic yield, center strike rate, CTBD, and safety.Results: Thirty patients were enrolled (mean age 55.6±10.7 years). Lesions had a mean diameter of 14.0±4.3 mm and a median distance to the nearest bronchus of 18 mm. The ICNVA strategy resulted in a mean CTBD of 13.4 mm. We achieved a 100% (30/30) navigational success rate (TIL) and a 66.7% (20/30) center strike rate. The overall diagnostic yield was 90% (27/30), with 90.9% (20/22) sensitivity for malignancy. Pneumothorax occurred in 2 patients (6.7%) and mild hemorrhage in 7 (23.3%), with no severe adverse events occurred.Conclusions: RAB combined with the ICNVA strategy demonstrates high diagnostic yield and safety for bronchus-unconnected PPLs. This approach effectively mitigates CTBD, enabling precise localization and sampling of lesions traditionally considered difficult to access.

items.title: Flow-controlled ventilation in cardiac surgery: the question of lung protection
Final efficacy and safety data from the Phase I/II ARROW study of pralsetinib in patients with advanced REarranged during Transfection fusion-positive non-small cell lung cancer
Pirfenidone in bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome after lung transplantation: two negative trials, one clearer path forward
Effects of leritrelvir for adults with mild-to-moderate coronavirus disease 2019: A multicenter real-world study
items.abstract: Background: Real-world evidence for leritrelvir, a single-component 3C-like protease inhibitor, in adults with mild-to-moderate coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) remains limited. We evaluated the association of early leritrelvir use with symptom resolution, negative viral-test conversion, and adverse events in routine clinical practice.Methods: This prospective, multicenter, nonrandomized, open-label observational cohort study was conducted at 141 sites in China (mainland ). Among 1,527 adults with mild-to-moderate COVID-19, 1,388 received leritrelvir (400 mg three times daily for 5 days) plus standard care and 139 received standard care alone. The primary endpoint was time to sustained resolution of 11 predefined symptoms. The key secondary endpoint was time to negative severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) nucleic acid test (NAT) conversion. All participants contributed a primary time-to-event record. We estimated unadjusted and multivariable-adjusted Cox models and performed 1:1 propensity score (PS) matching (136 participants per group).Results: For sustained symptom resolution, the unadjusted hazard ratio (HR) was 1.41 [95% confidence interval (CI): 1.18–1.68; P<0.001], the multivariable-adjusted HR was 1.66 (95% CI: 1.38–1.99; P<0.001), and the PS-matched HR was 1.81 (robust 95% CI: 1.43–2.29; P<0.001). In the matched cohort, median time to symptom resolution was 6 days with leritrelvir and 8 days with standard care alone. For negative NAT conversion, the corresponding HRs were 1.20 (95% CI: 1.01–1.43; P=0.040), 1.22 (95% CI: 1.01–1.47; P=0.04), and 1.47 (robust 95% CI: 1.21–1.79; P<0.001); matched medians were 3 and 4 days. Adverse events occurred in 22.41% and 19.42% of the unmatched groups, respectively.Conclusions: In this prospective, multicenter, nonrandomized cohort, leritrelvir use was associated with earlier sustained symptom resolution and negative SARS-CoV-2 NAT conversion than standard care alone. Although the direction of association was consistent across multivariable-adjusted and PS-matched analyses, residual confounding, open-label symptom assessment, nonproportional hazards, incomplete follow-up, and the absence of severe-outcome events preclude causal, subgroup-specific, or severe-outcome conclusions.

items.title: Clinical outcomes with initial oral triple and dual therapy in echocardiography-defined connective tissue disease-associated pulmonary hypertension: a retrospective single-center cohort study
items.abstract: Background: Connective tissue disease-associated pulmonary hypertension (CTD-PH) is a serious complication, but evidence on early oral treatment intensification in patients followed primarily by echocardiography is limited. We evaluated outcomes associated with initial selexipag-containing oral triple therapy vs. dual therapy in echocardiography-defined CTD-PH. Methods: This single-center retrospective cohort included consecutive adults who initiated PH-targeted therapy between April 2020 and June 2025. Treatment was selected by treating physicians in routine care and was not randomized: dual therapy comprised macitentan plus tadalafil, whereas triple therapy additionally included selexipag. Baseline clinical, laboratory, and echocardiographic variables were obtained from standardized institutional assessments and reassessed at week 26. The primary endpoint was the change in the number (0–3) of European Society of Cardiology/European Respiratory Society (ESC/ERS) noninvasive low-risk criteria met: World Health Organization functional class (WHO-FC) I–II, 6-minute walk distance (6MWD) >440 m, and B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) <50 ng/L or N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) <300 ng/L. Complete cases with all three components available at both time points were analyzed without imputation. Disease-progression events were recorded through 30 weeks, and adverse events were assessed during follow-up. Results: Of 119 patients, 59 received triple therapy and 60 received dual therapy. The groups had similar baseline functional and biomarker profiles (6MWD, 290.0 vs. 286.9 m; NT-proBNP, 1,455 vs. 1,473 pg/mL); mean age was 45.5 vs. 47.2 years in the triple and dual therapy group respectively, and 93% vs. 83% were women. At week 26, the change in low-risk criteria differed between groups (P=0.003), with 57.6% vs. 33.3% meeting all the three criteria. Mean 6MWD increased by 156 vs. 104 m (adjusted difference, 52 m; 95% confidence interval (CI): 29–78; P<0.001), and WHO-FC distributions differed at week 26 (P=0.007). Exploratory analysis yielded an hazard ratio (HR) of 0.75 (95% CI: 0.39–1.43) for the first disease-progression event. At least one adverse event occurred in 53/59 (89.8%) vs. 47/60 (78.3%) patients; diarrhea occurred in 24/59 (40.7%) vs. 19/60 (31.7%), nausea in 21/59 (35.6%) vs. 16/60 (26.7%), and jaw pain in 16/59 (27.1%) vs. 11/60 (18.3%), with no significant between-group differences. Conclusions: In this real-world cohort of patients with echocardiography-defined CTD-PH, initial selexipag-containing oral triple therapy was associated with greater improvement in noninvasive ESC/ERS risk status and functional outcomes than dual therapy over 26 weeks, supporting further evaluation of noninvasive risk-guided oral treatment intensification in CTD-associated pulmonary vascular disease. However, given the small, single-center, nonrandomized retrospective design, these findings cannot establish superior efficacy or safety and require prospective multicenter confirmation with systematic hemodynamic assessment.

items.title: The effects of Mycobacterium tuberculosis genotypes on clinical phenotypes revealed by whole-genome sequencing technology in China
items.abstract: Background: Findings related to the associations between Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB) lineages and tuberculosis (TB) clinical phenotypes remain inconsistent across studies, primarily because conventional genotyping techniques lack the resolution to distinguish fine-scale sublineages. This study aimed to rigorously verify the clinical characteristics and prognostic significance of predominant Beijing-lineage strains circulating in China using high-resolution genomic evidence.Methods: In total, 173 patients with TB were enrolled in the study, and whole-genome sequencing (WGS) was performed on 213 clinical MTB isolates; mixed-strain infections were excluded from subsequent analyses. Phylogenetic sublineage classification was performed based on single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) profiling. Multivariate logistic regression was used to independently assess the associations between MTB genotypes, clinical manifestations, and treatment outcomes, after adjusting for demographic and clinical confounding factors.Results: Among the 172 valid isolates, 80.8% were classified as East Asian Beijing lineage (lineage 2), 18.0% as Euro-American lineage (lineage 4), and 1.2% as Indo-Oceanic lineage (lineage 1). Compared with the non-Beijing strains, the Beijing strains were independently associated with an increased risk of pulmonary cavitation [adjusted odds ratio (aOR) =4.76, 95% confidence interval (CI): 2.01–11.26, P=0.006], as well as a decreased risk of disseminated TB (aOR =0.40, 95% CI: 0.17–0.95, P=0.04). No significant association was observed between the Beijing genotype and treatment failure, whereas cavitary disease was an independent predictor of treatment failure.Conclusions: MTB genetic diversity contributes substantially to heterogeneity in TB clinical phenotypes. WGS enables precise sublineage identification and facilitates robust genotype-phenotype analysis. These findings support the implementation of genomic surveillance to optimize individualized clinical management and inform targeted TB prevention strategies in endemic regions.

items.title: Artificial intelligence in esophageal cancer radiotherapy: a literature review
items.abstract: Background and Objective: Radiotherapy is a key component in the management of esophageal cancer (EC). Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative tool for optimizing radiotherapy workflows. Numerous AI-based tools are being developed to improve efficiency and facilitate the personalization of radiation oncology. This study aimed to provide an up-to-date review of the literature on recent advances in AI applications across the EC radiotherapy workflow.Methods: The PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science databases were searched to retrieve original English-language articles published from January 1, 2020 to May 26, 2026. The following search terms were used: “Esophageal neoplasms”, “esophageal cancer”, “oesophageal cancer” AND “artificial intelligence”, “AI”, AND “radiation oncology”, “radiotherapy”, “radiation”, “chemoradiotherapy”. The included studies covered different steps in the radiotherapy workflow; that is, initial treatment decision-making, treatment planning and preparation, treatment delivery, and post-treatment follow-up.Key Content and Findings: A total of 105 studies covering the different stages of the radiotherapy workflow were included in the review. Most studies focused on initial treatment decision-making, primarily benefit-risk stratification through predictive modeling of treatment outcomes and treatment-related toxicities, followed by treatment planning and preparation, particularly automated segmentation and treatment planning. Conversely, few studies investigated AI applications in treatment plan approval and quality assurance, or treatment delivery. Notably, most of the included studies were retrospective, with substantial heterogeneity in study designs, methodologies, and reporting.Conclusions: AI demonstrates substantial potential to facilitate clinical decision-making while improving the efficiency and accuracy of radiotherapy workflows. Future research should prioritize multicenter prospective studies, standardized methodological and reporting frameworks, and explainable AI (XAI) to improve the reliability, transparency, and clinical translation of AI models.

Rethinking adult primary snoring: from diagnostic ambiguity to phenotype-informed, patient-centered care
